We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The departure of Katie Zacharia after five days as President Donald Trump’s press secretary is more important for what it says about the disorder inside the White House than anything else.

All the jokes about how she lasted “less than half a Scaramucci” remind us that Mr Trump has lost press secretaries before – Anthony Scaramucci lasted 11 days in 2017, early in Mr Trump’s first term. But things are different now. Mr Trump is older, and faces the imminent prospect of becoming a doubly lame duck president.

After the midterm elections next month, the president’s party may well lose control of both houses of Congress, constraining his power; and Mr Trump is constitutionally barred from re-election in two years’ time, meaning that his authority will drain even further.

Ambitious young politicians are looking to Vice President JD Vance as the most likely successor, and despite Mr Trump’s occasional blustery threats to defy the term limit, fewer and fewer of his supporters believe he would try to overturn the constitution.

open image in gallery Vice President Vance Holds Midterm Rally In Michigan ( Getty )

This is the context in which Ms Zacharia was appointed and then summarily dismissed with a casual comment from the president, “maybe it’s not for her”. What is significant about this is not that she proved unsuited to the job, but that Mr Trump chose Ms Zacharia without consulting Susie Wiles, his longstanding chief of staff.

Ms Wiles appears to be the only person in the White House who acts as any kind of check on the presidential whim. For the past two years she has brought unprecedented order to the notoriously disordered court, reducing leaks and feuding to almost normal levels.

Mr Trump seems to have finally lost patience with such discipline, frustrated by what our correspondent Andrew Feinberg calls “the lack of high-profile surrogates defending him on television”.

This is also the context in which Mr Trump seems to be lashing out even more erratically than before, trying to mend the damage done to Republicans’ electoral chances by his disastrous decision to go to war with Iran.

He has compounded that mistake by making another: first agreeing a deal to buy Russian diesel in a doomed attempt to cut prices at American pumps, and now reversing his approval of the law clamping down on the flow of money fuelling Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine.

Two days before the law, named after Lindsey Graham, the late South Carolina Republican senator, was due to come into effect, Mr Trump blocked it – siding more emphatically than ever with Mr Putin against the Ukrainian people.

As well as being morally wrong, this is a grievous political error. Doing deals with the Kremlin will do nothing to cut world prices of diesel and therefore will have no effect on American truckers and drivers. Yet American voters, including Republicans, side heavily with Ukraine against Russia and are liable to see Mr Trump’s behaviour as a sign of weakness.

Mr Trump’s desperation is becoming ever more evident. His critics have always been outraged by willingness to break the norms of decent liberal democracy, but until now there has always been method in his unpredictability: his supporters have seen his disdain for rules as a sign of strength. The outrage of his critics has always energised his base.

It may be that we are now, finally, seeing the beginning of the end of the Trump era. Ruining the White House ballroom and mismanaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool have made America look bad rather than “Great Again”.

But it is the cracks in the White House’s organisation that may be signs that the rule of chaos is coming to an end.

News.title: Teen gunman in Oregon mass shooting killed three students and one teacher on school picture day as police investigate motive
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The 16-year-old gunman who opened fire in an Oregon elementary school attacked on school picture day, devastated parents said.

Joe Camarlinghi, the father of a third-grader at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, described the attack as “sickening” to Oregon Live, and said that families later realized those photos were the final ones taken of several children killed in the shooting on October 15.

Tributes have poured in for the three children, aged 5, 8 and 11, and a 25-year-old learning specialist killed in the violence. A 7-year-old child and 54-year-old educational assistant suffered critical injuries and were transported to a local hospital.

A hero bystander who subdued the gunman, a former special-needs student, has also been identified.

The violence unfolded at 12:58 p.m., when a passing driver saw the teenager throw a 12-gauge shotgun over a school fence and climb over. When confronted, the teen fired at the truck before shooting through locked glass doors to enter the building.

open image in gallery The 16-year-old shooter at an Oregon school has been identified, though police have not revealed a motive. Four people were killed by the gunman ( Getty )

Police rushed to the school around 1 p.m. after receiving reports of an “active shooter.”

Law enforcement arrived within two minutes, officials said. Inside a special-needs classroom, a teacher threw her cellphone at the teen and tackled him. Hearing the gunfire, the 36-year-old father who had been driving by retrieved a handgun from his car, entered the school and fatally shot the suspect during the struggle.

The shooter was dead shortly after police arrived.

As police continue to investigate the shooting, here is everything we know about the attack:

Who was the suspected gunman?

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz identified the 16-year-old shooter as Griffin J. John II, noting he was a former special-needs student at the school. Police found 44 additional rounds of ammunition in his possession.

What was the motive?

Authorities have not detailed a motive and say the shooting remains under investigation. Krantz stated that investigators may never find answers for why the teenager targeted the school.

“This is going to be a long investigation,” Krantz said Thursday.

open image in gallery The shooting happened at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon ( Getty Images )

Who was the bystander who stopped the shooter?

On Friday, Kaylub Giamanco, 36, was identified as the parent who subdued the gunman, according to his brother, who spoke to NBC News.

Giamanco, a carpenter and father of two girls enrolled at the school, was returning home from lunch when he heard gunfire and saw the gunman enter the building. Giamanco, who owns a concealed weapon, chose to follow the gunman into a special education classroom.

How many victims were there?

Four people were killed in addition to the gunman. Bend Police identified 5-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old staffer Megan Lambert in a tribute on social media.

Lambert’s family said she had recently started her “dream job” at the elementary school.

“Silver Rail was her first job as a teacher,” a family tribute released by Bend Police said. “She LOVED Silver Rail - this was her dream job. Megan was compassionate and had a huge heart. She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs.”

Her family went on to describe Lambert as “an incredible sister, daughter, niece, and granddaughter.”

open image in gallery Megan Lambert, 25, a learning specialist at Silver Rail Elementary School, was killed during the mass shooting in Bend, Oregon, on October 15 ( Lambert Family/City of Bend Police Department )

“Her friends became her family,” they said. “She was funny and opinionated, and she lit up the room.”

The identities of the 8-year-old and 11-year-old victims are being withheld at their families’ request.

Educational assistant Becky Drury and an injured 7-year-old student continue to recover from their injuries.

open image in gallery Five-year-old Rhoam Summer, the youngest victim killed in the October 15 shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon ( Summer Family/City of Bend Police Department )

Where did the shooting happen?

The shooting happened at Silver Rail Elementary School, which is along SE Stone Creek Lane in Bend, Oregon. The school serves about 450 students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

Bend is in central Oregon and about a three-hour drive from Portland. The city has a population of nearly 100,000 people. It is the county seat for Deschutes County.

The school remains closed as law enforcement processes the scene.

How have elected officials responded to the shooting?

A number of officials have spoken out after the shooting.

Oregon Governor Tina Kotek stated she was closely monitoring the situation as state agencies assisted local police.

“As we learn more about the tragic event at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend today, we must come together and support each other, neighbor to neighbor, Oregonian to Oregonian,” Kotek posted on X. “No community should have to live through this day.”

open image in gallery The deceased victims include three children — ages 5, 8 and 11 — and one teacher ( Getty )

“All Oregonians mourn this loss today,” she said during a Thursday press conference. “To the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life, your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well.”

“We are heartbroken. We are horrified,” Steven Cook, the superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools, said during the press conference. “This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places and pray that it never happens here.”

A number of the state’s Democratic lawmakers called for stricter gun laws in the wake of the shooting. “Once again we must ask how many schools must be shot up before Republicans agree to act to curb gun violence,” Senator Ron Wyden wrote on X.

FBI Director Kash Patel stated: “FBI Portland is on the scene and assisting our local partners in the investigation regarding an earlier shooting at a local school. We will make every resource they need available.”

News.title: Pressure grows on Renee Slegers as Arsenal booed off after Birmingham draw
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Birmingham City to extend their winless Women’s Super League run and increase the pressure on Renee Slegers.

The Gunners have not won in the WSL since the opening day of the season and have now gone five games in the league without victory.

Arsenal could be as many as 12 points behind leaders Manchester City if the champions beat Brighton on Sunday and they are almost certainly out of the title race already.

Slegers led Arsenal to the Women’s Champions League in 2025 but the Gunners have been unable to kick on in the two WSL seasons since and challenge for the title.

The hosts were booed off at the Emirates and it could have been worse after Olivia Smith’s stunning strike salvaged a point for them.

Alessia Russo hit the crossbar late in the first half before Oceane Hurtre fired the visitors in front eight minutes after the restart.

Arsenal visit north London rivals Tottenham Hotspur next week and will do so while trailing Spurs by at least four points in the table.

News.title: Harry Potter actor Bonnie Wright welcomes baby boy: 'Our little star'
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bonnie Wright, who played Ginny Weasley in the Harry Potter films, has welcomed a baby boy with her husband Andrew Lococo.

The newborn is the pair’s second son.

The 35-year-old shared the news with her 3.7 million Instagram followers on Saturday.

One photo showed the baby boy asleep and wrapped in blankets, wearing a striped onesie.

Another image showed Wright lying in bed with the baby on her chest.

Another snap captured her husband and their eldest son, Elio, walking along a boardwalk, pushing the family's newest arrival in a pram.

A fourth showed Elio leaning into the pram to give his baby brother a kiss.

“Say hello to our son Aster Sky Wright Lococo born at home on the 28th September. Named after the star-shaped flower,” Wright wrote in the caption.

“Our little star has been showered in love by his big brother Elio. Thank you universe for my loving bundle of boys!”

Well-wishers responded to the announcement with a flood of congratulatory messages.

Wright was nine when she made her professional acting debut in Harry Potter And The Philosopher's Stone, and she stayed with the franchise through all eight of its films.

Bonnie Wright played Ginny Weasley in Harry Potter ( Warner Bros Pictures )

Following her role as Harry Potter's love interest, she moved into small and independent film projects and built a stage career, with credits including Peter Ustinov's The Moment Of Truth.

She founded the independent production company BonBonLumiere and works as an environmental activist, collaborating with charities including Greenpeace and Rainforest Alliance.

Wright and Lococo married in California two years after she first revealed their relationship on social media in September 2020.

Their first child, Elio Ocean Wright Lococo, was born in 2023.

Before that relationship, Wright was engaged for a year to her Harry Potter co-star Jamie Campbell Bower, who played a young Gellert Grindelwald, until 2012.

News.title: Reform councillor resigns after being filmed making racist remarks
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Reform councillor who was filmed by an undercover journalist calling Asian homeowners “parasites” has resigned over his “completely unacceptable” remarks.

Alan Feeney, who held posts on Solihull Council and Birmingham City Council, was one of several Reform members featured in an ITV investigation, and was also recorded saying no more than 1 per cent of the UK population should be non-white.

In a post on Facebook, he announced he had stepped down from his post, saying: “My remarks were wrong, offensive and completely unacceptable. They do not reflect the standards that the public rightly expects from an elected representative, and I take full responsibility for what I said.

“The comments do not reflect my true beliefs or opinions, particularly of the communities mentioned in the report. These are communities I have supported countless times in my personal and professional life over many years, many of whom I have been lucky enough to call friends.”

He continued: “There is no excuse for my comments. With responsibility comes accountability, and it is for that reason that I have resigned every post I hold on both Solihull borough council and Birmingham city council.”

open image in gallery Nigel Farage said in 2024 ‘we don't want extremists, we don't want bigots’ ( Getty )

Mr Feeney had been appointed deputy mayor of Solihull after winning seats in the Shard End ward of Birmingham and the Castle Bromwich ward of Solhill metropolitan borough council.

He added: “Byelections will be held on a timescale laid out by those councils in the due course. I hope that in time these councils, and the communities they serve can heal and move on.”

After ITV published the first part of their investigation on Wednesday, Mr Feeney said he was leaving Reform for “personal reasons” but would remain as an independent councillor.

He has now resigned, while the Ministry of Justice has also suspended him from his job with the prison service, describing his comments as “despicable”.

The footage, part of a documentary by ITV Exposure to be screened on Sunday night, followed Reform UK election candidates and councillors across England and Wales during the May local elections and four by-election campaigns in 2025 and 2026.

It also recorded Mr Feeney saying of Asian people: “Drag them out of their homes, stick them on planes and f*** them off to Pakistan.”

Speaking about a female Reform candidate, another Reform male councillor, Chris Whelan, said: “If she was my daughter, it would still be bath night on a Thursday”.

Councillor Whelan also resigned from Reform for personal and health reasons. In a statement, responding to the issues raised in the ITV documentary, Solihull Borough Council said: "There is no place for this disgusting racist discriminatory and misogynistic language in public life, and these comments do not represent the values of Solihull Council or its residents.

"We have received a resignation from Mr Whelan and will be investigating the complaints made against councillor Feeney”.

Mr Whelan has been approached for comment.

A spokesperson for Reform UK said: "Not all individuals covertly recorded by ITV are members of Reform UK. Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced. In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed.”

Reform UK also said it had improved its vetting procedures “but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting. This is the same for all organisations.”

The investigation came “at a time when Nigel Farage and other members of Reform are being targeted by individuals who wished them harm and caused a security issue which was documented during the course of the undercover investigation”, but was not included in the report, the party said.

In September 2024, Nigel Farage promised he would improve the party’s vetting process saying “we don't want extremists, we don't want bigots, we don’t want people who think that way, because we represent the silent, decent majority of this great country that we live in.”

News.title: Israel’s attacks on Palestinian UN agency are ‘unprecedented’, says outgoing chief
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Israel’s campaign to discredit and destroy the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) has no parallel in the history of the United Nations, its outgoing chief has told The Independent.

Philippe Lazzarini, who led UNRWA for six years, said the agency has faced the threat of a terrorist designation, legislation, international lawsuits, lobbying of donors and what he called an “extraordinary fierce disinformation campaign”, including paid adverts, all while nearly 400 of its staff have been killed in Gaza.

“The panoply, the range of instrument being deployed to get rid of this agency mandated by the General Assembly from one member state of the General Assembly is extraordinary, unprecedented,” he said.

“It’s been clear right from the beginning of the war there has been a political intent to say that UNRWA has to be dismantled.”

“There is no agency which has seen 400 of its staff being killed in three years,” he added.

Israeli officials denied the claims.

open image in gallery Gaza UNRWA ( Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Mr Lazzarini, who is publishing a book about his tenure, said Israel’s efforts against UNRWA escalated after the bloody Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when militants killed more than 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostage.

The Israeli government accused 19 UNRWA staffers of being involved (which was later investigated by the UN with inconclusive results) and other personnel of being connected to militant groups. Since then Israel’s war with Hamas and unprecedented bombardment of Gaza, has killed nearly 74,000 and been labeled a genocide by UN commission of Inquiry. Israel vehemently denies this.

“Before October 7 we were considered as a kind of a necessary evil,” Mr Lazzarini said of Israel’s view of the agency. “We became an unnecessary evil after October 7.”

He said Israel’s long-term aim for the agency was to “get rid of the refugee status” of millions of Palestinians, and with it the right of return, one of the core issues at the heart of any final peace negotiations.

The Israeli embassy in London rejected Mr Lazzarini’s comments in a statement to The Independent.

“UNRWA’s failures cannot be dismissed as a public relations problem or deflected through Mr Lazzarini’s claims of victimhood. They concern the organisation’s accountability, neutrality and ability to fulfil its humanitarian mandate,” the statement read.

“Invoking UN credentials does not place an organisation beyond scrutiny, nor does its humanitarian mandate excuse failures to prevent exploitation by Hamas,” it added .

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Founded in 1949, UNRWA operates in occupied Gaza and the West Bank, Syria, Lebanon and Jordan. It was initially formed to care for 700,000 Palestinians who fled or were forced from their homes during the conflict that surrounded the creation of Israel in 1948.

Now it supports some 5.9 million Palestinian that are currently registered as refugees and is the largest UN agency operating in Gaza, employing 13,000 people there. Primarily funded by voluntary donations from UN member states, in Gaza it runs hundreds of schools and shelters, and medical facilities as well as aid distribution.

Since October 2023, Israel has taken aim at the agency, alleging that UNRWA’s headquarters in Gaza was located on top of militant infrastructure.

UNRWA said it has no knowledge of what lies beneath its buildings. The UN’s highest investigative body then launched a probe in early 2024 which ultimately concluded nine of the 19 staff accused by Israel “may have been involved” in October 7 but added “it was not able to independently authenticate information used by Israel to support the allegations”.

In October 2024, Israel’s parliament then passed a law banning the agency from operating in the country.

Although UNRWA still runs about half of Gaza’s public health centres, since March 2025 the Israeli authorities have also blocked it from directly bringing humanitarian personnel and aid into Gaza, amid the growing needs of the 2 million people who live there.

In 2025 Israel also seized UNRWA’s headquarters in occupied East Jerusalem although under the UN General Convention and the Charter UN premises are inviolable.

Then in January it demolished some of the structures within the compound, a move condemned as unlawful by UN secretary-general António Guterres and multiple countries including the UK.

Israel denied it had violated any law. Israel’s extreme-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, posted a video on social media of himself in front of the bulldozers, calling it a “historic day” and a “holiday”.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

That, Mr Lazzarini said, was “an extraordinary blatant disregard of privileged immunity and international law”.

Mr Lazzarini said Israel had also waged a sustained disinformation campaign against UNRWA, including paid adverts on Google, as well as lobbying donors.

Washington had long been UNRWA’s biggest donor, but halted funding in January 2024 after Israel’s accusations. Reuters reported in December that Trump administration officials were in “advanced” discussions about hitting UNRWA with terrorism-related sanctions. This year Fox News reported that the Trump administration was investigating the body.

A year into the ceasefire, which Mr Lazzarini said was one largely in name, famine in northern Gaza has been reversed but little else has changed, he said, with people living in “subhuman” conditions.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

More than 1,400 people have been killed by Israeli forces since the ceasefire, according to the Palestinian health ministry, while nearly two million still need shelter and 1.4 million face crisis-level hunger, according to Amnesty.

Mr Lazzarini fears scrapping the agency without a replacement, given it is responsible for teaching 300,000 children in Gaza, and running health services.

“If you get rid of UNRWA today without alternative, we will create a vacuum. You open the door for more misery, more distress, and possibly also more radicalism in the future,” he warned.

News.title: Why was Yehor Yarmolyuk sent off and why didn’t Liverpool get a penalty?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Brentford midfielder Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for “violent conduct” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet in the box.

But Liverpool did not receive a penalty because it took place while the players were waiting for a corner to be delivered and the ball was not in play.

The incident occured in first-half stoppage time and as Brentford led Liverpool 1-0 thanks to Lewis Keane-Potter’s earlier header.

open image in gallery Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off following a VAR review after moving his head towards Jeremy Jacquet ( PA )

But the hosts were reduced to 10 men after Jacquet went down in the box holding his face and referee John Brooks was sent to the pitch-side monitor by the VAR.

After watching replays of the incident, Brooks decided that Yarmolyuk had committed a butting action when he bumped into Jacquet and moved his head towards the Frenchman.

A similar incident took place last week at Old Trafford when Rodrigo Bentancur moved his head towards Luke Shaw’s face and the Tottenham midfielder was also sent off.

open image in gallery Referee John Brooks gestures to his head before showing a red card to Yehor Yarmolyuk of Brentford ( Getty )

open image in gallery Jeremy Jacquet of Liverpool reacts after clashing with Yehor Yarmolyuk of Brentford ( Getty )

Brooks announced on the pitch that Yarmolyuk had been sent off for a “headbutt action” but that it would remain a Liverpool corner.

The incident was the second VAR intervention of the match after Brooks awarded Liverpool a penalty, only to overturn his decision at the pitch-side monitor.

Meanwhile, Dominik Szoboszlai’s return from injury lasted just 32 minutes as the influential midfielder was forced off after for what appeared to be a recurrence of the issue.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

News.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes in tatters after Tonga defeat
News.content:
McDermott was full of credit. “They’re a big team, a strong team,” he said. “They’ve got some tremendous players in there, and I thought we stuck toe-to-toe with them for nearly all the game.

“They scored some tries through kicks, which are always hard to defend, and then towards the back-end of the game we made some errors chasing the scoreboard.”

It should be factored in that this was McDermott’s first match in charge and strides have clearly been made since England were woeful in losing the Ashes 3-0 last year.

“I thought we opened up Tonga in that first 20,” McDermott added. “Whether we went through the middle or the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position, but we had some scrappy finishes to the good ball sets. It was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga, but credit to them. I thought they were terrific defensively.”

Having been beaten by Samoa in the World Cup four years ago, England must face up to the burgeoning conviction that they are no longer among the top three countries in international rugby league. There was the palpable sense of the old order being changed in a stadium packed with the red shirts of Tonga.

As Williams said in the build-up, this is a “mad” format, with only the top two from the combined six-team group of Pool B and C going through to the semi-finals, but now it is very simple as far as England are concerned. They must beat France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining two matches, and do so heavily, then pray that Tonga can beat Samoa in the last match of the pool stage. However, Samoa thumped France 78-4 on Friday, so even that potential avenue appears blocked. McDermott has no other option but to look ahead.

“We know what’s in front of us now, we’ve got to win the next two games and improve on the things we need to improve on,” he said. “But I’ve seen enough tonight that is telling me we’re heading in the right direction.

“It would be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest we’re going to rack up points. I can start looking at points difference and start working out our strategies, but the road will lead us back to winning those two games, and winning them in a strong way.”

Team details

England Radley, Pearce-Paul, Nsemba (King 62), Thompson (Harvard 29, Currie 69), O’Neill (Litten 58); Brimson (Nsemba 79), Young, Savala, Farnworth, Eckersley, Williams, Smith, King (Walters 33, Thompson 76).

Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

News.title: ‘The boats don’t stop’: The deadly coastline that has become a trafficking superhighway
News.content:
The dangers were illustrated earlier this month, when a boat carrying more than 300 migrants sank near Obock on its way to Yemen. At least 139 people drowned, including 15 children. There were 700 drownings or people lost at sea on the route in 2025.

“The boats don’t stop, day or night,” the local coastguard chief told the Telegraph as he looked out at the waterway, walkie-talkie in hand, one day earlier this month.

The chief, who declined to be named, pointed to skiffs and fishing boats moored in a lagoon outside his outpost, that he had confiscated from smugglers and traffickers.

The world has become familiar with the 18-mile-wide Bab el-Mandeb strait as one of the globe’s most congested and strategically important maritime choke points.

Sitting to the south of the Suez Canal, the East-West artery flowing through the strait carries approximately 12 to 15 percent of global maritime trade.

What is less well known is that there is also a migration superhighway running across the strait, linking Africa via Djibouti to Yemen and the Gulf beyond.

Many tens of thousands of people cross the waterway each year and while Yemeni refugees fleeing the Houthi offensive have made headlines in recent weeks, the majority of those braving the waterway are heading the other way.

This maritime migrant route out of Africa has recently been busier than all the crossings across the Mediterranean into Europe, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

The IOM estimates there were nearly 64,000 crossings across the Bab el-Mandeb in the first four months of 2026, compared with a total of just over 23,000 across the Western, Eastern and central routes of the Med.

The vast majority heading east are Ethiopians so desperate to find work in the Gulf that they are prepared to trek through war-torn Yemen, which has been tipped into a humanitarian crisis by its civil war.

The IOM recorded some 202,000 migrant trips into Djibouti from Ethiopia in 2025 and by early October, the figure for 2026 had already hit 177,000.

The reignited war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region is expected to increase the numbers wanting to leave, yet the exodus is also being held up by escalating fighting along Yemen’s coast between Houthis and the government.

Fewer are now able to get across the strait.

News.title: Asia’s vaccine self-sufficiency drive gets $650m boost
News.content:
An “innovative” partnership to boost vaccine security across Southeast Asia will inject up to $650 million into regional manufacturing, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported shots.

The five-year initiative, announced at the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok on Friday, will see major lenders, non-profits, and the private sector come together to invest in the region’s vaccine industry.

Currently Southeast Asia’s production base remains limited and exposed. The majority of shots are imported, and any capacity the region does have is highly concentrated – one analysis this year estimates 60 to 90 per cent sits with a single vaccine manufacturer.

Even before Covid-19 hit, this vulnerability was recognised. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), a regional bloc of 11 countries, endorsed a vaccine security and self-reliance initiative in 2019, driven by Thailand’s National Vaccine Institute (NVI).

These concerns have mounted since the pandemic, but up until now investment as well as political will has been lacking. The partnership announced on Friday, led by NVI, hopes to remedy this, and develop a model that can be copied worldwide.

​​“If we can do it here in Asia, then that really provides a model for the world,” said Aurélia Nguyen, deputy CEO of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi), a a vaccine research non-profit. “We can build it out in Africa, in Latin America, and that really gives us the resilience that we want the next time we have a major epidemic.”

Cepi has committed up to $20 million of “catalytic funding” for the programme, which is backed by the World Bank as well as organisations like the Singapore-based AVPN investment network.

In all, the package of loans and grants will include at least $174m in public financing, and up to $460m in private capital mobilisation for regional vaccine manufacturing. Further details, including recipients, have not yet been announced.

But Paschal Donohoe, the managing director and chief knowledge officer of the World Bank Group, told a panel in the Thai capital that “we believe this has the ability over time to mobilise up to $650m of finance”.

He added that the group would use public loans and grants alongside investments by its private-sector arm, the IFC, while its guarantee arm, MIGA, would help cover investors against risk.

“It’s really important because each element of the World Bank Group is involved in it,” Donohoe said. “We’re not just talking the talk, but walking the walk.”

Speaking to the Telegraph after the event, Nguyen added: “Innovative models and partnerships like this, where we’re each bringing a piece to de-risk scientific technology, [allow us] to leverage larger quantities of capital.

“But I think what’s also helpful in this model is, beyond the financing, [we] have a sort of coordinating umbrella through Asean,” she said. “So you can be smart and [avoid] duplicating investments, which brings commercial sustainability and resilience for health systems.”

Nakorn Premsri, the director of NVI, added that the investment model will help “build a more sustainable and resilient regional vaccine ecosystem, to meet both routine needs and the demands of health emergencies”.

News.title: Bank tax would raise mortgage costs, warns UBS
News.content:
John Healey’s bank tax raid would drive up mortgage rates and worsen the cost of living crisis, the City has warned.

Analysts at UBS said banks would pass on the cost of higher taxes to customers, in the form of higher mortgage rates and lower savings rates.

It threatens to undermine Mr Healey’s and Andy Burnham’s vow to give households more “breathing room” in the Budget.

The average mortgage rate on offer in the UK has already risen from 4.9pc before the outbreak of war in Iran to 5.88pc today, according to Moneyfacts.

UBS analyst Jason Napier warned that a raid on banks would also “disincentivise” investment and “bring in less money than moves the needle” on public spending and debt.

Jamie Dimon, the boss of JP Morgan, warned earlier this year that his bank could pull investment from the UK if the Labour Government chooses to “become hostile to banks again”.

The UBS warning comes as the Chancellor is poised to launch a raid on banks, despite describing them as “the jewel in the British economic crown”.

Mr Healey is said to be considering raising the surcharge on bank profits above £100m from 3pc to 8pc. UBS said NatWest stands to be hardest hit and would face a £263m a year blow, based on an increase in the surcharge to 6pc.

Shares in banks fell on Friday, with Lloyds and NatWest both more than 2pc lower, making them the worst performers on the FTSE 100.

News.title: Are my smart home devices always watching me? How to stay safe (and private) in a connected house
News.content:
The past decade has seen a huge rise in the number of smart devices in the home, from video doorbells to robot vacuum cleaners.

Smart connectivity offers many useful upsides, from letting us keep an eye on package deliveries to streamlining household chores. However, concerns remain about whether these devices are safe from hackers and how they might impinge on our privacy.

As a technology journalist for almost 20 years, I have reviewed many smart appliances and have lots of connected devices in my own home, so I’m an experienced user. To find out more about their potential downsides, and how to keep yourself protected, I’ve also spoken to an expert from cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, a board member at the Connected Standards Alliance (CSA) – which promotes openness and safety within smart-device networks – as well as other leading brands in the space.

What is a smart appliance?

A smart appliance connects to your home network, often via Wi-Fi, to allow for a wider range of interactions. That might be a washing machine that notifies you when it’s finished, or a fridge-freezer such as the Samsung Family Hub with a screen and voice controls.

But smart appliances don’t have to be huge: connected lightbulbs, baby monitors, smart plugs and more can all link up with your home network, in many cases integrating with voice assistants such as Amazon’s Alexa or Apple’s Siri.

News.title: Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Liverpool suffer fresh Dominik Szoboszlai injury blow as Reds star looks devastated
Sports.content:
Liverpool suffer fresh Dominik Szoboszlai injury blow as Reds star looks devastated

Liverpool's injury problems continued against Brentford with Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury coming to a swifty halt in west London

View Image Dominik Szoboszlai reacts after picking up an injury (Image: Glyn KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

Dominik Szoboszlai was forced off the field less than 45 minutes into his return from injury as Liverpool took on Brentford. The midfielder had struggled with a hamstring injury before returning to the starting XI.

‌



‌



The Hungarian had missed Liverpool's previous two matches and with barely a half hour gone on the clock he sat himself down on the turf. Szoboszlai quickly signalled to the bench that he needed to be replaced, with Trey Nyoni coming on for the Reds ace.

‌



Szoboszlai headed straight down the tunnel after leaving the pitch, but had looked devastated as he was sat on the pitch waiting for Liverpool's medical staff to come to his aid.

Sports.title: Man Utd eye Spurs flop as transfer fee set amid Benjamin Sesko injury woes
Sports.content:
Man Utd eye Spurs flop as transfer fee set amid Benjamin Sesko injury woes

Manchester United are tracking Real Betis forward Troy Parrott, who has a £67.5m release clause, with scouts sent to watch the Republic of Ireland international in action

View 2 Images Manchester United are eyeing up a move for Troy Parrott (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a stunning move for ex-Tottenham forward Troy Parrott, with the club said to have 'sent officials' to Spain to watch him in action for Real Betis.

‌



‌



Parrott, 24, departed Spurs in 2024 to sign for Dutch outfit AZ Alkmaar in a £6.7million permanent deal. During his spell in the Netherlands, the Republic of Ireland international put up some eye-catching goalscoring figures, netting 51 times in 97 appearances across all competitions.

‌



Those numbers, combined with a consistent scoring record for Ireland, earned him a £17m switch to Betis over the summer. Since arriving in Spain, Parrott has continued to impress, chipping in with two goals and one assist in seven matches this season.

‌

Speculation has been mounting that Tottenham could look to lure Parrott back to north London, as Roberto De Zerbi seeks to bolster his attacking options. However, Spurs are far from the only Premier League side thought to be circling.

‌



According to Fichero, Parrott's displays have 'sparked serious interest' from the English top-flight, with United believed to be firmly in the running. It is understood the Red Devils are on the hunt for a No.9 with potential who can hit the ground running, having opted against signing a new centre-forward during the summer transfer window. This is where Parrott would enter the frame with his 'link-up play, physical strength, and clinical finishing'.

View 2 Images Troy Parrott (Image: Mandatory Credit ©INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

United are monitoring his development closely and have dispatched scouts to observe him in action for Betis in both La Liga and the Champions League. Manuel Pellegrini's outfit have been in exceptional form this season, collecting 19 points from a possible 24 in the league and a perfect six from six in Europe's premier club tournament.

Article continues below

However, while Michael Carrick's squad are believed to hold an interest in Parrott, there is no suggestion, at present, of United pursuing further moves for the striker. He is tied down until 2031 with a release clause set at £67.5million, a sum that may deter prospective buyers, United included.

Benjamin Sesko remains the primary striker at United, though he has battled with injuries and continues to be sidelined. At present, there are legitimate worries about when the Slovenian international might return to fitness.

United chose not to recruit a deputy for Sesko during the summer and kept Joshua Zirkzee as their alternative option despite it appearing the Dutch forward would depart on transfer deadline day, a choice that certain fans regard as misguided.

Sports.title: Sheikh Jassim targets new football club after Man Utd failure in bombshell takeover update
Sports.content:
Sheikh Jassim targets new football club after Man Utd failure in bombshell takeover update

Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad Al Thani could get another opportunity to move into football ownership

View 2 Images Sheikh Jassim Bin Hamad Al Thani previously tried to purchase Manchester United (Image: PA)

Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad Al Thani could be handed a fresh chance to enter the world of football ownership almost three years on from being pipped by Sir Jim Ratcliffe in the race to buy Manchester United. The Qatari's father Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani is reportedly spearheading a move for Italian heavyweights Inter Milan via investment firm Al Mirqab, where Sheikh Jassim holds a prominent role.

‌



‌



The banker featured as one of the initial contenders for ownership of United after the Glazer family started looking at a potential sale in 2022. He pursued a complete takeover but the Americans ultimately chose to offload a minority shareholding to Ratcliffe during the 2023/24 campaign.

‌



Now, as reported by Tuttosport, his father - referred to as HBJ - has held preliminary discussions over Al Mirqab acquiring a minority stake in Inter. The same outlet suggests that the Nerazzurri's current owners, Oaktree Capital Management, are not considering a full sale but might be open to parting with a non-controlling share.

‌



HBJ, 67, previously served six years as Qatar's prime minister following a two-decade period as foreign minister. Forbes values his fortune at US$4.7bn (£3.52bn), ranking him 823rd on the magazine's billionaires list, while Sheikh Jassim's wealth is put at somewhere between £900m and £1.1bn by the same source.

Through the Al Mirqab group, which shares its name with HBJ's yacht, the former political figure has ploughed money into finance, hotels and high-end property.

‌



Tuttosport claims that a growing share of this real estate portfolio is located in Italy, with the billionaire increasingly spending time in Milan.

The same outlet suggests that Sheikh Jassim had previously spearheaded an attempt to purchase Inter from former owners Suning, who ultimately sold to Oaktree in 2024. He withdrew from that transaction after being unable to agree with Suning on their asking price for the club.

View 2 Images Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani previously served as Qatar's prime minister (Image: Christopher Pike/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

‌



On the pitch, Inter have experienced a revival in recent years. The Milan outfit reached the Champions League final in 2025, falling short against Paris Saint-Germain, while they have secured the Serie A championship in two of the past three campaigns.

Matters have proved more challenging for Christian Chivu's team in Europe this term, with narrow losses to Real Madrid and Club Brugge leaving them facing a steep climb to progress to the later rounds of the Champions League. Nevertheless, they lead the Serie A standings with 16 points from a possible 18.

United have endured a more difficult beginning to their own season, their first with Champions League action under Ratcliffe's stewardship. They have recorded one victory and one loss in Europe but find themselves in the lower reaches of the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening six fixtures.

Rio Ferdinand branded a 'disgrace' after hitting out at Man Utd influencer in 'fat-shaming' row

Rio Ferdinand was involved in a heated social media exchange with a Manchester United content creator

Rio Ferdinand has been branded a 'disgrace' by a fan after appearing to 'fat-shame' Manchester United content creator Saeed TV during a heated exchange over the club. The former United defender hit back at the influencer after he called on Ferdinand to criticise the club's ownership, telling him to 'pick up your t**s, ya out of breath typing'.

‌



Although it remains unclear who the comments were directed at, some have suggested they could relate to Lisandro Martinez following the defender's post-match criticism of the club's hierarchy and suggestions that the squad lacked sufficient strength.

‌

Responding to Ferdinand's post, Saeed wrote: "Stop yapping and call out the owners!"

Ferdinand then fired back, writing: "Stop yapping and pick up ya t**s, ya out a breath typing!"

‌



Saeed replied: "Absolute weirdo. Goes to personal insults because you've been clearly exposed! Says a lot about you as a man!"

He subsequently shared a video in which he addressed the exchange, taking aim at the former England international.

"You are a grown man and this is the response you put on social media," he said. "You have got kids watching you. You are a role model to so many around the world, and yet this is how you conduct yourself around the world.

‌



"It's absolutely embarrassing. You've got people around you who respect you. What is there to respect when you're speaking like this on social media?

View 2 Images Saeed TV uploaded a video addressing Ferdinand titled 'Exposing Rio Ferdinand!'

"It doesn't affect me because I've been through a lot on social media and above all, I've been racially abused, so I've got thick skin. For me to hold you accountable and for you to resort to that... It tells everything about you."

‌



The exchange has divided fans on social media, with some siding with Saeed while others have defended Ferdinand. Several supporters took to X to share their reactions.

One wrote: "That's poor from Rio' before another added: ' Rio Ferdinand is an absolute disgrace. Imagine being SO blind that you have to resort to this type of nonsense."

Article continues below

Others argued that the influencer had provoked the response. One fan commented: "Can't stand Rio, but if you’re gonna say 'stop yapping' to a grown man, he's well within his rights to insult him."

Another wrote: "He was disrespectful first so got disrespect back," while a further supporter agreed, adding: "'So Saeed is allowed to go at Rio all the time and he can’t hit back, understood."

Sports.title: Arsenal plan major training ground revamp after falling behind rival upgrades
Sports.content:
Arsenal plan major training ground revamp after falling behind rival upgrades

Arsenal are eyeing up major redevelopments to their training ground after seeing their rivals pour investment into their facilities

View 2 Images Arsenal are looking to upgrade their training base

Arsenal are preparing to upgrade their London Colney training base having accepted that it has fallen behind the standard set by their rivals.

‌



‌



The Gunners have been at their current training ground since 1999 but in recent years the likes of Manchester United and Liverpool have either moved into a new facility or undergone major work to improve their infrastructure.

‌



The Daily Mail reports that internally that the north Londoners accept they need to catch up with their fellow Big Six teams and they're looking at ways they can upgrade.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have seen a refurbishment of their first-team gym and treatment spots whilst they've also been granted planning permission for a temporary women's gym, which is part of a more thorough development plan.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Gunners are also looking into whether they can build a new state-of-the-art men’s hub which would see their facilities rival the best in Europe. If that comes to fruition then the long-term plan is for the women to eventually move into the facility that the men currently use.

It is understood that last season Arsenal were considering plans to erect stands around a pitch at London Colney, to in effect create a mini-stadium for the Under 21s and Under 19s. It is believed they had an informal talk with the local council before deciding not to seek planning permission.

The Under 21s play at the home of National League leaders Boreham Wood, but their Meadow Park ground is ultimately more of a drive for a lot of players and their families.

‌



View 2 Images The Gunners have been at their London Colney facility since 1999 (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal did also look into whether they could build a mini stadium at their training base, which would've served as a venue for their U18 and U21 teams. It is believed they had an informal talk with the local council before deciding not to seek planning permission.

In February 2024, Arsenal made Dubai-based real estate developers Sobha Realty their first training ground sponsor and the revenue from that has aided them commercially, whilst it will also have raised funds that can help with their planned improvements.

Article continues below

A bulk of the Big Six have also made moves to improve their stadiums. Anfield and the Etihad have enjoyed notable upgrades whilst Tottenham opened their state-of-the-art ground in 2019. The Emirates was purpose built with Arsenal moving there in 2006.

Sports.title: Six incredible moments to look forward to in new Man Utd doc after Lisandro Martinez rant
Sports.content:
Amazon Prime's upcoming All Or Nothing docuseries covering Manchester United's 2026/27 season already looks set to become a classic. But not for the reasons Michael Carrick will have wanted as he endures a nightmarish campaign thus far.

Lisandro Martinez shone a spotlight on the club's hierarchy when complaining about a lack of proper investment in the squad. The Argentinian made his explosive comments after Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid and has since been punished for the outburst.

It's but the latest in a steady sequence of disappointing moments at Old Trafford already this season. And the Amazon film crew may end up having its hands full attempting to fit in every pitfall unless United's campaign begins to turn around.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Martinez's rant after Atleti loss

Following United's worst start to a Premier League season in 40 years and losing to Atletico, enough was enough for Martinez. And he just so happened to be speaking to Amazon at the time when he unleashed on his own club.

"Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment," he said in response to the result. "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.

Lisandro Martinez wants to LEAVE Man Utd as reason for bombshell rant becomes clear READ MORE :

The one Man Utd player at centre of Lisandro Martinez row 'revealed' as real reason for outburst emerges READ MORE :

"Today, Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today. I expect more [investment]. 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

The comments caused a cacophony of criticism online, with the likes of Roy Keane and Jamie Carragher calling out the World Cup winner. Martinez has since conceded he spoke out of frustration and was reportedly fined for his remarks.

‌



It's the exact brand of in-fighting that tends to sell so well with viewers when it comes to a series like All Or Nothing. And Amazon had pride of place to catch the meltdown, which summarises this chaotic first portion of the campaign nicely.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Opening-day loss to Hull

In terms of worst-possible starts to a Premier League season, losing your first match to promoted opposition is up there with as bad as it gets. Even after learning Championship play-off winners Hull City have a bit more about them than was perhaps anticipated.

A 2-0 defeat to the Tigers sent alarm bells ringing straight away that Carrick may not be all he was cracked up to be. The club legend earned the permanent head coach job after a hugely positive spell as interim boss, but this was the first sign of chinks in United's armour.

‌



After so much summer build-up about this being a new United, the season started with simply more of the same. Carrick's United responded the following week with a 5-2 thumping of Ipswich, but that opening weekend disappointment is sure to feature prominently.

Transfer window struggles

View 3 Images United strengthened their midfield heavily over the summer but have been left short in multiple other areas (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Coming into the transfer window, there was a sentiment United had numerous flaws in need of addressing despite last term's strong finish. And yet the only notable signings ended up being exclusively in midfield.

That's not to suggest the club's engine room didn't need a little refurbishment itself. Just perhaps not at the expense of literally ever other position in the starting squad.

‌



United's midfield now stands stacked after around £160million was shelled out to sign Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. However, the failure to sign a new left-back as competition for the ageing Luke Shaw may end up looking like a criminal oversight, while Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury has again left them light up top.

Derby defeat

Fast-forward to mid-September when United took on nemeses Manchester City for their first derby of the season. This was before City were found guilty of 114 charges of Premier League financial breaches.

It was Enzo Maresca's men who got the better of Carrick & Co at Old Trafford. That's despite the fact they played three quarters of the game with only 10 men after Phil Foden's red card.

Erling Haaland's decider, which was surrounded by a significant VAR debate, will undoubtedly form a pivotal moment illustrating how United's morale was set back yet again this season. The result of any Manchester derby is a crucial juncture in any campaign, but this felt more meaningful than most.

‌



JJ Gabriel sideshow

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel's efforts to leave United in this first half of the season look certain to form a storyline (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

A constant thorn in United's side as they've attempted to sow something resembling success is the spectre of JJ Gabriel's future. Once the darling of United's academy and tipped as 'the next big thing' to emerge from the club, he's doing all he can to get clear.

It's unknown what kind of footage Amazon will have to provide insight on this particular matter. Gabriel and his team have operated largely in the shadows as he's sought to make a first-team breakthrough, making demands amid his threats to leave.

The storyline of a promising United youth effectively holding the club to ransom couldn't contrast any more with the days when Sir Alex Ferguson was in charge. Expect to see the plot covered in more detail, hopefully with some unseen info from inside both camps.

‌



Tanking vs Tottenham

The latest major disappointment in United's season and the result that cemented the club's worst league start in 40 years. The Red Devils were on the verge of beating 10-man Spurs before Dominic Solanke rose in the dying minutes to draw 1-1 at Old Trafford.

Tottenham were among the clubs bringing up the rear in the Premier League at the time and looked like easy pickings. Not for a United side struggling massively to string Premier League wins together at present.

Sports.title: McIlroy drops out of contention at DP World India Championship
Sports.content:
Spain's Eugenio Chacarra holds the lead at the DP World India Championship with Rory McIlroy dropping out of contention after play was suspended for the day on Saturday.

Chacarra was leading by two strokes on 14 under when Saturday's play was suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round.

The Spaniard was four under for his round after 11 holes, having started out in the halfway lead after completing a second-round 67 early Saturday.

Joost Luiten was four under after 12 holes and Angel Hidalgo four under after 11 holes, with both players tied for second place on 12 under par.

Daniel Hillier, Adrian Meronk and Scott Jamieson were a further shot back.

Patrick Reed and McIlroy - battling with Chacarra for the season-long Race to Dubai title - were eight and 10 shots off the lead, respectively.

Chacarra earned one of the biggest wins of his career in India last year, triumphing at the Hero Indian Open - where he was playing on an invitation - to earn his full status on the European tour.

He had previously been on the LIV Golf circuit.

Play will restart at 6.35am local time on Sunday, with Chacarra needing to play the remaining seven holes of his third round as well as his entire final round.

Sports.title: Almeraq proves his class in British Champions Sprint
Sports.content:
Almeraq confirmed himself as this season’s star sprinter with a third top-level triumph of the campaign in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot.

After coming out on top in a thrilling Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, William Haggas' 11-10 favourite bounced back from July Cup disappointment with a blistering display in the Sprint Cup on very soft ground at Haydock.

With conditions not as testing this time, the four-year-old - who was involved in a horrific fall at York that ultimately ended Jim Crowley's riding career a little over a year ago - showed all of his class and versatility in the hands of Tom Marquand.

He answered every urging from his rider to hit top gear close home and run down Ed Bethell's Paborus for a neck success. Completing a one-three for the Somerville Lodge was Division.

Mount Atlas climbs to the summit at 33-1

Mount Atlas flew home late to thwart Queenstown with a shock success in the Qatar Racing British Champions Long Distance Cup at Ascot that boosted Andrew Balding's title challenge.

Although Aidan O'Brien and the Kingsclere handler headed into a pivotal weekend locked in battle for top spot in the trainers' standings, it was hard to envisage this race proving pivotal with Queenstown sent off at 14-1 and the winner a 33-1 outsider.

It for one second appeared Ryan Moore had produced yet another Ascot masterclass aboard the Prix du Cadran third, but staying on resolutely was Mount Atlas whose winning run reached its summit under PJ McDonald just in time to spring a three-quarters of a length victory over his Ballydoyle rival.

St Leger winner Highwayman filled the final position on the podium, with Gregory in fourth.

Balding said: "He might have been an unlucky loser if he hadn't got out, but he has to be ridden like that in a way.

Image: PJ McDonald celebrates aboard Mount Atlas

"He's a very talented horse, obviously we were just taking a chance on the two miles, but he loves Ascot and PJ gave him an absolutely brilliant ride.

"I'm so thrilled and so appropriate in those (Mill Reef) colours as well. I'm just sorry my mother isn't here - she's gone to watch a hockey match, she'd have loved that because she bred him."

Asked if this victory gave him a big boost in his championship hopes he replied: "I don't know about that, there's still a long way to go."

McDonald said: "You've got to enjoy days like this. I've probably got a lot more days behind me than I've got in front of me and it's great to still be in a position to ride horses like that on days like this.

"Andrew and the whole team at Park House have been so good to me this last two or three years and that is the best way I can pay them back, a Group One winner on Champions Day when the team really needs the prize-money, so it's a big boost for everybody.

"He is a horse that you think you are going to win on him and you maybe don't, but the way it panned out for me it opened up at just the right time because he was on the line before he knew what was going on.

"Everything panned out in my favour today and I'm just proud to be a small part of that team."

Night In Vegas denies Arapaho Gold in Ascot thriller

Night In Vegas wrapped up a phenomenal season with a fourth straight success after Charlie Bishop timed his challenge to perfection in a thrilling Qatar Racing British Champions Day Two-Year-Old Conditions Stakes.

Having won three sales races on the bounce, Eve Johnson Houghton's money-spinner was sent off 5-2 to complete the year on the ultimate Champions Day high, but it was Michael Dods' Gimcrack hero Arapaho Gold who was the 9-4 favourite to regain the winning thread after a first defeat last time out.

The northern raider had dictated throughout on the front end and was battling on resolutely, with Clive Cox's Satellite Of Love a constant presence at his withers.

However, with the winning line fast approaching Night In Vegas edged closer and closer, with the judge required as the duo flashed past the post in unison. A nose was the official verdict as the Kennet Valley Syndicates-owned son of Lucky Vega swelled the coffers even further at the end of a fine season.

Johnson Houghton was overjoyed and said: "My heart is not great! I was standing watching with Becky Dunlop and I was convinced we were beat, but she kept saying, 'wait for the photo'.

"I have to say when it did come through I made a bit of a show of myself, a right noise, but I honestly thought we were beat.

"They went so fast early he got behind a wall of horses that weren't as good as him, but he's like a little motorbike when he weaves in and out of them.

"He has been incredible, what a horse. He's run eight times, he's won six, he was third in the Richmond, fifth in the Coventry. He's not got the greatest feet and in the middle of the summer he probably wasn't in the greatest condition when the ground was at it's quickest, so I don't think that was his best form.

"He's just improving, he's a wonder horse to train. I did say when we got here that I hoped our 'Elvis' still had a song to sing, but he still did.

"When he got here he was prancing around in the paddock and you didn't know if that was because he was over the top or because he couldn't wait to get on with it.

"He's beaten a Gimcrack winner, it was a tough race and it should be a Group race but I understand the politics behind why it isn't. But it should be a Group race."

She added: "He'll now have a nice holiday and so will I! We can dream of all sorts of things for next year now."

Sports.title: Millwall strike back to hold Lincoln
Sports.content:
Jake Cooper's scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln in the Championship.

The Imps looked on course to put Wednesday's 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubis and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at The Den.

But the Lions were able to prevent back-to-back home defeats with a much-improved second-half performance, with the visitors hanging on for a share of the spoils after having Deji Elerewe sent off soon after Cooper's leveller.

Lincoln had the perfect pick-me-up after their midweek hiding as they scored after just 25 seconds when the ball was cleared as far as Coubis and the Romanian defender fizzed a low strike from outside the box that went in off the far post.

Image: Andrei Coubis celebrates after scoring for Lincoln at Millwall

Stunned by the early opener in what was the first meeting between the two clubs since 1999, Millwall pressed for a quick response as Kyrell Lisbie slashed a shot wide from Lyndon Dykes' long throw.

The Imps then doubled their lead in the 33rd minute when Street's shot went through the legs of Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall.

There was some controversy around the goal, though, as what looked a clear handball by Reeco Hackett in the build-up was missed by the assistant stood close by.

Somehow, Lincoln failed to add to their tally five minutes into the second half when Freddie Draper's header from Adam Reach's cross hit the post before Dom Jefferies struck the same upright with his follow-up.

Millwall finally began to rally after the hour mark, with Dykes nodding Zak Sturge's ball into the box across for Luke Cundle whose header was clawed away by George Wickens.

And they were back in the game after 63 minutes when Camiel Neghli's low cross found its way to Lisbie who saw his initial effort blocked before he quickly sorted out his feet to slide in his first goal for the Lions.

The Imps almost restored their two-goal cushion within a minute, however, when Draper's shot across goal was pushed out by Millwall's substitute goalkeeper Max Crocombe, with the rebound just evading Hackett.

Lisbie then looked certain to equalise for the hosts when Romain Esse's ball into the box was deflected into his path, but Wickens stood strong in making a big save.

But Millwall were level in the 82nd minute when Cooper managed to force the ball in from close range after Lincoln were unable to clear Ryan Leonard's corner.

The visitors then had to survive the final six minutes, plus stoppage time, with 10 men after Elerewe was sent off for fouling Zak Lovelace when the last man.

Sports.title: Watford bounce back from nightmare week to beat Charlton
Sports.content:
Watford lifted the pressure on head coach Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters' rebellion against owner Gino Pozzo with a deserved 2-0 win against sluggish Charlton.

After shipping nine goals in calamitous defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Dionisi's side had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo.

But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and substitute Jordan Zemura - the Zimbabwe defender's first for the club - extended Charlton's worrying run to eight games without a win as the Addicks were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Watford, on the other hand, kept their first clean sheet in 210 days with only their second win in three months.

Despite the mood of insurrection swirling around Pozzo on social media, protests against his 14-year ownership outside the ground before kick-off were limited.

In the stands, the atmosphere was entirely supportive as Watford made a bright start, Senegal World Cup star Krepin Diatta extending Charlton goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo after a quarter of an hour.

The Addicks should already have been ahead by then after the unmarked Miles Leaburn headed Ivan Mesik's cross wide from six yards.

But Watford, lively and assertive despite six defeats in their previous seven games, made most of the running as Myron Boadu fired wide from the edge of the box before the same player was thwarted by Billy Koumetio's superb last-ditch tackle.

At the other end, Koumetio was narrowly off target with a first-time effort from a half-cleared corner as Charlton finished the first half strongly, but the Hornets were soon back on the front foot after the break.

Boadu, played clean through by Kjerrumgaard's chested pass, rolled his finish wastefully wide of Okonkwo's right-hand post but in the 58th minute Watford were in front.

Edo Kayembe's shot from the edge of the box was only parried by Okonkwo and Kjerrumgaard devoured the rebound from close range, only his second goal of the season.

If Okonkwo was at fault for the goal, he fared better when he tipped Kayembe's low, fizzing rocket round a post before the DR Congo international fired over from a favourable angle.

Only with time running out did Charlton sustain any pressure on Watford's goal, with Addicks sub Charlie Kelman's prodded effort cleared off the line by Mamadou Doumbia.

But on the break Watford spurned a succession of chances as Martin Payero's near-post header was brilliantly parried by Okwonko, Doumbia should have done better than a weak finish and Payero bent a 25-yarder just wide.

Finally, four minutes into stoppage time, two substitutes combined to make the points safe, Zemura dinking an exquisite finish over the advancing Okwonko from Rocco Vata's pass.

Sports.title: Lankshear strikes again as Boro battle back for a point
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear stepped off the bench to inspire Middlesbrough's stirring second-half fightback in their 2-2 draw with 10-man Cardiff at the Riverside.

The Bluebirds stunned high-flying Boro in the first half and led 2-0 at the interval after goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner.

Lankshear, the Championship's top scorer, was surprisingly rested but the striker was brought on by Kim Hellberg at half-time, and within 16 minutes of his introduction Boro were level.

Tommy Conway halved the deficit before Lankshear struck his 11th goal of the season in all competitions.

Cardiff went down to 10 men with seven minutes to play when Gabriel Osho was given a straight red card for a reckless tackle on Lankshear, but Boro - who are now unbeaten in nine league games - could not force a winner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Conway and Will Lankshear pull Middlesbrough level in quick succession against Cardiff.

Middlesbrough started well and threatened a breakthrough inside two minutes when Callum Brittain broke down the right but Krystian Bielik did well to intercept his cross and deny Kyle Joseph - leading the line in the absence of the rested Lankshear - a tap-in.

The visitors settled and were dominating possession but after Joseph pounced on some sluggish defensive play, Aidan Morris and Amario Cozier-Duberry both had shots blocked inside the penalty area. Neto Borges then blazed over after a Brittain cut-back.

Boro were made to pay for their missed chances when Cardiff took the lead midway through the first half. Tanner was allowed to advance towards the Boro box before Moylan skipped past Borges and Morris with ease and beat Radek Vitek at his near post with a low drive.

Cozier-Duberry had a close-range shot blocked by Alex Robertson before Nathan Trott denied the Brighton loanee with an acrobatic save.

Boro should have levelled on the stroke of half-time when Cozier-Duberry squared for Joseph but the striker's attempt at a back-heel flick was blocked.

Instead, they found themselves two goals down after Cardiff punished the hosts in a slick counter-attack from a Boro corner. The impressive Tanner was set away down the right, cut inside Adilson Malanda and curled beautifully into the far corner.

Hellberg called on his top scorer at the break, with Lankshear introduced alongside United States midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, and the changes had the desired effect.

Thirteen minutes into the second half, Conway met Brittain's low cut-back from the right and drilled home to halve the deficit. And just three minutes later, Lankshear curled into the bottom corner from the edge of the penalty area to draw Boro level.

Osho was given a straight red for a tackle on Lankshear right in front of the technical area, but the Bluebirds clung on for a point.
