Sports.title: Chelsea climb into the top four and end NINE-MONTH wait for a clean sheet - as Mike Penders proves he is ready to seize his chance after Emiliano Martinez's brual injury at Everton
Sports.content:
Chelsea climb into the top four and end NINE-MONTH wait for a clean sheet - as Mike Penders proves he is ready to seize his chance after Emiliano Martinez's brual injury at Everton

At first, a few Everton fans suspected Emiliano Martinez was time-wasting. Then the seriousness of the situation sank in. Chelsea's goalkeeper was faking nothing.

He had collided with Jarrad Branthwaite, who is a hulk of a man, when bravely coming to clear a set-piece after 67 minutes.

It floored him as his Chelsea team-mates immediately signalled for help.

What followed were almost ten minutes of no football; only concern for Martinez as Joao Pedro had a royal pop at the paramedics for hardly rushing with the stretcher.

This was not how Mike Penders – Chelsea's 21-year-old goalkeeper whose potential is high – wanted to make his Premier League debut. He had hoped to earn his opportunity eventually.

But here, Penders was thrown in at the deep end as Martinez was taken away.

Pedro Neto broke the deadlock inside the first minute of the second half

Morgan Rogers got in to another off-the-ball bust up this time with the Everton's James Tarkowski, both recieved a yellow card for their antics

Rogers was lucky not to receive a second yellow moments later after colliding strongly with James Garner

Nevertheless, using two goalkeepers, Chelsea secured their first clean sheet since January. They had conceded in each of their last 22 league games. They had waited nine months for this.

Martinez refused to allow Everton to score, and then Penders took over from there, even seeing through the 11 minutes of stoppage time added on to the end.

Nevertheless, using two goalkeepers, Chelsea secured their first clean sheet since January. They had conceded in each of their last 22 league games. They had waited nine months for this.

Martinez refused to allow Everton to score, and then Penders took over from there, even seeing through the 11 minutes of stoppage time added on to the end.

Stopping Everton from scoring will have pleased Xabi Alonso as much as the way Chelsea continued their kick-off glitch. Chelsea got the second half going, and yet again, they scored within a minute.

It was Pedro Neto with the goal, Jorrel Hato with the assist, and Morgan Rogers with the inventive back heel in the build-up. With that, Chelsea led 1-0, just 43 seconds after kicking off.

Hato was not even supposed to be starting. Pep Chavarria was earmarked to be Chelsea's left wing back.

It was Pedro Neto with the goal, Jorrel Hato with the assist, and Morgan Rogers with the inventive back heel in the build-up. With that, Chelsea led 1-0, just 43 seconds after kicking off

Emi Martinez suffered a nasty blow to the head half way through the second half that forced the Argentinian to leave the pitch on a stretcher

Neto put the game to bed with an calm finish in stoppage time

But he picked up a problem despite travelling to the Hill Dickinson Stadium and so had to drop out of the squad. Hato replaced him, and was crucial in this opener being scored.

Neto later added Chelsea's second goal just as the 11 minutes of stoppage time were announced. That was timed well, and it came from a 25-yard free-kick.

Chelsea's supporters had been chanting 'Hendo again, ole, ole'. They wanted a repeat of his goal from last weekend against Bournemouth. Jordan Henderson tried but struck the wall. The ball fell kindly for Neto, however.

Everton tried sending balls into the box, but Penders was clean enough in collecting them.

Per sources, Penders was confident of succeeding Robert Sanchez when the 28-year-old Spaniard went into this season as Chelsea's No1.

Even Liam Rosenior preferred Filip Jorgensen to Sanchez for a while during his doomed tenure in charge of the club, so Penders believed he was capable of taking over as first choice at some stage in 2026-27.

Yet Daily Mail Sport has heard how Penders' confidence waned when Martinez was then signed from Aston Villa on a two-year contract with the option of a further year.

The 34-year-old Argentinian replaced Sanchez, who was sent to Como after a poor performance in Chelsea's season-opening win at Fulham. That is a dry loan with no option or obligation included, and Sanchez is currently second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas.

Martinez's arrival surprised Penders, who had spent the summer hearing Alonso say he was happy with his goalkeeping set-up and would not be signing a new No1.

According to a source close to the goalkeeping situation at Chelsea, Penders felt the sudden signing of Martinez pushed him further away from a starting place and changed the complexion of his coming campaign.

Yet Martinez's injury here gave him his first chance in the Premier League, and more opportunities may follow, depending on how long his competition will be sidelined.

Sports.title: Chelsea star Emiliano Martinez rushed to hospital after sickening head injury during Everton clash - as Argentina goalkeeper is BOOED while stretchered off
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Emiliano Martinez rushed to hospital after sickening head injury during Everton clash - as Argentina goalkeeper is BOOED while stretchered off

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez has been rushed to hospital after suffering a sickening head injury during their trip to Everton.

And the Argentinian was booed as he was stretchered off the pitch at the Hill Dickinson Stadium with the visitors 1-0 up after Pedro Neto's goal.

He had received medical treatment after smashing heads with Toffees defender Jarrad Branthwaite and their clash caused a roughly 10-minute delay.

'As far as I know, he left the stadium conscious,' Xabi Alonso told TNT Sports after the match. 'He's in the hospital doing precautionary tests. This is what I know so far.

Martinez had come to punch the ball out from a free-kick when Branthwaite went up for a header and the pair collided.

They both hit the floor immediately after impact, causing great concern in the stadium.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Matinez was rushed to hospital with a head injury after a collision

He had come together with Jarrad Branthwaite in a sickening clash and needed medical attention before beign stretchered off

Branthwaite also required treatment and a concussion test but was able to carry on

Paramedics rushed on and also attended to Branthwaite, who cut his nose and lip, but he was able to carry on.

TNT Sports' broadcast did not show any replay of the incident and cameras cut away from 34-year-old Martinez, who joined Chelsea in the summer.

Martinez was only lifted onto the stretcher after six minutes, with Mike Penders coming on as his replacement in the 73rd minute when he had been removed.

He seemed to be conscious as he was being stretchered off as his arms were moving.

Medics had been giving him oxygen as he lay on his back on the turf.

His injury is a blow for Chelsea, who signed him from Aston Villa for £7.5million late in the window to seemingly fix their goalkeeper issue.

Former number one Robert Sanchez conceded three on the opening weekend against Fulham and is now on loan at Como.

But Chelsea's porous defence has often left the 2022 World Cup winner exposed and he is yet to keep a clean sheet across a full 90 minutes.

The incident caused a roughly 10-minute delay and Martinez was booed as he was taken off

Penders, a 21-year-old Belgian goalkeeper with experience at Genk and Strasbourg, came on for his Premier League debut in his stead.

Neto bagged his second goal of the day in the 90th minute to set Chelsea on course for victory.

Their win sent Xabi Alonso's side fourth in the table, and Everton down to sixth, though their match was the first of the weekend so their placements stand to change.

Chelsea have improved in the last couple of weeks.

They went into the international break on the back of a dismal 3-0 defeat at Brentford, but have since thrashed Bournemouth 5-1 and now taken three points at Everton, who came into the clash unbeaten.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho admits Vinicius Jr should have LEFT Real Madrid last summer 'to a country where he is respected' as boss lavishes praise on former Arsenal target
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho admits Vinicius Jr should have LEFT Real Madrid last summer 'to a country where he is respected' as boss lavishes praise on former Arsenal target

Jose Mourinho thinks Vinicius Junior should have left Real Madrid in the summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

Vinicius Jr has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

His future has come under more scrutiny in recent times as he has had a slow start to the season - one goal and three assists in ten outings - and is now serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

Mourinho said: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

Jose Mourinho says he would've left Real Madrid in the summer if he were Vinicius Junior

'I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected,' said Mourinho, of the star who has suffered persistent racial abuse in Spain

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 386 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Mourinho has been a strong defender of Vinicius and recently insisted to TNT Sports that he is going to get back on track.

'He is going to emerge,' the Portuguese promised. 'It is just a question of when.'

Sports.title: Former Man United star Ander Herrera reveals he is now 'playing for free' after choosing to donate weekly wage to his boyhood club - having cashed in on £53m at Old Trafford and PSG
Sports.content:
Former Man United star Ander Herrera reveals he is now 'playing for free' after choosing to donate weekly wage to his boyhood club - having cashed in on £53m at Old Trafford and PSG

Ex-Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera has revealed he is playing for free at his boyhood club Real Zaragoza.

The 37-year-old who has two caps for the Spanish national team was, until very recently, living out the final years of his storied career in Argentina with Boca Juniors but has now decided to ply his trade in the Spanish third division with Real Zaragoza, in hopes of bringing the historic club back to the big time.

Herrera is reportedly earning £5,500 per week, a far cry from the £150,000 he earned while playing for European giants Paris Saint-Germain. But in an interview with Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand on the former centre-half's YouTube channel, Rio Ferdinand Presents, the Spaniard revealed that every penny of his wage will be going to the club's foundation.

The six-time Copa del Rey and one-time Europa League cup winner said: 'Now in a difficult moment for the club, I think we all, we the fans, we have the responsibility to help the team and the club. And I feel so proud of my career.

'I feel so proud about what I have achieved in terms of football and also in terms of money. So I don't need it. I wanted to play for free. I wanted to help for free.

'At home, my city, where I grew up, and hopefully, as I told you before, helping the club to come back to professional football.'

The Spaniard revealed the motivation behind his decision to return to Real Zaragoza in an interview on Rio Ferdinand Presents source: RioFerdinandPresents/YouTube

Herrera spent five years with Manchester United winning four major trophies but is now hoping to bring his boyhood club back to the professional game

Real Zaragoza, slipped into the third division of Spanish football, officially a semi-professional division, at the end of last season in one of the most shocking declines a big European club has experienced in recent years.

Herrera also stressed the importance of his decision: 'I think we also have to give something back to football, you know, and I wanted to do this because I am not only a professional football player, I am also a football fan and I love what I do.

'And one day, probably soon, when I am retired, I want to feel proud of what I have done during my career.'

Ferdinand took Herrera's candor as an opportunity to pile more criticism onto Manchester United's rivals, Manchester City, saying: 'In a world where Man City have these charges hanging over their head, it's so good to hear about a gesture like this still in the game of football.'

The pair continued to joke about the potential re-attributing of Premier League winners medals following the bombshell Manchester City verdict.

Ferdinand began by saying: 'I'm waiting for my medal as well, so you can have one and I can have another one as well.' Herrera gave a classy response saying: 'I don't know if we deserve the trophy, but for sure they don't deserve to win it.

'If the Premier League want to keep being respected all around the world they have to do something.'

Herrera could potentially be entitled to a Premier League winners medal as he was a key part of Jose Mourinho's 2017-18 Manchester United side that finished second to City, although they were 19 points off the pace.

The one-time Europa League and FA Cup winner with Manchester United did express some sympathy for the Manchester City players during his interview, saying: 'I don't know if you will agree with me but if I was a Man City player I would be angry with my owners, I would be angry with my board, because they have put all that I have done during these years in doubt.'

Sports.title: Chris Woakes reveals how killjoy Ashes hero Ashley Giles stopped England stars celebrating World Cup triumph - and takes aim at ECB for 'bottling' open top bus parade
Sports.content:
Chris Woakes has accused the ECB of ‘bottling’ the chance to project England’s historic World Cup win with an open top bus parade.

In an extract from his autobiography The Wizard, published by The Guardian, the ex England all-rounder lamented the lack of a celebration commensurate with the magnitude of winning a first 50-over title in 2019.

Arguing that it was on a par with the iconic Ashes triumph of 14 years earlier, he wrote: ‘The 2005 team had been given an open-top bus parade through London and I couldn’t help wonder why delivering the first men’s World Cup in England’s history didn’t merit something similar.

‘The country had been transfixed by that final, with a record 15 million viewers tuning in over the course of the match, after Sky had shared the coverage with Channel 4.

‘Fair play to Sky: they’d paid top dollar for those rights and were perfectly entitled to keep the coverage to themselves, but they recognised the greater good and did the sport a huge service. So why did the ECB bottle it?

‘Football clubs get the open-top bus out for League Cup wins and supporters line the streets to see their heroes. We could have done the same, reaching out to thousands more people than we did. It still makes my blood boil to this day.’

The 37-year-old Woakes, who also featured in England’s Twenty20 World Cup-winning side of 2022, recalled the buzz of being able to celebrate the super over victory over New Zealand post match, with friends and family including wife Amie joining him on the Lord’s outfield.

Chris Woakes has hit out at killjoy chiefs who denied England's World Cup heroes of a party

England conquered the world in 2019 but a strict curfew meant they could not enjoy a proper celebration

Celebrations continued with champagne and other drinks in the dressing room, but a block on taking those celebrations into central London’s early hours rankled some of the senior players, according to Woakes.

‘From there, it was back to the Landmark hotel, where a bit of aggro followed. It was around 10pm but our midnight curfew was still in place, making it a bit pointless to go back out in town unless the restriction was lifted,’ he added.

‘Sadly, Ashley Giles, who’d been our director of cricket since the previous year, was having none of it.

‘It felt like the ECB was too worried about what could go wrong. Some of the lads properly kicked off here, not least since Gilo himself had been part of the 2005 celebrations that had become folklore.

‘So, we settled in back at the hotel bar feeling a bit aggrieved; forced to settle for the same surroundings as the night before when a fresh location was the order of the day.

‘A bit like the lack of a parade, it seemed needlessly cautious. We had won a World Cup, for heaven’s sake – if you can’t milk it then, when can you?’

Sports.title: Poppy protest footballer James McClean claims former club 'hung me out to dry' over political stance - and opens up on death threat that left him needing police protection
Sports.content:
Poppy protest footballer James McClean claims former club 'hung me out to dry' over political stance - and opens up on death threat that left him needing police protection

Poppy protest footballer James McClean says his former club Sunderland 'hung him out to dry' over his stance.

And he has opened up on the death threat which saw his house guarded by police after he first went against the grain in 2012.

McClean, 37, is remembered in English football for his refusal to wear the poppy because he feels it shows disrespect to people who died during the Troubles in his home nation of Northern Ireland. He also played in the Premier League for five seasons with the Black Cats and West Brom.

His hometown, Londonderry, known to Republicans as Derry, was the scene for the infamous 1972 Bloody Sunday massacre, in which British soldiers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a protest march, with 14 killed.

'Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen,' he told The Guardian.

'It was a very difficult year and I felt a lot of that could have been handled better by the club. But Sunderland came out with a statement before the game which drew all eyes on me. It was there to protect the club. They basically said this is James’s personal decision but we, as a club, wholeheartedly support the poppy appeal.

James McClean says Sunderland 'hung him out to dry' over his poppy protest stance

The star, who was born in Northern Ireland, has always refused to wear the poppy as he feels it shows disrespect to people who died during the Troubles

'I wanted to make my own statement but I was constantly told by the club that: "No, no, it’ll die over. Just leave it."

'I’d just turned 23 and I thought the club had a duty of care to look after me and that’s what they were doing. I’d won the player of the year the previous season but I felt they hung me out to dry.

'The next game was away to Fulham on a Sunday, on Sky. A threat was made that I would be shot if I came on to the pitch. I remember Erin [his wife] panicking. It sounds extreme and people might say: "Oh, wise up, you’re not going to be shot on TV." But the night before the game I was assigned two police officers to stand outside my door. So the Met police took it seriously and that made it more real.'

McClean has followed his stance ever since, despite the intimidations. In 2024, he even stood separately from the Wrexham and Mansfield players as they observed a minute of silence for Remembrance Day.

He has previously stated that if the poppy was only used to memorialise those who died solely in WW1 and WW2 then he would be happy to oblige with the show of respect.

His decision has previously seen McClean suffer torrents of abuse from angry supporters that view his poppy snub as an insult to the memory of armed forces personnel who have lost their lives in combat.

The Republic of Ireland international is a divisive figure in professional football having previously issued calls for a united Ireland, refused to wear a poppy as is tradition in fixtures throughout November and once posed IRA-style in a balaclava in front of his children for a 'school history lesson'.

In September, he clashed with Birmingham City supporters when being substituted and later called a fan at the match a 'smelly fat gammon' after catching a cup of Bovril that had been thrown at him.

He says he would sometimes go 'looking for conflict' during his career - and even suffered from death threats

He is back at hometown club Derry City but is not playing and says they fed him 'b*******'

He admits to the Guardian that sometimes he riles people up deliberately.

'There were days where I went looking for the conflict,' he says.

McClean has been back in the headlines recently after moving to his hometown club Derry City.

Derry attempted to bin off McClean in August – despite signing him in January on a multi-year deal – reportedly claiming he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

He has branded it 'incomprehensible' and a 'dangerous precedent' for the club to try and terminate his deal due to his physical issues.

And he told the Guardian: 'I was meant to be coming home for the fairytale ending. But you quickly realise the promises are just b*******.

'It’s not good. It’s a player against owner and there’s only one winner. I think that’s it in terms of Derry City. You never think you’ll be betrayed by your own so it’s painful.'

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
Sports.content:
Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has claimed Manchester City must be deduced "multiple double figures of points" after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Maguire said: "The redacted report sets out year by year how much the sham contracts contributed to the artificial commercial revenue. Over the rolling three-year period, in some years we could be talking about a £350million difference. That would shatter all records for PSR compliance.

"Everton and Nottingham Forest's deductions covered a single breach in a single year, an overspend of no more than £20million. So is there a ceiling on what can be deducted? And the sanctions hearing could already have taken place. Because City are appealing and everyone has NDAs, we might not know the sanction until the appeal result. But it has to be multiple double figures of points, before you start the calculations.

"I worked out that if you add up nine years of Champions League non-participation for individual clubs at an average of £50million a time, around £20million for the Europa League, plus potential claims from players who missed bonuses, the Premier League's legal fees and a fine, we're talking in excess of a billion pounds regardless of the points deduction.

When asked about the possibility of City being kicked out of the Premier League, Maguire responded: "I think it would be a very unusual vote. We did see Bury get expelled from League Two some time ago but I think that the other clubs would have to bear in mind that Manchester City would probably take legal redress and that could prove to be very expensive if they are expelled without the verdict being held and without the appeal. So it's a risky path to tread, but the strength of feeling does vary from club to club.

"Certainly some of the other elite clubs are very unhappy with the delay in the situation because they feel it has an impact upon their ability to qualify for the Champions League. I think some of the more mid-tier clubs who don't see Manchester City as a threat, their main concern is, is this going to further increase the already sky-high legal costs that have been incurred by the Premier League and they don't want any part of it.

"So, they want a quick resolution and then they can get on with the rest of their season and focus on their own clubs."

Sports.content:
Michael Carrick makes Man Utd transfer admission with January plans set

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has hinted at potential January transfer window activity

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has teased January movement. (Image: Alex Livesey, Getty Images)

Pablo Barrios and Ademola Lookman handed Carrick's side a third defeat in five matches, heaping further pressure on the Premier League-winning former midfielder.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change

Emma Raducanu has been backed to win Wimbledon during her career despite failing to even make the last eight in SW19 as of yet

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu is looking to compete for another Grand Slam (Image: Getty)

Former British No 1 Dan Evans has claimed he "genuinely thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day" - but maintained she needs to be on the court more often.

‌



‌



The 23-year-old has been on our screens for half a decade having shot to stardom when she was just a teenager. Her stunning victory at the US Open in 2021 saw her profile skyrocket as she broke numerous records en route to claiming the top prize in New York.

‌



That did bring with it huge expectation and Raducanu has not scaled those heights since. She's not even reached a Grand Slam quarter-final outside of her US Open success but Evans still sees her as talented enough to claim one of the sport's biggest honours.

‌



He told the Telegraph : “She’s good, and I think – I’m saying this in as nice a way as possible – I think she thinks she’s good. Not in an arrogant way, but when she plays big matches, she’s like ‘Whatever. This is just another match.’ And yeah, I just think one day she’ll get it.

Andy Murray's return to tennis court confirmed as Rafael Nadal calls out Scot READ MORE :

“The crowd can play such a big part in tennis and you have to keep yourself together on Centre Court, because it’s a daunting place to go and play. But she looks like she loves it out there.”

‌



Raducanu's best result at Wimbledon has been the fourth round, which she reached twice. Last year she showed that she could mix it with the elite, bringing the best out of Aryna Sabalenka when they squared off on Centre Court.

Injuries have plagued her career, whilst she's also struggled to settle on a coach, which in itself has seen her cop criticism. Evans insists that Raducanu would need to spend more time honing her talent if she wants to realise her potential.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu won the US Open in 2021 (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

“There’s no doubt she needs to have a racket in her hand a bit more," he said. "I’m sure she’s getting pushed side-to-side by endorsements, and there’s a bit of tug of war on what she needs to do, what she doesn’t. I admit I’ve not watched her practices very often, but from what I’m told she’s a good trainer: she works for two, three hours in a row with hardly any break.”

Tim Henman is another former British No 1 who believes Raducanu has it in her to win another Grand Slam. "When you've done it once, you know it's possible to do it again. But ultimately, it all comes down to the process and the daily work," he said.

But last year Mark Petchey, who did serve as her interim coach for a period, said it "won't be easy" for Raducanu to win another major title - but believes it is possible if she changed her baseline game against the "big hitters".

Sports.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison
Sports.content:
Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison

La Liga president Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid's media output to 'Nazi propaganda' in an extraordinary claim and Los Blancos have furiously hit back

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex)

Real Madrid have demanded the resignation of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he extraordinarily compared the club's media strategy to 'Nazi propaganda'.

‌



‌



Tebas accused selected journalists of promoting the views of senior Real officials, stating they were acting as the club's 'official mouthpiece' portraying Los Blancos as victims of refereeing decisions.

‌



"Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing," Tebas wrote on social media.

‌



"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

‌



"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.

"The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase. Real Madrid TV is a central piece of that machinery. Where is the full match analysis for each round of games?

"Where are the possible errors that harm other clubs or those that favor Real Madrid? If they applied the same magnifying glass to every match, the result might ruin their script. But the script demands that Real Madrid always appear as the victim."

‌



Real responded in a lengthy statement on their website, branding the comparison 'morally repugnant'.

"The repeated conduct of Javier Tebas shows a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," they wrote.

"Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone who occupies two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football should resort to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

‌



View 2 Images Real have hit back furiously (Image: Getty Images)

"His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and regeneration constitute, in the opinion of our club, a real scourge for Spanish football.

"Consequently, Real Madrid CF demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation."

‌



Tebas insists he is unconcerned by Real's latest demand, accusing the club and 'their lapdogs' of trying to destroy La Liga.

He wrote: "I've lost count of the times that, in thirteen years, Real Madrid's leaders have demanded my resignation or tried to disqualify me: complaints to the CSD, directly or through third parties, criminal lawsuits… Today's is just another one.

"What still hasn't arrived are the responses. They confuse neutrality with independence. My position demands independence, not passivity in the face of injustice or silence in the face of the continuous, disproportionate, and insulting attacks from Real Madrid TV and its lapdogs on our competition.

Article continues below

"The La Liga president must defend it. Including against Real Madrid's leaders. My conclusion: they seek to DESTROY the national competition.

"What they haven't achieved so far with the Superliga, they're trying with a distorted narrative from their media and their lapdogs. They call it regeneration while attacking the prestige of the competition they participate in."

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois accused of throwing illegal shots in Fabio Wardley fight
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois accused of throwing illegal shots in Fabio Wardley fight

Dubois climbed off the canvas twice in the opening three rounds of the Brits’ brutal first clash in May and will look for a repeat against Wardley tonight

View 2 Images Daniel Dubois beat Fabio Wardley in May (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Daniel Dubois has been accused of resorting to dirty tricks ahead of his rematch with Fabio Wardley.

‌



‌



Dubois climbed off the canvas twice in the opening three rounds of the Brits’ brutal first clash in May. He went on to dominate, leaving Wardley battled and bruised when the slugfest was finally stopped in the 11th round. Dubois was crowned heavyweight world champion for the second time and will defend his crown in tonight's sequel.

‌



But Wardley's manager, Michael Ofo, has claimed the Londoner was guilty of throwing illegal shots five months ago. "I believe Fabio is in a better place than he was and he's ready to go to war," he said. "The first fight was an amazing fight but there was also a lot going on in that fight that has not been talked about enough. The MMA rugby tackling; there was a lot leading with the head and a lot of rabbit punches. We are going to be applying a lot of pressure to make sure those things are not going to be happening."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

View 2 Images Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley face off (Image: Nick Potts/the Press Association)

‌



Wardley reigned for only 173 days before being relieved of his WBO belt. He immediately insisted on a rematch and will walk to the ring 161 days after his first career defeat. Doubts have been raised over his decision to return so soon, but Wardley said: "I gave myself four weeks away from it all. A whole lot is made of needing time off to recover but I know how I felt after the fight.

"I was wondering why I wasn't back in the gym and that we needed to hurry it along. There was a lot of cosmetic damage but it's heavyweight boxing. We're big men and we're going to end up with a few bumps and bruises. This feels like my more natural place, being the underdog who took the second fight too soon. That’s been the story my whole career, so I’m comfortable being back here. "A loss is never part of the plan but the thought is worse than the reality.

"I was never going to get through unscathed, undefeated like Floyd Mayweather, because I want to be in there with the best guys. And that jeopardy leaves lots of room for things to go wrong. I know where I went wrong, it didn't take long to realise where I messed up. We’ve made changes and adjustments for this fight and we’ll implement them on Saturday night.

Article continues below

Fabio Wardley inspired by Ipswich heroics ahead of Daniel Dubois rematch READ MORE :

Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley undercard, running order and fight times READ MORE :

I was over-zealous and confident in my power in the first fight. I probably believed too much that the right hand would land, but that’s easy to adjust. I have to be controlled and not just march forward and throw right hands. But if someone wants a war with me then I’m happy to oblige. Often I’m the instigator and once I smell blood, I’m getting him out of there."

Dubois will start as the favourite to deliver a repeat performance on home soil in London. And he added: “I’m ready to go to war. Of course I respect him, but I’m just ready to go out to battle. I’m feeling stronger than in the first fight. I’m grounded and ready to do my job. First I need to get through Saturday and then it’s on to bigger and better things.”

Sports.title: 'I was set to sign for Man Utd – but I had to say no for two reasons'
Sports.content:
'I was set to sign for Man Utd – but I had to say no for two reasons'

Manchester United have a huge pulling power but they don't always land every target

View 2 Images (Image: Leonardo Fernandez, Getty Images)

Clarence Seedorf has revealed how close he came to joining Manchester United. But the Real Madrid and AC Milan legend had two big reasons for turning the club down.

‌



‌



The former midfielder had a big decision to make when he left the Bernabeu at the turn of the millennium. Sir Alex Ferguson was trying to convince him to move to Old Trafford.

‌



However, the tantalising prospect of playing alongside Ronaldo (R9) and Christian Vieri was too good to turn down. So was the Italian weather.

‌



Speaking to Kobbie Mainoo on Amazon Prime Video Sport's YouTube channel, the 50-year-old admitted he "wanted to come here for a long time" and was "supposed to even play here."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

When the young United star enquired why the transfer to Old Trafford never materialised, Seedorf elaborated: "I went to Inter Milan instead. Marcello Lippi, I don't know if you remember the coach, world champion with Italy.

‌



"He called me. He said, 'Uh, Clarence, you want to come and play behind Ronaldo R9 and Christian Vieri?' I said, 'Okay, let me just take my bags. I'm coming.' Italy was a bit more familiar. Probably was the reason why I chose to go there as well."

At that point, Seedorf had established himself as a creative force in Real's engine room, netting 20 goals and providing 35 assists across 159 outings.

View 2 Images Clarence Seedorf admitted a chat with Marcello Lippi changed his mind (Image: FC Internazionale/Inter via Getty Images)

‌



He secured the La Liga crown, two domestic cups and the Champions League.

He departed for Inter Milan following three campaigns in Spain, joining the Serie A outfit for approximately £20million (€24m).

While he failed to lift any silverware there, he did achieve glory in Italy - albeit with Inter's bitter rivals. Seedorf made 432 appearances for AC Milan, netting 62 goals, providing 67 assists and claiming nine trophies.

Article continues below

Among his haul were two Champions Leagues, two UEFA Super Cups, two Serie A titles and three domestic cups.

Following a decade of glory at AC Milan, Seedorf headed to Botafogo in Brazil to bring his playing days to a close. He hung up his boots in 2014 after clinching the league title with his final club.

Sports.title: 13 boxing icons predict Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley result as clear victor emerges
Sports.content:
13 boxing icons predict Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley result as clear victor emerges

Boxing greats have cast their predictions for Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley 2 and a resounding consensus has emerged ahead of Saturday's rematch

View 4 Images Some of boxing's elite figures have made their predictions for Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley's rematch (Image: Getty Images)

The British boxing aristocracy has made its predictions for Saturday's rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. 'Dynamite' blitzed his way to a late stoppage victory when these fighters first met in May to clinch the WBO heavyweight belt.

‌



‌



That result brought an end to Wardley's undefeated record in the first blemish of his boxing career. Dubois will hope to draw a line under their rivalry and cement back-to-back victories for the first time in more than two years.

‌



The rivals will face off once more at London's O2 Arena as the British boxing public watches on with anticipation. And Mirror Fighting has compiled a list of what every major figure has said about the outcome, with a very clear favourite emerging.

‌



Eddie Hearn - Dubois win

Hearn has had a change of opinion since the first bout. He recalled: “I backed Fabio to win that [first] fight, right? It was the first time I ever backed him to win in the last five fights that he has been in – and he lost, but he was incredible."

Changing his tune this time around, he added: “I think that he is a massive underdog in the second fight.”

Fabio Wardley explains mindset ahead of Daniel Dubois rematch READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Carl Froch - Dubois win

"When I look at Fabio Wardley, he took a lot of damage in that [first] fight, and Daniel Dubois actually finished strong, stood proud and was full of energy," he said on his Froch on Fighting YouTube channel. "In the rematch, I just think Daniel Dubois’ got an extra 10 per cent over Wardley and I think that’ll be enough.

"So Fabio Wardley, unfortunately, I don’t think will get this job done and he’ll probably get stopped again. Daniel Dubois’ going to be coming into this fight really confident."

‌

Learn more £24.99 or £0 DAZN Order the fight here Product Description Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO world title in a rematch with Fabio Wardley on Saturday, October 17, at London's O2 Arena . Fans can order the fight on DAZN PPV for £24.99 or watch it at no extra cost with DAZN Ultimate.

Derek Chisora - Dubois KO

"I think that this is Wardley’s last fight," said 'War' on talkSPORT. "I don’t think that he wants to box anymore. This is his cash out.

"After three rounds, Daniel’s going to win it by knockout."

‌



David Haye - Wardley win

"[Wardley] is a very tough man, he's a warrior," said former unified cruiserweight champion and WBA heavyweight titleholder David Haye on Seconds Out. "We've seen that time and time again, win or lose, he's laying it all out on the line.

"So I think he'll be ready and if it's to be, if he's able to hold it together, then he's got a chance. But Dubois looked solid last time out. Got dropped a couple of times and was able to weather the storm. So you're gonna get fireworks. Fabio's obviously gonna come with something more this time around. He understands what it's about.

"Throwing that massive overhand right that's nowhere near the target constantly. He'll have watched videos of that and thought, 'What was I doing? I need to set up my big back hand.' And we're gonna get good action. I think it'll be a lot closer [this time]. I don't think Fabio will be making the same basic, novice mistakes he was making first time around.

‌



View 4 Images Former heavyweight world champion David Haye has backed Wardley to learn from the first fight (Image: Eric Espada/Getty Images)

"I don't think [Dubois] is gonna change that much, because he won the [first] fight. And when you win fights, you think, 'I've got it figured out.' So I think he's gonna be pretty much the same. He'll be a similar fighter that turned up.

"He got decked early but Fabio didn't know what he was doing, how to get someone out of there. I think Fabio, if the knockout he received, the punishment he received, if he's able to recover from that, he'll have a better shot in this return fight."

‌



Spencer Oliver - Dubois win

"My prediction for the fight is that Daniel Dubois wins the rematch much more comfortably than he did in the first fight," said former European super bantamweight champion Spencer Oliver on talkSPORT.

"He has grown as a fighter both physically and mentally, and he is going from strength to strength. It's going to be a tough night for Fabio Wardley."

Agit Kabayel - Dubois win

WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel told Playbook Boxing: "I think maybe Daniel win but this is heavyweight boxing.

‌



"Definitely [Wardley has a chance] but I watched the reaction from Usyk for the fight with Fabio and Daniel and what Usyk said is correct, Fabio lost this fight on his jab. He forgot his jab, he came only with the right hand.

"When Fabio makes this better in the second fight, he can beat him. I don’t know if this is boxing politics but for the UK fans, this is the biggest fight in the heavyweight division.

"The winner of the fight, maybe he can fight with [Filip] Hrgovic or he fights with me for the belts. This is the way for everyone, but we will see."

‌



Tony Bellew - On the fence

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"I need to see what Fabio's got left," said ex-WBC cruiserweight champion Tony Bellew while speaking to DAZN. "That's a hard one...I'm not gonna lie, if Fabio comes back fully, he's a dangerous man, because he's so brave.

"And when Daniel is having success, he's a monster. It's a really, really hard fight. I wouldn't write either off of it. It's a killer. It's a brilliant, brilliant fight."

‌



Johnny Nelson - Dubois win

Former WBO cruiserweight king Johnny Nelson said on talkBOXING: "It's about levels and [their last fight] shows quite clearly that Daniel's is way above Fabio's. I think Fabio is going to box so much better but Daniel is going to step it up even more."

Darren Barker - Dubois win

"Fabio Wardley's an absolute machine, one of the toughest men out there. You'd want him on the front line," former IBF middleweight champion Darren Barker told DAZN. "You'd want him to be stood next to you in battle. The man’s an absolute soldier and has the ability to knock anyone out.

"Think back to the punches that dropped Daniel Dubois in the first fight. They were glancing blows. They weren't full — he didn't have full purchase on the shots. A couple of them glanced the top of the head. If he hits the target correctly, he's got every chance of getting the win.

‌



"But I just feel Dubois has found a new confidence. He's exorcised those demons from when the word ‘quit’ was being thrown around. Filip Hrgovic hit him with about 20 right hands a couple of years ago. He stayed there, kept digging in and found a way to win.

"He got dropped twice by Wardley but managed to get the victory. It was a very good fight, but it was kind of one-sided in big portions.

"I know Wardley loaded up, found big shots and made it exciting, but the boxing from Dubois was really good. As long as he's not complacent and doesn't get overconfident, I feel he'll have a bit too much for Wardley."

‌



George Groves - Dubois win

View 4 Images George Groves has tipped Dubois to finish off the rivalry if he's at his best (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking on Sky Sports' Toe2Toe podcast, former WBA super-middleweight titleholder George Groves said: "I've seen [Wardley] say, 'I caught him. I hurt him. It's my fault I blew it. It was mine to lose...'

"I don't think that's the case, to be honest. It was almost Dubois' to lose. Dubois is the better boxer, you know. [He has] better movement, faster hands. I mean they both can crack but you think Dubois has got crazy power.

‌



"I think they've both got great chins. You can't fault Wardley's chin...when you see him get caught on the button, the punches bounce off him.

"One thing I thought about is the mentality of Dubois, because sometimes he's on it and usually, sometimes, after a big win, he's not there. And I just think he's beat Wardley now. Does he think, 'Eh, I'm better than Wardley,' and he's not quite switched on... If he has [that mentality], he may come unstuck.

"Because let's get it straight, Wardley with no amateur pedigree, very limited boxer, but very effective with the way he is. Big, strong, powerful, game and maybe a slight awkwardness to his style. Dubois figured that out last time. If he shows up, he walks it."

‌



Steve Bunce - On the fence

"Wardley is taking an enormous gamble," commentator Steve Bunce wrote in his BBC Sport column. "His nose was badly damaged in the first fight, and the cut across its bridge is an old wound that has reopened before.

"He has also been through plenty of hard rounds throughout his career, sometimes unnecessarily against opponents he was expected to beat comfortably. That concerns me. But I've spoken to Wardley a couple of times in the build-up, and he makes a compelling argument for an immediate rematch...

"Dubois seems more sheltered than normal this week, which in his case translates into more focused. He knows how close he came to losing the first fight, having made mistakes and been dropped twice. This time he seems confident without being overconfident.

‌



"If he stops Wardley again in another spectacular fight, I would argue he becomes the most marketable heavyweight in the division."

Fabio Wardley - Wardley KO

View 4 Images Wardley is aiming to avenge his 11th-round stoppage defeat to Dubois (Image: Getty Images)

"I've not made a career out of going to points," said the challenger. "I've made a career out of finishing fights before the bell. I had it done almost in the first round of our fight, almost in the third round.

Article continues below

"We'll pick apart those moments, pick apart you stylistically, what worked and what didn't work, and within the first quarter of the fight, you'll be gone."

Daniel Dubois - Dubois win

Speaking ahead of Saturday's rematch, Dubois said: "A win by any means necessary. I respect you. You're a good gladiator, a good dance partner, but I'm going to win."

Final score: Dubois 9-2 Wardley

Sports.title: Mike and Zara Tindall's impressive net worth after six-word royal family financial claim
Sports.content:
Mike and Zara Tindall's impressive net worth after six-word royal family financial claim

The combined wealth of Mike and Zara Tindall makes for interesting reading

View 3 Images The Tindalls have a sizeable net worth (Image: Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

Mike and Zara Tindall possess a staggering net worth despite maintaining that the royal family doesn't offer them financial support. The couple, who celebrated their 15th wedding anniversary earlier this year, are said to boast a combined fortune of £30million thanks to their respective sporting careers and entrepreneurial ventures.

‌



‌



The King's niece is an accomplished equestrian who won a silver medal in eventing at the London 2012 Olympics and was once named BBC Sports Personality of the Year.

‌



On top of her athletic accolades, Zara has enjoyed long-term endorsements with high-end brands, including a reported £1m deal with clothing company Musto. She's also been a brand ambassador for Land Rover and Rolex for 20 years, with both deals coming in the same year she won the individual eventing world title at Aachen.

‌



Mike, who turned 48 years old on Sunday, wrote himself into rugby folklore as part of the England squad that won the 2003 World Cup. The triumph was one of several high points in his 17-year professional career.
