Sports.title: Moses Itauma Claims Critics Were Happy He Lost
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma sounds bitter about the criticism following his defeat to Filip Hrgovic, claiming some people were happy to see him lose. His disappointment is clear, but his response leaves unanswered whether those critics identified weaknesses he needs to correct.

The young heavyweight repeatedly insists he doesn’t care about outside opinions. Yet his comments suggest the reaction has stayed with him, particularly when it came from people he previously supported.

“I’ve seen personalities change and I’ve seen a couple people be happy that I lost,” Itauma told The Stomping Ground. “I’m like, ‘Wow.’ I was like, ‘Man, I’ve cheered you on.’”

Itauma doesn’t name those people or explain what they said. That makes it difficult to judge whether they celebrated his defeat or offered criticism he didn’t want to hear. Those are different things, and his account provides little detail to support the harsher interpretation.

Being supportive of another fighter also doesn’t require that person to approve of your performance or your corner’s decisions. Someone can want Itauma to succeed while believing his preparation or tactics need work.

Asked about criticism of Ben Davison and his training team, Itauma emphasized their healthy relationship. That explains his loyalty, but a good relationship doesn’t answer questions about what happened during the fight.

To his credit, Itauma acknowledged his responsibility.

“Ultimately I lost the fight and I take full responsibility for that.”

He also credited Hrgovic’s experience and admitted the defeat was difficult to accept. There is recognition that he encountered something his previous fights and sparring hadn’t prepared him for.

The concern is how quickly the conversation about his team becomes a discussion about other people’s personalities. If criticism gets interpreted as pleasure at his failure, potentially valuable observations become easier to dismiss.

Itauma doesn’t have to agree with every pundit. But his return will depend on correcting what went wrong against Hrgovic. Whether the people pointing it out cheered for him beforehand has little bearing on whether their points were right.

Itauma seems to be taking the criticism personally. Rather than discussing what the critics got right or wrong, he’s talking about people being happy he lost. That gives him a reason to brush aside points that might help him.

He may feel let down by people he’s cheered for, but that doesn’t make their criticism wrong. They can support him and still think his conditioning, defense, or preparation wasn’t good enough.

Calling them haters won’t fix any of that. If he dismisses good advice because he doesn’t like hearing it, the next good heavyweight he faces could punish the same flaws.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Sees Hadribeaj’s Left Hand Threatening Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora could be vulnerable to a left hand he doesn’t see coming against Ermal Hadribeaj, according to Tim Bradley, who gives the challenger a chance of springing an upset on Saturday night despite picking the champion to win.

Bradley sees danger in the southpaw pairing. Fundora’s height and punch output can make him difficult to beat round after round, but Hadribeaj’s awkward delivery could create an opening for a punch that changes the fight.

“Does he have a lot of knockouts? No. But sometimes it’s not about having a lot of power. It’s about catching a guy when he don’t see a punch coming,” Bradley said on his channel.

That is the route Bradley identifies for Hadribeaj. Trying to match Fundora’s volume would require the challenger to spend long stretches within punching range. A well-timed left hand could punish Fundora while he is attacking.

Bradley referenced Sergio Martinez’s knockout of Paul Williams when discussing the danger, using that southpaw pairing to illustrate how an unexpected shot can undo a tall fighter. The comparison describes a possible opening; it doesn’t establish that Hadribeaj has Martinez’s timing or finishing ability.

“I think he has a damn good chance of winning, man. I really do.”

Bradley also believes an unfamiliar challenger can arrive better prepared than the champion expects. He recalled studying Junior Witter for a year before taking his title, searching for weaknesses while Witter knew comparatively little about him.

Hadribeaj could have spent similar time studying Fundora. Finding an opening on video, though, is only the beginning. He still has to exploit it while dealing with the champion’s reach and constant punching.

Bradley gives Fundora credit for living in the gym and improving rather than assuming he will underestimate his opponent. His final pick is Fundora on experience.

The upset case rests on Hadribeaj making one opening count. His modest knockout record makes that harder to sell, but Bradley believes the left hand gives him a chance.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Turns Toward Liam Paro Unification
Sports.content:
Devin Haney could keep his November 28 date in Atlanta and pursue a second welterweight title against Liam Paro after negotiations with Shakur Stevenson broke down.

An official monitoring the talks told BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire that Haney will move toward a unification against IBF champion Paro at State Farm Arena. The fight has not been announced, but it would give the WBO champion a route back into the ring after months spent negotiating with Shakur.

Haney has a hold on the venue for November 28, with Brian Norman Jr. and Tiger Johnson penciled in for separate support bouts, according to the report.

Keeping that date would be significant. Haney has not fought since beating Norman on November 22 last year. Another round of prolonged negotiations would threaten to stretch his absence beyond twelve months.

The split with Shakur comes with conflicting explanations. Shakur accused Haney of changing the proposed weight from 145 to 147 pounds. Haney rejected that account, writing on X:

“I agreed to 145.”

Haney also accused Shakur of attempting to introduce a rehydration clause and complained about the time spent negotiating:

“I wasted six months negotiating with you.”

An unnamed official quoted by Pugmire offered a different version, alleging that Shakur accepted 145 pounds without a rehydration clause before Haney’s side changed the weight to 147. Those competing accounts leave the cause of the breakdown disputed.

A Paro fight would allow Haney to turn his attention toward collecting another belt at his established weight. It would also give the Atlanta event a championship main event while Shakur searches for his next opponent.

The next step is getting Paro finalized. Haney has a reported venue hold and a possible opponent, but after spending months on a fight that fell apart, he needs an agreement that gets him back into the ring.

Paro is a significantly better stylistic matchup for fans than Shakur Stevenson. A Haney against Shakur pairing had all the ingredients for twelve rounds of clinching and feinting. Both guys prefer to operate on the outside, pick their moments, and control distance through defensive positioning. Put them together, and you get a low-output chess match where neither wants to lead.

Paro forces the issue. When Paro upset Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico, he showed he does not mind trading in the pocket, digging to the body, and fighting through rough spots.

That pressure directly tests Haney’s vulnerabilities. Haney cannot simply coast behind a safety-first jab for twelve rounds if Paro is actively crowding him, ripping hooks to the ribs, and making every clinch costly. Haney would have to throw real combinations to earn respect and keep Paro off him.

Sports.title: Bam Rodriguez Offers March, But Inoue May Move On
Sports.content:
Jesse Rodriguez is willing to meet Naoya Inoue in March, yet that timeline still depends entirely on the undisputed champion waiting for him. Inoue may prefer an earlier ring return, which would leave Rodriguez on the outside looking in as he continues handling business at bantamweight.

Trainer Robert Garcia revealed that Rodriguez can make a March date work, moving up his original April or May target. Still, the camp intends to take on WBO champion Christian Medina in December first.

Robert confirmed the updated outlook to The Ring: “I previously said April or May, but we can be ready for March.”

While that shortens the wait, early 2027 remains unresolved. Turki Alalshikh pointed toward a January appearance in Japan. Eddie Hearn mentioned February or March instead. Clear alignment on a date is completely absent.

Rodriguez must fulfill a contract before New Year’s Eve, with Garcia eyeing December 11 or December 19 against Medina. The camp figures Rodriguez can enjoy the holidays, then jump straight into camp for Inoue.

That expectation rests on an ideal outcome against Medina. Cuts, bruised knuckles, or an unexpectedly brutal bout could easily force Rodriguez to take extra recovery time. Inoue would effectively be pinning his calendar on a fighter who still has to survive another bout first.

Inoue is already eyeing an eventual jump to featherweight. Sitting around waiting for Rodriguez to finish his stay at 118 pounds makes little sense for the Japanese star.

Garcia admitted neither he nor Hearn has received an official approach to begin talks. The public chatter is moving much faster than the paperwork.

Putting March on the table does not guarantee Inoue’s cooperation. If March works on both sides, the matchup can happen. If Inoue wants to fight sooner, Rodriguez will either have to scrap his December plans or watch this major fight slip away.

Bam is acting like someone who wants the glory of calling out Inoue without actually taking the risk of meeting him on his terms.

When a fighter gets an invitation to share a ring with the sport’s biggest pound-for-pound attraction, they drop everything. They do not tell the undisputed champion to take a number and wait until spring because Christian Medina is on the calendar. That makes zero sense. A routine belt grab against Medina does nothing for Rodriguez’s profile, brings in a fraction of the money, and accomplishes very little that fans care about.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Team Wants Daniel Dubois Fouls Policed
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley’s team wants tighter control of Daniel Dubois’ head-first attacks in Saturday’s rematch, with manager Michael Ofo calling for stronger officiating after their first fight.

The concern is about Wardley being able to punch without Dubois driving into him with his head. Those collisions can interrupt an attack, knock a fighter out of position, and make him hesitate before throwing again.

Dubois recovered from two knockdowns to stop Wardley in May and take the WBO heavyweight title. Ahead of their return at London’s O2 Arena, Ofo has accused the champion of leading with his head and using a tackle during that fight.

“We’re calling for a stronger referee, because it’s needed,” Ofo told Sky Sports Boxing.

Dubois’ trainer Don Charles rejected the criticism, describing the opposing camp’s complaints as “insecurity and weakness.”

Wardley’s camp has a reasonable case for asking the referee to watch those entries closely. When Dubois comes forward behind his punches, head contact can make it difficult for Wardley to plant his feet and counter. Intent is difficult to establish, but repeated collisions still need attention.

That becomes especially important if Wardley hurts Dubois again. He needs the opportunity to follow up without a foul interrupting his work and giving the champion time to recover.

However, Wardley cannot build his approach around the referee intervening. His jab has to give Dubois something to get past, and combinations would make him less predictable than loading up on individual power shots. Moving after punching could also reduce the opportunities for Dubois to drive into him.

Wardley showed he could hurt Dubois in the first fight. The harder task is turning those moments into a finish while avoiding another punishing battle at close range. Firmer officiating could help, but his own adjustments will have to do most of the work. Wardley cannot rely on the third man to solve that puzzle.

If Dubois is going to be stopped from barreling in head-first, Wardley has to make the physical cost of doing so intolerable, just like Oleksandr Usyk did.

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Robinson’s Unbeaten Run Goes Beyond 50-0
Sports.content:
Sugar Ray Robinson’s 91-fight unbeaten run deserves greater recognition than boxing’s fixation on 50-0 allows. He built it after his first defeat, showing how much a fighter can accomplish once a perfect career record is gone.

Floyd Mayweather finished his professional career at 50-0, an exceptional achievement. Robinson’s sequence lasted 41 fights longer, and the case for its superiority rests on more than the number. It included repeated victories over championship opposition while Robinson won world titles at welterweight and middleweight.

Jake LaMotta handed Robinson his first professional defeat in February 1943. Robinson fought him again just three weeks later and won. That willingness to return immediately against the man who had beaten him helped launch a run that continued until Randy Turpin defeated him in 1951.

During those 91 unbeaten fights, Robinson defeated LaMotta four times and Kid Gavilan twice. Henry Armstrong, Sammy Angott and Bobo Olson were also among his victims. He repeatedly accepted the risk of facing accomplished opponents, including return fights against men who already knew his style.

For this writer, that combination of volume, opposition and repeated tests makes Robinson’s run a greater sustained achievement than Mayweather’s perfect career total. Losing to LaMotta did nothing to prevent Robinson from producing the strongest stretch of his career.

Julio Cesar Chavez also took an unbeaten sequence far beyond 50 fights. He won his first 87 before a controversial draw with Pernell Whitaker in September 1993. Two further victories brought him to 89-0-1 before Frankie Randall ended his 90-fight unbeaten run in January 1994.

Chavez’s run included victories over Edwin Rosario, Roger Mayweather, Meldrick Taylor and Hector Camacho. The Whitaker controversy belongs in any honest account, but so do the championship victories Chavez accumulated before Randall finally beat him.

An unbeaten streak can include draws, so these totals measure something different from 50 consecutive wins. Even with that qualification, Robinson and Chavez show how narrow the discussion becomes when a perfect retirement record receives all the attention.

Mayweather earned his place in boxing history. Robinson’s first defeat, however, opened the way to 91 fights that deserve to be judged above a marketable zero.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest 41 suspected criminals in intelligence-led operation at Lapaz and Chantan
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested 41 suspects during an intelligence-led operation targeting criminal and narcotics-related activities at Lapaz and Chantan in Accra.

The operation, carried out by the Service’s Special Operations Team (SOT) at about noon on Thursday, October 15, led to the arrest of 35 males and six females.

In a statement, the police said quantities of dried leaves suspected to be narcotic substances were retrieved during searches conducted on the suspects and within the areas covered by the operation.

According to the police, investigations are under way to establish the source and ownership of the suspected narcotic substances, as well as their intended use.

The Service said the findings would determine the next course of action against the suspects.

“Investigations are ongoing to establish the source, ownership and intended use of the suspected narcotic substances, after which appropriate legal action will be taken against any suspect found culpable,” the statement said.

Ghana News.title: World Food Day 2026: Forikrom women champion local foods and call for stronger support for rural farmers
Ghana News.content:
As the world marks World Food Day under the theme “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow”, women farmers in Forikrom, in the Bono East Region, have added their voices to the global call for action, urging Ghanaians to eat local, support rural farmers, and push for policies that strengthen food security.

The international day, an initiative of the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), comes amid growing pressure on global agrifood systems, with over 36 million people in West and Central Africa still struggling to access sufficient food.

In Forikrom, the day was marked by a mini local food Durbar at the training camp of the Abrono Organic Farming Project (ABOFAP), organised in collaboration with the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana (RUWFAG).

The event brought together women farmers, agricultural extension officers, nutrition experts, and traditional leaders to celebrate Ghana's local foods and advocate for sustainable farming.

Executive Director of ABOFAP, Nana Kwao Adams, encouraged participants to prioritise locally produced food and to work harder to produce enough food for the country.

"We should eat our own food and keep working harder to produce the needed food for the country. It is time we look at policies that will empower rural farmers so that farming becomes sustainable," he said.

Chairing the function, Forikromhemaa Nana Sakyiwaa Abanaba, admonished Ghanaians to embrace the consumption of organic foods, which she described as healthy and beneficial.

"I urge everyone to consume organic foods. They are healthy for our bodies and good for our well-being," she stated.

Anita Suntaa, National Coordinator for the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana, called for policies that will help women farmers produce enough food.

"We need policies that will help women farmers produce enough food. This includes the establishment of irrigation systems to aid all-year-round farming, particularly in the Upper West Region," she said.

Festus Addai, the Techiman Municipal Agric Extension Officer, noted that despite available resources to produce more food, it is quite unfortunate that many people still go hungry.

"With available resources to produce more food, it's quite unfortunate that a lot of people still go hungry. More needs to be done to address this," he emphasised.

Faiza Issah, Nutrition Officer at the Forikrom Health Centre, admonished participants to consume local foods that contain the four-star diet—a nutrition framework promoting a balanced intake of different food groups for good health.

"I admonish us all to consume our local foods that contain the four-star diet for our good health," she advised.

This year's World Food Day commemoration in Forikrom served as a reminder that sustainable food systems begin with supporting those who produce our food—especially rural women farmers—and with a collective commitment to eating what we grow.

As the world reflects on the challenges facing global agrifood systems, the message from Forikrom is clear: empower rural farmers, invest in irrigation, promote organic and local foods, and ensure that no one goes hungry.

Ghana News.title: Fanaka International University & GISI sign MoU to enhance professional capital market training
Ghana News.content:
Fanaka International University College and the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute (GISI) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to integrate professional capital market training into Fanaka’s Master of Science in Finance programme.

The partnership is expected to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice, while equipping students with the skills and professional qualifications needed to pursue careers in the securities and investment industry.

The collaboration between Fanaka International University College and the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute will strengthen professional standards and build capacity within Ghana’s capital market.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Rector of Fanaka International University College, Professor Samuel Agyei-Ampomah, said the collaboration will help enhance knowledge of students in finance and investment.

“The financial curriculum landscape is shifting rapidly, and with GISI’s leadership and continuous professional development, students and faculty will have direct access to cutting-edge insights on modern asset classes, corporate governance and digital financial frameworks”, he said.

Through the collaboration, students will benefit from practical industry exposure and professional development opportunities that could improve their readiness for employment in securities trading, investment management and other areas of the financial services industry.

Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute, Alexander Williams, said the collaboration would promote curriculum benchmarking, professional development and closer engagement between academia and industry.

The agreement also reflects broader efforts to strengthen the relationship between universities and professional institutions, ensuring that graduates leave school with knowledge that responds to the needs of the job market.

For Ghana’s capital market, the collaboration is expected to contribute to the development of a pipeline of skilled professionals who can support investment activities, improve market participation and contribute to the growth of the country’s financial sector.

The partnership is expected to provide students with practical industry exposure and internationally recognised professional development opportunities, while strengthening the pipeline of skilled professionals for Ghana’s securities and investment market.

Ghana News.title: Diana Hamilton releases new single ‘Wate M’anim’
Ghana News.content:
Diana Hamilton has released her new single, “Wate M'anim,” which arrived on Friday, 16 October 2026, across all streaming platforms, alongside its accompanying music video on YouTube.

Written by Cofi Boham and produced by Herbert Crassie (Oshogbo), the song presents a testimony of gratitude, reflecting on God’s faithfulness and the journey that has shaped Diana’s life and ministry.

Meaning “You Have Honoured Me,” “W'ate M'anim” draws attention to the grace behind the journey. Its message encourages listeners to pause, look back, and recognise God’s hand in their own stories, while embracing the future with faith.

For the accompanying video, Diana once again partners with McWillies, continuing a creative relationship that includes work on some of her award-winning videos, such as “Adom” and “Mo ne yo.” Their renewed collaboration brings a personal testimony to the screen through artistic storytelling.

The video offers a glimpse into Diana’s past while using imagery to look towards the future. Moving between remembrance and expectation, it connects where she has come from with the hope she carries for what lies ahead.

This retrospective approach gives audiences an opportunity to reflect on the person and the journey behind the music. The past becomes part of a continuing testimony, while the imagery of the future expresses anticipation for the next chapter.

For those who have followed Diana’s ministry over the years, “Wate M'anim” offers a moment of shared reflection and thanksgiving. For new listeners, it provides an invitation to connect with a message that reaches beyond one person’s experience: every life carries a story, and every testimony can become a source of encouragement to someone else.

As Diana looks back with gratitude and forward with expectation, “W’ate M'anim” invites audiences to do the same, to remember, give thanks, and keep trusting God for the journey ahead.

Stream “W’ate Manim” now on all streaming platforms and watch the accompanying music video on Diana Hamilton’s YouTube channel.

Ghana News.title: Ghana proposes visa waiver agreement with Lebanon to boost bilateral ties
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has proposed a visa waiver agreement with Lebanon covering holders of diplomatic, service, and ordinary passports to strengthen bilateral relations and facilitate travel, trade, and investment between the two countries.

Ghana’s Ambassador to the Republic of Lebanon, with residence in Cairo, Egypt, H.E. Prof. Justice Solomon Korantwi-Barimah, highlighted the proposal during the presentation of his Letters of Credence to Lebanese President H.E. Joseph Aoun in Beirut on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

The proposed agreement is expected to promote people-to-people exchanges, facilitate business engagements and reinforce the longstanding friendship between Ghana and Lebanon.

Prof. Korantwi-Barimah reaffirmed Ghana’s readiness to work with the Lebanese government to identify new areas of cooperation and advance shared interests.

Strengthening longstanding relations

The Ambassador conveyed greetings from President John Dramani Mahama, the Government and people of Ghana to President Aoun and the people of Lebanon.

He underscored Ghana’s commitment to deepening relations with Lebanon, noting that the two countries established formal diplomatic ties in the early years of Ghana’s independence in 1957. Lebanon, he said, was the second country in the Middle East with which Ghana established formal diplomatic relations.

He added that the relationship predated formal diplomatic engagement and had grown over the years through commercial exchanges, people-to-people interactions and the settlement of Lebanese nationals in Ghana.

Prof. Korantwi-Barimah acknowledged the contributions of the Lebanese community to Ghana’s social and economic development, describing its integration into Ghanaian society as evidence of the enduring friendship and mutual trust between the two countries.

Trade and investment opportunities

On economic cooperation, the Ambassador commended Lebanese businesses for their longstanding investments in Ghana and their contributions to the country’s development.

He expressed Ghana’s interest in expanding collaboration with Lebanon in trade, investment, hospitality, education, healthcare and tourism.

According to him, stronger partnerships in these sectors could open up investment opportunities, encourage knowledge and skills transfer, create jobs and support sustainable economic growth in both countries.

He reiterated Ghana’s willingness to engage the Lebanese government and private sector to translate the longstanding relationship into practical economic benefits.

Cooperation on international issues

Prof. Korantwi-Barimah also expressed Ghana’s appreciation for Lebanon’s support for the adoption of United Nations General Assembly Resolution A/RES/80/250, concerning the trafficking of enslaved Africans and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans as the gravest crime against humanity.

He described Lebanon’s support as a demonstration of international solidarity and recognition of the importance of historical truth, justice and human dignity.

The Ambassador further highlighted Ghana’s longstanding contribution to the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), noting that the country’s participation reflected its commitment to international peace and security.

He reaffirmed Ghana’s support for peaceful conflict resolution and diplomatic initiatives aimed at promoting dialogue, stability and security at the regional and international levels.

He also expressed interest in strengthening cooperation with Lebanon on issues of mutual concern, including sustainable development and relations between Africa and the Middle East.

Labour and migration

On labour and migration, the Ambassador welcomed discussions between the two governments on establishing appropriate frameworks to manage labour mobility and migration.

He said closer cooperation could promote orderly migration, strengthen institutional collaboration and improve workers’ welfare and protection in line with applicable national laws and international obligations.

Prof. Korantwi-Barimah expressed Ghana’s readiness to engage relevant Lebanese authorities to explore practical arrangements that address the concerns of both countries.

Commitment to deeper cooperation

The Ambassador reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to working with the Lebanese government and relevant institutions to strengthen cooperation at both bilateral and multilateral levels.

He expressed confidence that sustained dialogue and mutual understanding would create further opportunities for collaboration and deepen the longstanding friendship between the two countries.

He also thanked President Aoun for the warm reception accorded to him and his delegation, expressing optimism about a productive tenure focused on advancing the shared interests of Ghana and Lebanon.

Ghana News.title: Disqualify Obuasi SHTS headmaster from Juaben NDC chairmanship race – Former NDC MP urges party
Ghana News.content:
Former National Democratic Congress (NDC) Member of Parliament for Amenfi Central, Peter Kwakye Ackah, has called on the party to disqualify the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, from contesting the party’s upcoming constituency election, saying his candidacy would be a disgrace to the party.

Mr Abdulai, who is accused of sexually abusing about 16 students at the school, is contesting the chairmanship of the NDC in the Juaben constituency.

Speaking on Adom TV’s Nnawɔtwe Yi on Saturday, October 17, Mr Ackah said party membership should not protect him.

“Nobody should shield such a person after he has raped someone’s child just because he’s a party member,” Mr Ackah said.

The Ghana Education Service (GES) has interdicted Mr Abdulai following a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, and a complaint has been lodged with the police.

Mr Ackah urged the constituency vetting committee to bar Zakaria from the race.

“I am appealing to the constituency vetting committee not to allow such a person to lead the party; he will collapse the party.”

He also asked the party’s national leadership to ensure that Mr Abdulai is suspended from the NDC, adding that there was no justification for what the headmaster is alleged to have done.

The former MP said suspension alone is not enough and called on the President, the Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, and the Interior Minister, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, to get involved.

“I’m appealing to the President to take it up and give the order to the Minister. Haruna, you must not sit on this at all.”

Mr Ackah also faulted the Obuasi Municipal Chief Executive, saying she failed to handle the matter properly after one victim’s family approached her.

“The girl is even ashamed to come out, so since her parents have come to you, why didn’t you take action… what is happening?” he questioned.

He said the student unrest that brought the case to public attention was not wrong, arguing that the students took matters into their own hands because they saw that the law was not working.

Such actions, he warned, will become the order of the day if the law keeps failing. The GES has said the unrest led to the destruction of school property and the temporary closure of the school.

Ghana News.title: NPP has resolved its internal wrangling – Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer for the 2028 elections and former Vice President, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has urged party members at the constituency and polling station levels to remain united and formidable.

He stated that the NPP would win the 2028 elections, but emphasised that they must be united to make that possible.

The former Vice President urged supporters at the grassroots level to work tirelessly to help the party win more parliamentary seats in the next general election.

He said that with a majority in Parliament, his government would be able to implement policies and interventions to improve the socio-economic conditions of Ghanaians.

Dr Bawumia gave the advice when he joined Muslim prayers at Kintampo as part of his thank-you tour of the Bono East Region. He also commended the NPP for successfully electing its constituency, regional and national executives ahead of the 2028 elections.

Accompanied by some national, regional and constituency executives of the NPP, the party leader presented GH¢30,000 in cash to the Muslim community in Kintampo.

Dr Bawumia called on the Kintampo Muslim community to rally behind the party to help it regain power.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Why adults are going back to summer camp
World.content:
Remedy for loneliness and burnout?

Adults across generations — from Gen X to Millennials to Gen Z — are embracing camp life as a remedy for two major ills of modern life: loneliness and burnout.

“Hundreds of millions of people every day feel a gap between their level of connection and where they want it to be, for a variety of reasons: social media and AI leading to feeling disconnected, not going into the office, living far away from their families, not having connected neighbourhoods,” said Adam “Smiley” Poswolsky, a keynote speaker and author who specialises in human connection and workplace culture.

Poswolsky’s career naturally grew out of his experience as an adult camp counselor at Camp Grounded from 2013 to 2017.

“I think the idea of adult camp might initially produce an eyeroll. ‘Why would an adult need camp? It’s childlike; we’re too old.’ But it’s the exact opposite,” said Poswolsky, who met his now-wife, Ali, at Camp Grounded.

“It’s the very thing many adults are missing the most — this chance to play and opportunity to connect with people that’s not related to networking, your career, your title.”

In 2023, Melanie Kelly, 44, felt burnt out from her work running marketing and communications for a solar company. A former painting major, she signed up for a weeklong art-making camp at Anderson Ranch Arts Center in Snowmass Village, Colorado in the US, to see if she could rediscover the “flow state” she remembered from painting that she rarely experienced at work.

Overnight, Kelly’s days went from being spent answering emails and staring at her computer screen to creating tangible art and sharing workshop space with like-minded campers.

“I was always trying to be more productive in a work sense or seeking professional development aligned with my work,” said Kelly. Art camp was the antidote to that tendency.

“It feels like there’s a bit of release in these types of moments or activities because you’re allowing yourself to rest,” she said. “Rest isn’t sleep. The opposite of work isn’t sleep; it’s play.”

Outside of workshop time, the art programme at Anderson Ranch also organised meals and activities for attendees to make socialising as frictionless as possible. While many of these camps are attended by couples, groups of girlfriends or, in Aronov’s company’s case, coworkers, they also cater to solo campers looking to meet new people.

At Michigan’s Camp Forever Fun, founder Joel Reisig actively encourages single attendees with the promise of a safe, fun and connected experience.

Reisig, a movie producer, had the idea to open an adult camp about a decade ago, after filming a movie about a group of girls attending horse camp. After shooting wrapped each day, the cast and crew relaxed by stargazing, petting horses and having dance parties.

“I thought to myself, adults need a summer camp break every bit as much as kids do,” Reisig said.

“It is very hard to make new friends after college. You are generally interacting with a few neighbours and a couple of people you work with. A weekend at Camp Forever Fun is a time to relax, climb the rock wall, sit in a kayak, ride a horse and actually have real conversations and possibly friendships with other stressed-out adults.”

At Camp Forever Fun, it’s 100 percent socially acceptable to introduce yourself to every single person at camp with zero fear of rejection. That’s not something most adults are able to find at a bar or coffee shop — and certainly not from the comfort of their couch, where people are increasingly spending their time. (According to a 2024 study, from 2003 to 2022, the average time Americans spend at home on a typical day has risen by one hour and 39 minutes.)

Alyx van der Vorm, 25, is a John Harvard Scholar who studied neuroscience and is the founder of social connection platform Clyx. She attributes rising rates of loneliness in part to how easy it’s become to get what we need without ever leaving home.

“So many things have been made frictionless, from laundry to ordering food, that when it actually comes to making plans, it seems like a bit of a mountain,” she says. “Add the fact that not everyone wants to be reaching out and initiating, and you suddenly have people spending a lot less time in person.”

That erosion of boundaries extends beyond social life: home, work and leisure are increasingly bleeding into one another. Since 2020, work increasingly follows people home, a recipe for burnout. According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, in March 2026, 22.6 percent of American workers teleworked, compared to just 17.9 percent in 2022. Telework was so rare before the coronavirus pandemic that the agency did not even measure rates prior to that.

“Many adults are now working in environments that constantly ask them to produce, multitask and stay connected,” said Matthew Leahy, a licensed clinical psychologist who has spent years designing and running camp programmes. “AI has only increased this. Even our downtime often becomes another form of consumption through our devices.”

Camp programmes and spending time in nature interrupt that cycle, Leahy said.

“Instead of focusing on productivity, at camp we encourage presence. People spend time outdoors, try new things, laugh, play and engage with others simply because it’s enjoyable.”

Adult camps “offer a container”, explained Sarah Boss, psychiatrist and clinical director of The Balance clinic, in Mallorca, Spain. “In that container, normal rules are suspended. Permission is given to be silly, to be bad at things and to talk to strangers. And that permission does a lot of the therapeutic work.”

Leahy believes that people aren’t necessarily looking to escape adulthood so much as environments where every hour feels like it has to be productive or plugged in.

“I don’t think adults are trying to relive childhood so much as recover some of the emotional experiences that childhood offered — wonder, awe, playfulness and genuine connection,” he said.

Loneliness and burnout aren’t just affecting people in the United States; the adult camp trend is growing globally as well.

Sarah El Nabulsi, a licensed clinical psychologist based in Dubai, is seeing this same burnout among her patients. Adult camps are also on the rise in the UAE, like the Bear Grylls Explorers Camp in Jebel Jais, Ras Al Khaimah, which opened in 2021 as a collection of nine recycled shipping container cabins and has since expanded to 16.

Meanwhile, the broader outdoor adventure market is also attracting visitors. Hatta Resorts and Wadi Hub, a glamping and outdoor-adventure destination in Dubai’s Hajar Mountains, welcomed more than 351,000 visitors between September 2023 and April 2024 — a 40.4 percent increase over the previous season, according to Dubail Holding.

“What I see in session, repeatedly, is that adults aren’t burned out from work alone; they’re burned out from the absence of unstructured, low-stakes social contact,” El Nabulsi said.

“Adult life strips out almost every context where people used to make friends without trying: no assigned seating, no shared schedule, no built-in repetition of seeing the same faces. Camp reintroduces exactly that structure, low-pressure, physical, screen-free and bounded in time.”

World.title: Hurricane Trudy makes its way towards Mexico, threatening heavy rain
World.content:
Trudy is the latest in successive storms that have hit Mexico’s Pacific coast this year.

Share Hurricane Trudy makes its way towards Mexico, threatening heavy rain on social media

Hurricane Trudy ‌maintained its strength as it moved towards Mexico’s western ⁠coast on ⁠Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen further before beginning to weaken on Sunday.

A hurricane warning was in effect from Manzanillo in Colima state to Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco.

The United States National Hurricane Center said ⁠Trudy was about 305km (190 miles) south-southeast of Manzanillo early on Saturday, with maximum sustained winds of 150 km/h (90mph).

The hurricane was moving at about 13km/h (8mph) and was forecast to approach southwestern and west-central Mexico later on Saturday before passing near the coast overnight into Sunday.

Hurricane conditions are expected ‌in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region during the day, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch.

Trudy is forecast to bring 10 to 20cm (four to eight inches) of rain, ⁠with isolated totals of about 38cm (15 ⁠inches), across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC.

Outer ⁠rain bands could produce two to four inches of rain, with isolated totals of ⁠approximately 15cm (six inches), in Guerrero and Nayarit, ⁠where localised flash flooding is possible, the centre said.

The NHC also warned of possible coastal flooding from storm surge in areas exposed to onshore winds, accompanied ‌by large and destructive waves.



Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico’s southwestern coast and are expected to spread ‌northward towards ‌the country’s west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

The Mexican navy urged the maritime community and coastal residents to exercise extreme caution due to high waves, heavy rains and the risk of rising river levels, flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas.

The state of Colima has said that risks are currently low, but the storm could bring significant rainfall that could have damaging effects due to the saturated ground following the successive storms that have hit the Pacific coast.

World.title: Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal: Premier League – preview, teams, prediction
World.content:
The Gunners failed to score in their last two visits to the City Ground, as both matches ended in goalless draws.

Share Arsenal look to end goal drought at Forest in Premier League clash on social media

Who: Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal

What: English Premier League

Where: City Ground, Nottingham, United Kingdom

When: Sunday, October 18 , at 4:30pm (15:30 GMT)

How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 12:30 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Arsenal will try to end their goal drought at the City Ground when they play Nottingham Forest on Sunday – the Gunners failed to score in their last two visits, as both matches ended in goalless draws.

Meanwhile, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said his side had learned lessons from their “extremely average” performance at Brighton before the international break as they returned to winning ways against Leeds last weekend.

The Spaniard was left to stew for 21 days after the 3-0 humbling at the Amex last month – the first defeat of the season for the Premier League champions.

But the Gunners got that performance out of their system at the Emirates last Saturday, coming from behind to beat Leeds 2-1.

Arsenal also cruised to a 3-0 home win over Lille in midweek to extend their perfect start in the Champions League.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner was beaten on his return to Crystal Palace as Daichi Kamada’s first Premier League goal inspired the Eagles’ 3-1 win last weekend.

Arsenal headed into this weekend in second place in the Premier League, three points behind Manchester City, while Nottingham Forest were 15th.

What happened in Arsenal’s last Premier League game?

Arsenal got back on track as the Premier League champions survived a scare to beat Leeds, although Arteta’s side were in danger of a second successive loss when they fell behind at the Emirates Stadium.



James Justin fired Leeds ahead in the 55th minute after Arsenal failed to clear Gabriel Gudmundsson’s cross.

Arteta had admitted Arsenal were nursing a “pain in the tummy” from the Brighton loss, but Italy defender Riccardo Calafiori found the cure when he converted Ben White’s header from close range in the 62nd minute.

Arsenal showcased their strength in depth as substitute Bruno Guimaraes drilled the winner from the edge of the area just six minutes after coming off the bench.

The Brazilian’s first goal at the Emirates since his close-season move from Newcastle made it five wins from six league matches for the Gunners.

What happened in Forest’s last Premier League game?

Glasner had led Palace to a shock FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City in 2025 and masterminded their UEFA Conference League success in May.

But the 52-year-old Austrian opted to quit Selhurst Park after reported issues with the club’s hierarchy over their transfer policy, opening the way for his move to Forest.

He was greeted warmly by Palace fans before kickoff and it looked like being a victorious return for Glasner when Forest’s Dan Ndoye opened the scoring in the third minute.

But Forest wasted a host of chances to increase their lead and Japan midfielder Kamada levelled in the 41st minute to end his long wait for a top-flight goal.

Jefferson Lerma nodded Palace in front in first-half stoppage time and Yeremy Pino’s 59th-minute goal sent Glasner home empty-handed.

What have the managers said about the game?

Mikel Arteta, Arsenal manager:

“We’re going to try really hard to score goals and to prevent goals as well. It’s going to be a really tough match, they’re an extremely well-coached team.

“We know that, we already have experience with Oliver [Glasner] in the past and they’re a team that at home can create a really special momentum, so we are ready for it.”

Oliver Glasner, Forest manager:

“In every game this season [Arsenal] were outrunning the opposition. It’s incredible. The effort and the mindset Mikel [Arteta] has created there is incredible.

“This makes it so tough to play against them and you see it from every single player. They have so many world-class players they can react from the bench.”

Prediction:

The Opta supercomputer has made Arsenal the clear favourites, with a win probability of 58.3 percent. Forest were given a 20.4 percent chance of winning, a draw is 21.3 percent.

Head-to-head



Matches: 109

Arsenal wins: 56

Forest wins: 29

Draws: 24

Last five encounters:

January 17, 2026: Forest 0-0 Arsenal (Premier League)

September 13, 2025: Arsenal 3-0 Forest (Premier League)

February 26, 2025: Forest 0-0 Arsenal (Premier League)

November 23, 2024: Arsenal 3-0 Forest (Premier League)

January 30, 2024: Forest 1-2 Arsenal (Premier League)

The last time Forest beat Arsenal was a 1-0 victory at the City Ground in May 2023, courtesy of a goal by Taiwo Awoniyi, which ended the Gunners’ title hopes that year.

What happened the last time the clubs played?

Arsenal missed a slew of chances in a 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest in January as a dogged defensive performance from Forest and wasteful finishing from the Arsenal forwards meant they took only a point from a game they dominated for long spells.

The best chance of the game fell to Arsenal substitute Bukayo Saka, who headed a Declan Rice cross back towards the far post, but Forest keeper Matz Sels pulled off a superb fingertip save to deny him.

Forest’s team news

Striker Igor Jesus and defender Nicolo Savona remain unavailable due to calf and knee injuries, respectively.

Key playmaker Morgan Gibbs-White is struggling with a minor muscular problem and is a doubt, while centre-back Nikola Milenkovic is back in training after a knee injury and could feature.

Predicted starting XI:

Sels (goalkeeper); Aina, Diomande, Murillo; Munoz, Schlager, McAtee, Williams; Gibbs-White, Ndoye; Delap

Arsenal’s team news

Winger Christos Tzolis (hamstring) and centre-back William Saliba (back) are unavailable for the Gunners.

Arteta said midfielder Martin Zubimendi could be fit to face Forest, but defender Piero Hincapie would likely miss the trip to the City Ground.

The pair suffered freak ankle injuries during a training session on the Emirates Stadium pitch after last week’s win against Leeds.

“Piero is evolving really well,” said Arteta. “Knowing his character and the way he pushes everybody, I’m sure it’s not going to take long, but he will probably need another week or two.

“Zubi looks much better, he already looked much better today. We have another session tomorrow (Saturday) and after that we will assess whether he’s available to play against Forest.”

Predicted starting XI:

Raya (goalkeeper); White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz

World.title: Egypt’s Sisi seeks authorisation for defence assistance to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Egyptian president pledges ‘any measure’ to help defend Saudi Arabia ‘if it is requested of us’.

Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has called for an emergency parliamentary session to authorise him to approve any requests from Saudi Arabia for defence assistance, if Riyadh were to ask.

Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy on Saturday, el-Sisi emphasised Cairo’s readiness to back the kingdom.

Egypt will “carry out any measure to protect” Saudi Arabia “in accordance with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and the directives of the Crown Prince, Mohammed bin Salman”, he said.

“I know that this matter requires the approval of the Egyptian parliament, and I hope that parliament will convene in an emergency session to give us this authorisation, if it is requested of us,” he said.

“I am not speaking in order for us to fight anyone or attack anyone. I am speaking only for defence.”

Attacks on Saudi Arabia

The request follows a barrage of attacks on the kingdom from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, including airports and oil facilities.

Recent Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia have mainly targeted key infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, Riyadh, but they appear to be edging closer to the city centre.

Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport earlier this month killed 14 people and wounded more than 300. Houthi attacks have also been reported on other airports, including Dammam, Abha, Jazan and Najran.

Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government launched a full-scale military campaign against the Houthis this month to recapture territory seized by them.



El-Sisi had backed Saudi calls for secure and unhindered navigation in the Red Sea in a meeting with the Saudi Crown Prince, known as MBS, in Cairo last month.

A statement from the Egyptian presidency then said that “the security of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states is an integral part of Egypt’s national security”.

Red Sea security

That meeting came just days after the Houthis seized Yemen’s Red Sea coast, gaining significant control over the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.

Saudi Arabia already has a defence pact with Pakistan and Turkiye, known as the Mecca Alliance for Defence, which was signed in August.

Earlier this month, the three countries agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under the pact and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

Analysts say Riyadh is looking for help to protect the kingdom and Red Sea shipping and that Egypt, whose Suez Canal revenue depends on the same traffic, is an obvious partner.

They say Egypt is eager to prevent Iran and its allies from imposing control over the region, especially over maritime traffic in the Red Sea, given the direct repercussions for the Suez Canal.

Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging Houthi attacks against the kingdom, a claim Tehran rejects. Iran has offered assistance to halt the conflict between the two sides.

World.title: California Gov Newsom boosts AI regulation as he eyes 2028 presidential run
World.content:
Newsom signed an executive order to examine kill switches for AI models and other measures he had earlier vetoed.

San Francisco, United States – In his last few executive orders signed as California governor, Gavin Newsom, whose final term ends in January, issued one asking for independent verification of artificial intelligence models and set up an expert committee to create kill switches for AI agents that could go rogue and cause harm.

In 2024, Newsom vetoed a bill, passed in the state assembly, asking for similar requirements that the governor has now called for in his executive order. Newsom said at the time that it would amount to “thwarting the promise of this technology”.

Now eyeing a 2028 United States presidential run, he wants to expand the definition of safety incidents, potentially to include the recent series of safety breaches, explore a kill switch and include other measures that were in the vetoed bill.

“He is in a lame duck period here,” says Alex Hanna, director of research at the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR), unsure that the measures will pass in the remainder of his term. “He is setting up his next thing.”

US voters are increasingly concerned about AI safety, data centres and job losses, and this could show Newsom is acting to address this, Hanna says.

After vetoing the 2024 bill, Newsom had asked Scott Wiener, the state senator who drafted the bill, to redraft it in consultation with an expert committee. He signed that frontier AI bill, the nation’s first, into law in October 2025. It asks large developers to disclose certain safety incidents, including the deaths of 50 or more people, large-scale cyberattacks or monetary theft.



Christabel Randolph, associate director at the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP), says, “It seems the governor operated from the premise that a slower pace of regulation would be sufficient because the companies would pace their investments, and did not anticipate that the companies would be accelerating the risks.”

AI companies have reportedly had thousands of safety incidents in internal and real-world tests in the last few months. These include efforts by agents to get information from the US Securities and Exchange Commission and Census Bureau, as well as confidential information from Australian and Canadian government sites. AI startup Hugging Face had earlier revealed that OpenAI agents had infiltrated its systems, one among a spate of such incidents.

“No governor has been more out-front on addressing the risks of AI than Governor Newsom,” Tara Gallegos, the governor’s director of communications, told Al Jazeera.

Monopoly of big AI companies

In his message vetoing the bill in September 2024, Newsom had said “the bill applies stringent standards to even the most basic functions” and noted that 32 of the world’s 50 leading AI companies are in California.

Industry representatives, too, had rallied against the bill.

“In essence, the bill is creating this disastrous regressive tax on AI innovation,” Anjney Midha, general partner at the Bay Area-based venture capital firm Andresen Horowitz, had said at the time. If enacted, it would force AI founders to move elsewhere, Midha warned.

“The bill was unworkable when it reached his desk,” Newsom’s spokesperson Gallegos told Al Jazeera.

But Hamid Ekbia, professor at Syracuse University and founding director of the Academic Alliance for AI Policy, says industry cannot be relied on to regulate itself.

“There is a need to break down the monopoly of the big AI companies,” Ekbia told Al Jazeera.

“Their financial stakes are too high,” to self-regulate, he said, referring to Open AI and Anthropic’s upcoming public offerings and tax breaks that some companies are reportedly taking advantage of to build data centres.

Newsom has now set up an expert committee to examine setting up a kill switch, which had been proposed in a more comprehensive manner in the original bill.

“SB 1047 [the bill that was vetoed] had a concrete architecture; the EO [executive order] only includes one aspect – the Kill Switch or shutdown/stoppage mechanisms, which is quite different and weaker than the ex ante termination obligation of SB 1047,” which required stronger safety measures even before training runs of the AI models could start, CAIDP’s Randolph said.



DAIR’s Hanna says that with the order, Newsom “is showing he is attentive without planning anything drastic”.

Building AI safety in real time

“We are building the field of AI safety in real time,” says Rebecca Finlay, chief executive officer of Partnership for AI, a nonprofit that works on technology governance, underscoring the challenges of regulating an industry growing at a meteoric pace.

Newsom has asked the California Emergency Services Office to send recommendations on AI regulation by November 15 and could convene a special legislative session to discuss how to implement these, possibly before his term ends.

This would be in contrast to the federal government, which has pushed for self-regulation by industry. CAIDP’s Randolph says California could play an important role in setting the floor for AI regulation given that much of the global AI industry is based there.

DAIR’s Hanna says Newsom is not only looking to show a contrast with US President Donald Trump, who believes in self-regulation by firms and last month signed a voluntary accord with several AI leaders, but also with possible Democratic contenders.

“With this, Newsom can look good on the primary debate stage,” she said.

Gallegos, the governor’s spokesperson, told Al Jazeera that “Governor Newsom isn’t interested in virtue-signalling or chasing headlines — he is leading the nation by taking a smarter, strategic, and effective approach to addressing frontier technology”.

Experts say that along with Newsom’s order setting up a committee to examine a kill switch, there is a need for measures for controls across the life cycle to reinforce safety.

“Safety needs to be built in. We issued 12 guidances across the lifecycle when the last ChatGPT model was released. There is a need for safety features throughout the life cycle,” of an AI model, Partnership for AI’s Finlay said.

As Newsom considers such recommendations from California agencies and the expert committee, Ekbia says governments “should take a lesson from what happened with social media. A handful of companies having control were able to do a lot of harm,” and regulate with an anticipatory approach and take on corporate monopolies.

World.title: Protesters clash with police during nationwide demonstrations in France
World.content:
Thousands rally in Paris and other cities for demonstrations set to unite students, teachers, unions and ‘yellow vests’.

Share Protesters clash with police during nationwide demonstrations in France on social media

Protesters have clashed with police in cities across France as major rallies take place across the country.

Scuffles broke out on Saturday in the capital, Paris, between groups of protesters and police, who used tear gas to push back people wearing hoods and masks.

The demonstrations are set to unite students, teachers, trade unions, and the resurging ‘yellow vest’ movement – remnants of the grassroots cost-of-living protests that shook France in 2018.

Large numbers of riot police were deployed in the Place de la Republique, a square northeast of the city centre, and surrounding streets on Saturday. Dozens of people were reportedly already detained.

Reporting from Paris, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said “a lot” of stun grenades and tear gas were being used by police.

She said that what began as a peaceful protests “never really got started”, as police quickly moved to isolate protesters, effectively trapping them between police lines. “That is where some of the trouble began,” Butler said.

In the southern city of Marseille, meanwhile, local media reported that protesters breached the town hall and looted shops in the city’s commercial district, while in Lyon, media reports said the local tourism office was set ablaze.

This is a “key moment” for France, said Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard, reporting from the western French city of Rennes.

“There are budget negotiations going on; the French government is trying to find ways to curb its ballooning national debt, and there consequential presidential elections happening next year,” she said.



France’s Interior Ministry had recorded 140 protest actions across the country by midday on Saturday, with 32,800 participants. The ministry said over 250 people had been arrested nationwide so far.

‘Where are we going as a country?’

Saturday’s protests against the rising costs of goods like fuel and food come on the back of weeks of rallies from French high school students, who took to the streets to protest poor conditions in their schools.

Some children who attended those high school protests reported serious injuries at the hands of police, including the case of one 15-year-old girl who lost a hand.
