World.title: Beer, rugby and AK-47s: HOW 1981 Seychelles coup unraveled
World.content:
The story of the botched 1981 Seychelles coup under 'Mad Mike' Hoare would be too farcical for even a Sly Stallone action flick. Image: File/Fotor

The story of the failed 1981 Seychelles coup is one the Department of Defence may wish never happened. An example of an isolated government in Apartheid being overconfident, under prepared and paying the price for it. Nevertheless, 45 years on, their hubris is something we can learn from …

It’s 25 November 1981. And a group of about 50 men step off a flight in the Seychelles posing as tourists on a stag trip. They call themselves the Ancient Order of Froth-Blowers. This happens to be a name borrowed from a real 1930s English beer-drinking club. The only difference is beneath false bottoms in their luggage, covered with rugby kit, is a barrage of AK-47s.

1981 SEYCHELLES COUP

The target in this hastily arranged 1981 Seychelles coup is President France-Albert René. He had seized power in 1977 by ousting James Mancham, a pro-Western leader. The aim was to put Mancham back in charge. The mission was being led by Colonel ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare. The Irishman was a legendary Congo mercenary, born in Calcutta, but living in Durban at the time.



The disguises in this 1981 Seychelles coup lasted all of a few minutes when they encountered an inquisitive customs official. A search turned up one of the many hidden rifles and gunfire erupted all across the airport. Cornered, the mercenaries fought their way to the airport control tower and held it hostage for several hours.

With no way out, they spotted their escape: An Air India Boeing 707, Flight 224, which was refueling on its way from Salisbury to Bombay. They commandeered it, with 65 passengers and 14 crew aboard, and ordered it to fly it back to South Africa. It was eventually diverted to Durban, where officials had shut down air traffic control for seven hours, and forced the mercenaries to surrender.

AFTERMATH OF FAILED 1981 SEYCHELLES COUP

Air India 707. Image: File

The Apartheid regime had a big problem, the world was watching and the reaction to the failed 1981 Seychelles coup was fierce. Most of the men were initially released, however, hijacking an airliner is serious and the government needed to deniability. So, ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare and 42 others were eventually charged and convicted of hijacking in a Pietermaritzburg court in 1982.



Hoare’s sentence, reported to be 20 years, was served in just 33 months before a presidential amnesty freed him. Other men received similarly short terms. The UN Security Council condemned the coup attempt in resolutions 496 and 507. René was only emboldened and stayed in power for another two decades.

But what do you think? Had you ever heard of the 1981 Seychelles coup? Do you have any other examples of crazy South African stories many might’ve forgotten? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: DStv to remove popular kids channel this November
World.content:
A popular children's channel will be cut from DStv this November. Image: canva / file

DStv is losing another international TV channel, with preschool channel JimJam set to disappear from the platform in November after more than a decade.

JimJam will be removed from DStv on 11 November 2026, bringing an end to its 13-year run on the pay-TV service.

The channel, provided by AMC Networks International (AMCNI), was added to DStv in November 2013. MultiChoice has confirmed the channel’s departure but has not explained why it is being removed.



JimJam to leave DStv

MultiChoice told TVwithThinus that JimJam is being removed as DStv continues to “review and refine its channel line-up”, but the broadcaster did not provide a specific reason for ending the channel’s distribution.

JimJam is also notably the last remaining AMC Networks International channel on DStv, meaning its departure will bring the relationship between the two companies to an end on the platform.

MultiChoice added that it will continue to invest in preschool entertainment despite JimJam’s departure.

Sthembiso Semenya, a MultiChoice spokesperson, said DStv is investing in preschool children’s programming through PlayRoom, which brings together local and international content for younger viewers.

Depending on their DStv package, families can also access preschool programming through Cartoonito, CBeebies and DreamWorks.

DStv customers can check the platform’s TV Guide for the channels and programmes available on their specific package.



The latest in a string of channel cuts

The channel’s departure comes during a year of significant changes to DStv’s channel line-up.

MultiChoice has already removed a number of channels in 2026, including BET Africa, MTV Base, CBS Justice and CBS Reality in January.

Cinemagic and Magic Showcase were subsequently removed at the end of June, while M-Net Movies 1, kykNET Lekker, Mzansi Bioskop and Mzansi Magic were discontinued in September.

The changes have also affected DStv’s specialist packages.

In October, MultiChoice announced that five channels would be removed from its R280 Add Indian package from 31 October.

These are SET Asia, Zee TV, SET Max, Zee Cinema and WION, leaving the package with just three channels: Star Plus, Star Vijay and Colors TV.

At the time, MultiChoice said it was refining the line-up to better match how customers watch content and was moving towards “fewer, stronger channels” rather than spreading similar content across more channels.

That decision followed DStv’s major package overhaul in September, after Canal+ completed its acquisition of MultiChoice’s parent company in 2025.

World.title: Orlando Pirates sweat over Sebelebele as Chiefs Derby looms
World.content:
Orlando Pirates could receive a timely boost ahead of the Soweto Derby, with Kamogelo Sebelebele potentially returning to action in time for their highly anticipated clash against Kaizer Chiefs at the end of the month.

The 23-year-old right-back suffered an injury setback during the first half of the MTN8 final against Mamelodi Sundowns, forcing him off the pitch as the Buccaneers went on to lose the match.

Sebelebele subsequently missed Pirates’ midweek encounter against TS Galaxy and is also expected to sit out Saturday’s CAF Champions League clash against African Stars.



His absence has left Pirates monitoring his recovery, with the Soweto Derby against their bitter rivals Chiefs looming on the horizon.

The injury could also present an opportunity for new signing Bulelani Sigomoshe to stake his claim for a place in the team as head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou considers his options at right-back.

Speaking about the defender’s condition, Ouaddou confirmed that Sebelebele was still being assessed by the club’s medical department, although he remains hopeful that the injury is not serious.



“He is still being assessed by the medical department. I still hope it is not so bad. But we will have some more news, I think, soon,” the Pirates coach said.

Ouaddou also ruled the defender out of the upcoming CAF Champions League fixture against African Stars but stopped short of confirming when he could return.

“But I think for the Champions League, definitely I cannot use him, but we will see for the next games if we can have him or not. We hope it’s not so bad,” he added as per FARPost.



Pirates will be hoping for positive news from their medical team as they prepare for a demanding run of fixtures. However, Sebelebele’s availability for the Soweto Derby will depend on the progress of his recovery.

Sebelebele has become an important player for Pirates

Since joining Orlando Pirates in 2025, Sebelebele has established himself as an important member of the squad, with his pace and attacking threat making him a valuable option on the right flank.



His performances have also earned him recognition at international level, as he has represented Bafana Bafana at the FIFA World Cup.

With the Soweto Derby fast approaching, Pirates will be eager to have the defender available for the crucial encounter. For now, the Buccaneers must wait for further medical assessments before determining whether he will be fit to face Kaizer Chiefs.

Who should replace Sebelebele?

World.title: ‘Happy valedictory day babes’: Rachel Kolisi shows Siya’s sister love
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi showed Liphelo, the sister of her ex-husband Siya Kolisi, love and support as she ends her schooling career, via an Instagram post on Saturday 17 October.

RACHEL KOLISI TO SIYA’S SISTER: ‘HAPPY VALEDICTORY DAY BABES’

Siya Kolisi’s sister, Liphelo Madlingozi is completing her matric year in 2026. Rachel Kolisi, the ex-wife of Siya, took to Instagram to celebrate Liphelo ending her school career. Take a look…

“Happy valedictory day babes 😭♥️. 2 down 2 to go! 😅,” she wrote.



Fans took to the comments section of the post to gush over Rachel.

“God bless you, sweetheart! ❤️ May He meet you at the point of your needs, enlarge your territory, and take you to even greater heights. May His favour and grace continue to follow you always! 🙏❤️,” wrote @zanndzube.



“Great support from you. Keep on with your good work🙏🌹🌹🌹,” wrote @gert.ferrerira.79.

“You’re doing such a great job. God bless you😍😍. They will never forget your constant love and support,” wrote @titusxolile.

“Well done to Phelo 🎊💯🙏🌸but Ms Rachel…this glow up is something else🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏,” wrote @jacobsshelley.







RACHEL AND SIYA KOLISI LEGALLY ADOPTED HIS SIBLINGS

Siya has two half-siblings Liyema and Liphelo. The siblings were reportedly left bouncing from orphanages to foster homes after their mother and father passed away. Siya and Rachel officially adopted his siblings in 2014, when they were financially stable enough to do so.

Siya reportedly found his siblings in foster care in Zwide – a township in Gqeberha. Siya explained that when he went to see his siblings, his sister didn’t know him.

“My little sister didn’t know me. She had been crawling when I last saw her. I told the woman taking care of them that I was going to take them for December holidays that year, which I did. But afterwards I said I can’t send them back,” he said according to reports.



“I had to go through a legal process, which I started after that holiday. It took about 18 months, but I finally legally adopted them,” he continued.

It’s been 12 years since Rachel and Siya adopted Liyema and Liphelo. Back in 2024, Rachel reflected on it being 10 years with the brother and sister duo.

“While celebrating Liphelo’s birthday last week, and having all 4 kids home for the weekend, we reflected on the fact that almost to the day, 10 years ago, Liphelo and Liyema came to spend a week with us in Cape Town to see that they were comfortable to make the move and come stay with us forever,” she wrote.



“I was 24 years old Nic was 3 months old, Liphelo had just turned 7 and Liyema 12. 10 years, of the greatest gift God could have ever given me,” she continued.

World.title: Counterfeit goods worth more than R160m seized from Joburg CBD
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Counterfeit and Illicit Goods Unit seized counterfeit goods worth more than R160 million during a multi-disciplinary operation in the Johannesburg CBD this week.

Police spokesperson Colonel Amanda van Wyk said the team, with support from the Public Order Policing (POP) Unit in Pretoria, the South African Revenue Services (SARS) Customs Division, and brand protectors, executed search-and-seizure warrants at several identified shops located in a retail building.

"This resulted in the seizure of more than 62 000 counterfeit items including high-end branded clothing, footwear, cosmetics, watches, jewellery, and sunglasses.

"The operation forms part of ongoing nationwide efforts to dismantle illegal trade, manufacturing, and distribution of counterfeit and illicit goods in the country," she said.

World.title: 'No favours for connected friends' - Zille tells DA rally
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - DA Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille has declared war on corruption.

She has promised an independent investigation into alleged corruption, with public hearings and published findings, and calls for stronger protections for whistleblowers.

Speaking during her campaign for the city, Zille also called for stronger protections for whistleblowers.

"Joburg needs its own Madlanga moment We will initiate an independent investigation into the corruption that has crippled this city, with public hearings and published findings. We will act on the evidence from the Auditor General, from whistleblowers, the Zondo Commission, and others.

"We will rebuild this city's anti-corruption capacity, shield it from political interference, and do whatever is possible to protect whistleblowers.

And we will scrutinize city contracts, starting with the biggest and the most suspicious. We will open up procurement to public scrutiny. Who got the contract? Why? What were they paid? And what did they deliver? No more secret deals. No favours for connected friends. No work, no pay," she said.

World.title: 'Cockroach' party founder released from Indian police custody
World.content:
NEW DELHI - India's Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after his arrest during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.

Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital's central Connaught Place district.

He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw.

"Abhijeet Dipke released," CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media.

Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India's chief election commissioner after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party.

The commission, which oversees voting in the world's most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on October 14 after entering Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody.

Members of Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.

Rights groups and critics however say Modi's government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents -- allegations the government rejects.

World.title: Joburg Crisis Alliance sounds the alarm on city's problems
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Joburg Crisis Alliance warns that Johannesburg cannot afford another five years of poor service delivery and crumbling infrastructure.

The alliance calls for stronger civic structures and greater community participation to hold the incoming city council accountable.

JCA co-convener Neeshan Balton said urgent action is needed to keep the city from sliding deeper into crisis.

The alliance met in Parkview earlier.

"It needs to now move beyond being a crisis alliance to something more formal to do the work that has been outlined here. Because the JCA itself must become a democratic organisation that must bring together people, that must build these civic structures.

"And when we build them, we need to make sure that all the education and advocacy work that we've spoken about here takes place across the length and breadth of the city.

"Because on the 4th, a new government comes into place in Johannesburg. They will be there for five years until 2031. Now, keep that in mind. 2031, we are going to be having these summits, and we will gather here in 2031. And very little would have changed besides having to pay more for very little. I don't think we can afford that. I don't think we can afford for this city to collapse."

World.title: Nepal floods 'defining moment' for climate action: UN
World.content:
KATHMANDU - Nepal's devastating floods should be a turning point for global climate action, with the international community helping the Himalayan nation recover, a top UN official told AFP on Saturday.

The country suffered one of the worst disasters in its history on August 26, when a mountain collapse near the China border triggered catastrophic floods that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.

Scientists said climate change played a significant role in that disaster.

Jorge Moreira da Silva, executive director of the UN Office for Project Services (UNOPS), which implements humanitarian and development projects, said he had witnessed "massive devastation" during a visit to affected communities.

Nepal, a largely rural country of 30 million people that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion.

"This is a defining moment not only for Nepal, this is a defining moment for the international community," Moreira da Silva told AFP in Kathmandu.

"It's not fair to ask a country that emits almost nothing of CO2 to suddenly pay alone the consequence of something that was not generated by the country," he added.

"That's why it's fundamental that global solidarity is brought to this equation."

- 'Climate justice' -

Moreira da Silva said reconstruction and resettlement must account for future climate risks, while the international community must "renew its commitment to climate".

"It's also about climate justice and climate responsibility," he said, warning that low-emitting countries would continue to bear the brunt of climate change.

"This is going to happen unless those countries that emit the most... change their pathway," he said.

Moreira da Silva said Nepal was rebuilding as global disruptions threatened food security. He also leads the UN task force for the Strait of Hormuz.

"The simultaneous disruption of the three maritime shock points... the Strait of Hormuz, in the Black Sea and in the Red Sea, poses a significant challenge, particularly on food security," he said.

The UN and its humanitarian partners launched a $49.6 million appeal last month to provide emergency assistance to flood victims.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations last month that the flooding "was a warning to the world" about the growing dangers of climate change.

By Paavan Mathema

World.title: Albanian capital sees fifth straight day of violent clashes
World.content:
TIRANA - Albania's capital Tirana saw clashes for a fifth straight day Saturday as protesters demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, who pledged to listen to their criticism.

Several hundred people, some masked, gathered around noon in front of the ministry of education, with protests later spreading across the city.

Protesters threw rocks at the police and set litter bins on fire, using them as barricades to prevent the police from advancing.

After police officers had used megaphones to call on those gathered to desist from violence, they used water cannons and tear gas to temporarily disperse the crowd.

Violent demonstrations have rocked Tirana since Tuesday, with thousands of protesters calling for Rama to step down over university conditions and high tuition fees.

At the beginning of the protest demonstrators set a suitcase on fire and threw it in the education ministry courtyard, symbolically showing they do not want to leave Albania.

Journalism student Sinan Billa said the protest was "a reaction to express discontent at the silence of our government."

"Young people have awoken for our parents, too," Billa told AFP.

"We are not asking for privileges. We are demanding our rights, our future and a better country," he said.

While visiting local business damaged in the demonstrations, Rama said he respected the students and added that "their right to protest must and will be protected.

"Their voices, the voices of young people and of every citizen who has taken part in protests today, must and will be heard with respect," Rama said.

However, he added that he "will not allow anyone to jeopardise the future of this country".

Local media reported further protests in the coastal town of Durres, where demonstrators smashed the windows of the post office and blocked roads with burning barricades.

On Friday night police deployed tear gas and water cannons as protesters hurled stones at security forces, burning dustbins to block roads across the city. The clashes continued into the night in several parts of the city.

Police said 10 people were arrested after Friday's demonstrations, with criminal proceedings lodged against a further 22.

The health ministry said 25 people, including nine police officers, sustained minor injuries during clashes in Tirana, Vlora and Lezha on Friday.

This week's escalation of unrest comes after months of anti-government protests in the Balkan nation, initially sparked by a controversial resort development linked to US President Donald Trump's family.

World.title: Jayawardene quits as coach of five-time IPL winners Mumbai
World.content:
MUMBAI - Mahela Jayawardene stepped down as head coach of Mumbai Indians on Saturday to end a nearly decade-long association with one of the Indian Premier League's most successful teams.

The 49-year-old former Sri Lanka captain led Mumbai to three titles in his first stint between 2017 and 2022.

He rejoined the team in 2024 but was unable to replicate his success as five-time IPL winners Mumbai finished fourth in 2025 and ninth out of 10 teams in 2026.

"Together we have shared some unforgettable moments, overcome challenges and built something we can all be proud of," Jayawardene said in a statement.

"I leave with immense pride in what we have achieved together and will always carry a special place in my heart for MI.

"I wish the team every success in the years ahead."

Jayawardene represented Sri Lanka in 149 Tests, 448 one-day internationals and 55 T20 matches between 1997 and 2015.

World.title: Leaders weigh 'huge benefit', risks of AI for global economy
World.content:
BANGKOK - The artificial intelligence boom has been a key driver of global growth, but also poses economic risks should investment in the technology falter, experts and policymakers said this week at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

Propelled by spending on data centres and microchips, AI has helped cushion the economic shock of rising global energy prices caused by war in the Middle East, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in a report on Tuesday.

The fund's chief economist Silvana Tenreyro noted this week that global trade rose 8.3 percent between 2023 and 2025, a figure she said would be closer to 4.6 percent without AI-related products.

"It is everywhere in the global economy," Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said of AI on Friday.

"You see it in GDP. You see it in the stock market. You see it in the bond market... So it is here, and it's just the beginning."

But some top officials gathered in Bangkok this week cautioned against relying too heavily on AI investment.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh called AI the "most consequential change" to the global economy in his lifetime, and said it had "a huge benefit". Still, he warned the road ahead would be "bumpy".

"The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don't know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies," he said.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva similarly noted the AI boom's boost to global growth, but she told AFP that any slowdown in the industry "would be felt across the world".

"If there is loss of confidence and money runs away from AI, that can lead to financial stability risks," Georgieva said.

An IMF report released this week projected that a decline in AI investment could reduce global GDP by 0.4 percent by 2028.

"Weaker or less durable AI investments and profitability could be a shock that triggers a market correction," the report said.

- War and regulation -

While AI investment and trade have softened the global economic impact of the Middle East war, economists at Moody's Analytics have warned that if the conflict drags on it could "puncture" the boom.

They said higher energy prices and tighter financial conditions could push up operating costs and interest rates, adding to doubts over "the long-term profitability and viability of AI business models".

"A drawn-out conflict would put serious strain on the economics behind AI investment," the group said.

The uncertainty around regulation has also clouded the technology's outlook.

Leaders like US President Donald Trump have urged more limited government regulation, even as some in the industry have called for legislation to mitigate risks.

Georgieva, the IMF chief, appeared on Friday to link such regulation to future investment.

"If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities," she said in Bangkok.

By Asad Hashim

World.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, total rises to seven
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health CS Aden Duale. [Edward Kiplimo, Standard]

Kenya has confirmed four new Ebola cases, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, including the first patient who died.

The Ministry of Health said the new cases involve a close male relative of the deceased patient and three health workers who treated him in hospital.

All four developed fever as their first symptom and were immediately isolated before staff collected samples for testing.

The samples tested positive at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) laboratory.

“The patients are currently receiving supportive care from our trained health workers,” the ministry said in a statement.

The male relative had been in quarantine since October 6, while the three health workers, two men and one woman, had been in quarantine since October 9.

The health workers attended to the first patient at the hospital between October 3 and 4. They are currently receiving supportive care at a designated treatment facility.

The ministry said it detected the four cases while the individuals were in quarantine, allowing early diagnosis and reducing the risk of further transmission to their families and the wider community.

“The Ministry wishes to reassure Kenyans that the risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission of the disease,” the statement said, adding that the second and third patients were stable and responding well to treatment.

So far, the authorities say 128 of the 130 identified contacts have been traced, with efforts ongoing to locate the remaining two.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: From 'Chogo' to senator? Winnie Odinga steps into her own political spotlight
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

From Raila Odinga’s shadow to her own political path, Winnie sets her sights on the Nairobi Senate seat in 2027. [Courtesy]

The hat was more than a hat. Literally.

As Raila Odinga’s body made its final journey home from India, his youngest daughter, Winnie, held tightly to his familiar cream-coloured fedora. It was one of the few things she could still protect, a small piece of a man whose presence had filled her life and Kenya’s political imagination for decades.

The image of Winnie carrying her father’s hat was deeply personal. The country was mourning a political giant, but she was mourning her father.

A year later, on the first anniversary of Raila’s death, Winnie has announced her intention to contest the Nairobi Senate seat in the 2027 General Election.

The timing is poignant. On a day devoted to remembering her father, she has declared her own political ambitions, signalling a shift from being one of the most recognisable faces of the Odinga family to a politician seeking a mandate in her own right.

“As Edwin Sifuna seeks a higher office, I see an opportunity in Nairobi, which is why I have decided I will vie for Senator of Nairobi County,” she said.

And just like that, the conversation shifted from the daughter who carried Baba’s hat to the politician who wants a seat of her own.

The last-born girl

To many Kenyans, Winnie is Chogo, the last-born child of Raila and Ida Odinga. The nickname carries the familiarity of family life, a reminder that behind the powerful surname is a daughter who grew up in a household where politics was never far from the conversation.

Her father was no ordinary political figure. His name could summon crowds, ignite debate and divide opinion. His decades-long career placed the Odinga family at the centre of Kenya’s political story.

Growing up as Raila’s youngest daughter meant sharing him with a country that claimed a piece of his time, energy and, eventually, his final goodbye.

Yet Winnie was not simply a spectator in her father’s political world. She worked around his campaigns and communications before stepping into politics herself, eventually winning a seat in the East African Legislative Assembly.

In November 2022, Parliament elected her to represent Kenya in the regional legislature, where she took office in December that year. Based in Arusha, Tanzania, she became part of the East African Community’s legislative institution, serving a five-year term running to 2027.

The EALA offered Winnie a political platform beyond her father’s immediate circle and an opportunity to participate in regional affairs. Her current tenure has also given her experience in legislative politics before her proposed move into elective politics at home.

The Nairobi Senate bid would take her into a different contest, one in which voters will have to decide whether her experience, ideas and political programme merit their support.

The hat she could not let go

For years, Raila’s trademark headgear had been part of his public identity, appearing at political rallies, meetings and public ceremonies. But in Winnie’s hands, it became something else: a personal possession tied to the final journey of a daughter and her father

She explained how protective she had been of it throughout the journey, describing it as one of the few things she could still hold on to.

The image captured a kind of helplessness that public figures’ families rarely get to show. Crowds could mourn Raila, politicians could speak of his legacy, and supporters could debate who would inherit his political movement. Winnie, however, had been left with the painful task of bringing her father home.

The symbolism of the hat has since acquired another layer. At a ceremony in Bondo earlier this month, elders placed a traditional hat on Winnie’s head in a symbolic gesture associated with the possibility of her carrying forward her father’s political mantle.

Winnie’s political journey has not started with this Senate announcement.

Her election to the East African Legislative Assembly placed her among Kenya’s representatives in a regional institution whose work concerns cooperation among East African Community partner states.

The role gave her a platform in regional legislation while her father remained a central figure in national politics.

The Senate is responsible for representing counties, participating in lawmaking on matters concerning counties and exercising oversight over revenue allocated to county governments. A Nairobi senator must therefore make a case on issues that touch residents directly, from public spending and service delivery to the accountability of county leadership.

The capital is also a demanding political terrain. Its electorate is diverse, its concerns immediate and its contests fiercely competitive.

A famous surname may open doors, but it cannot replace a convincing programme on jobs, housing, transport, healthcare and the management of public resources.

Winnie will have to demonstrate that she understands Nairobi beyond its place in her father’s national political story.

Can she translate the loyalty associated with Raila into support for her own agenda? Can she persuade voters that she is more than the daughter of a political icon?

Those questions will follow her into the campaign.

The Odingaism

Political inheritance can be both an advantage and a burden.

Raila’s name carries a formidable history of opposition politics, democratic reform and a loyal support base. It also invites comparisons that few politicians have to contend with.

Winnie’s challenge will be to honour that history without allowing it to become the entirety of her political identity.

Raila’s death left a space in the Orange Democratic Movement and among supporters who had looked to him for direction through decades of political contests. The question of who will carry his legacy has inevitably turned towards his family and the wider political movement he helped build.

Winnie’s Senate bid will require her to turn recognition into a political proposition that voters can interrogate. Her experience at EALA gives her a legislative starting point; the Nairobi contest will demand that she demonstrate how that experience can serve residents of the capital.

She must also navigate the expectations attached to her father’s name while making room for her own ideas, priorities and leadership style.

There is a temptation to see Winnie’s future entirely through the lens of inheritance. She is Raila’s daughter, the last-born known as Chogo, the woman who carried his hat and the politician whom some supporters hope will continue his legacy.

But she is also a woman making a decision about her own future.

The Senate bid offers her an opportunity to define what that future means, beyond the grief surrounding her father’s death and the weight of a name that has shaped Kenyan politics for decades.

The hat remains an unforgettable image from Raila’s final journey home. A daughter attempted to protect the last tangible thing she could hold on to.

The Senate will demand something different: a political vision, a campaign and the votes of Nairobi residents.

Chogo has announced her next move. Will Winnie Odinga turn the memory of Baba into a mandate of her own?

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
