Census 2027: Congress alleges RSS-BJP agenda behind rule changes

Congress defends âregime changeâ remark, says governments must be replaced through elections

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was granted bail on Saturday, within 24 hours of being placed in preventive custody, subject to certain conditions. Delhi Police told news agency ANI that he would be released after signing a peace bond. Dipke was detained shortly after leaving the residence of NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande to attend a âTiranga Yatraâ at Delhiâs Connaught Place, where prohibitory orders under Section 163 were in force.Air India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of flights to Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until October 24 because of heightened security concerns linked to Houthi attacks. Eligible passengers can opt for a one-time free date change or rebook from certain alternative Gulf destinations, subject to airline conditions and availability. The disruptions follow the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which took the death toll to 13 after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national injured in the incident had died.Clashes between the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) broke out at several nomination centres in Andhra Pradeshâs Kadapa district on Saturday, the second day of the nomination process.Violence was reported in Pulivendula, the home constituency of former chief minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, where police fired six rounds in the air and resorted to a lathi-charge to disperse the crowd. Stone-pelting was also reported at other locations.The Congress has accused the BJP-led Centre of pursuing a political agenda following amendments to the Census Rules, 1990, which expanded the pool of people eligible for census duties to include teachers from aided and unaided private institutions. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh raised concerns over the changes, citing alleged links to an RSS training camp and a panel on demographic changes. He described the expansion as a âRozgar Guarantee Yojana for thousands of RSS/BJP workersâ and claimed it could further undermine the credibility of the census process.Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram has defended the phrase âregime changeâ amid a political row over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He said the Oppositionâs duty was to âoppose, expose and deposeâ the government, clarifying that this meant opposing it politically, scrutinising it in Parliament and seeking its removal through elections, as the BJP accused the Opposition of seeking to destabilise the government.

World.title: 'An evening in Paris': Opposition questions 'nature' of Punjab CM Mann's France visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's visit to Paris has drawn sharp criticism from opposition leaders, with the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal questioning the purpose of his trip while raising concerns over drug abuse and law and order in Punjab.

The backlash comes as the state government faces scrutiny over recent killings linked to the state's drug menace, with the Union home ministry seeking reports on the cases.

BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.

BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.

""Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed... 23 police stations have been targeted in grenade attacks, and even police personnel feel unsafe while in uniform. At a time when all of Punjab is engulfed in a raging crisis, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has chosen to travel to France with his wife to celebrate his birthday. This is a deeply distressing situation," Chugh said on Saturday.





Questioning the nature of the visit, the BJP leader alleged, "If this is an official state visit, how is his wife accompanying him? In reality, a birthday party is being hosted in France under the guise of an official state visit."

Chugh also targeted the AAP government over the drug menace and security concerns, claiming that people opposing drug abuse were being killed and citing grenade attacks on police stations.

"Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed," he said, alleging that even police personnel felt unsafe.

The chief minister also faced criticism from Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia, who alleged that Mann had attended a police meeting in Phillaur on October 16 while under the influence of alcohol. The allegation has not been independently verified.

Referring to Mann's birthday and his trip to Paris, Majithia said, "Today is his birthday.

I even tweeted today about 'An Evening in Paris', which is a famous Hindi song, 'Rang-rangiliyan manane gaye hain'."

Majithia questioned the chief minister's handling of the drug issue, alleging that Mann had attended a meeting on the menace while intoxicated.

"Holding a meeting against drugs while being drunk as the Chief Minister, what on earth is happening?" he said.

Separately, Congress leader Sachin Pilot criticised the Punjab government's handling of law and order, alleging that killings, extortion, ransom demands and encounters had become common in the state.

Speaking during a visit to Moga district on Saturday, Pilot called for accountability and faster legal action in murder cases. He also referred to a family that, he alleged, had been waiting for justice and assistance three years after the death of a young man's father.

The opposition attacks come amid continuing criticism of the AAP government over drug abuse, gang violence and security in Punjab. The allegations against Mann and his government form part of the opposition's broader challenge to the state's handling of law and order.

World.title: Over 20 students of Kozhikode college suspended after group clash over social media post
World.content:
Over 20 students have been suspended from MET College of Arts and Science, an unaided college affiliated with the University of Calicut, at Nadapuram in Kozhikode, Keralam, following a clash between two groups over a social media post.

According to college authorities, 16 of those suspended are third-year undergraduate students and six others are in their first year.

The dispute between the two groups reportedly began on Friday over a social media post. Following this, one of the junior students was allegedly beaten up by seniors on the road leading to the college on Monday, the police said. The incident soon developed into a clash between the two groups as more students joined in. Visuals of the fight were also shared in social media groups, and many parents reached the area.

However, the police’s initial attempts to bring the situation under control failed, and additional personnel had to be called in. Though the injured students were admitted to nearby hospitals, some of them clashed there as well. The police subsequently took some students into custody and registered cases against six of them.

Meanwhile, cases were registered against at least 10 other students after another clash was reported at Thooneri in the same area.

World.title: ‘Run for Her’ brings runners together for gender equality
World.content:
More than 100 runners joined German endurance runner Alicia Bayer for a 5-km community run at KBR Park, promoting gender equality, women’s empowerment and inclusivity in sport.

‘Run for Her’ initiative is a mixed-gender initiative that encourages men and women to stand together for equality, challenge stereotypes and make public spaces more welcoming for women.

Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Alicia said she is very happy to see the good turnout of runners early in the morning.

Participants highlighted the need for more women’s running groups and opportunities for women to run with confidence and feel a sense of belonging.

Ms. Alicia uses endurance challenges to raise awareness of social causes. In 2026, she ran approximately 640 km from Mumbai to Goa to promote women’s empowerment and girls’ education. Her other challenges in Nepal supported awareness of human trafficking and menstrual health.

The event in Hyderabad also highlighted HERD, Ms. Alicia’s women-only running community, which offers women a space to find running partners, exchange experiences and build confidence.

Already active in Delhi, Singapore and Hyderabad, HERD plans to expand to Bengaluru, Mysuru, Goa and Mumbai, with a long-term vision of connecting women runners worldwide.

World.title: Railway Workshop opens infrastructure and Sculpture Park to the public
World.content:
The Golden Rock Railway Workshop at Ponmalai on Saturday opened its gate for the general public to enable them to have a look at its infrastructure and take part in Ayudha puja celebrations.

The railway administration made arrangements for the visitors to have a safe and pleasant time at the premier workshop of the Indian Railways.

Established during the colonial era in 1928 at Golden Rock, the workshop is involved in a myriad of activities such as overhaul of diesel locomotives, maintenance of coaches, MEMU rakes and wagons besides carrying out maintenance of Vande Bharat express trains and steam locomotives operating in the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

The main attraction for the visitors inside the sprawling premises was the Sculpture Park situated near the West Gate. The park contained fabricated models made from scrap generated in various shops functioning inside the workshop. The park now has 23 sculptures made of discarded engineering materials such as a vintage car, bike, jeep, aircraft, missile, rocket, landmarks such as Eiffel Tower, Leaning Tower of Pisa and sculptures with social messages such as ‘Save Earth’ and ‘Break the Shackle’.

The multi-view anamorphic sculpture of former President A.P.J Abdul Kalam and Mahatma Gandhi near the West Gate was also a special attraction for the visitors.

Exhibits of old photographs and models at the Workshop Training Centre were viewed with keen interest by the visitors. The visitors of all ages saw the exhibits with great enthusiasm, a press release from the workshop said.

World.title: Lord Malayappa Swamy rides Hanumantha Vahanam at Tirumala’s Brahmotsavams
World.content:
Lord Malayappa Swamy, the processional deity of Lord Venkateswara, appeared as Kodanda Rama on the Hanuman Vahanam on Saturday morning (October 17, 2026), marking the sixth day of the Navaratri Brahmotsavams at Tirumala.

Holding a bow and arrow, the deity rode Lord Hanuman—the ardent devotee of Lord Rama, through the Mada Streets, drawing devotees who offered camphor harati amid chanting of Govinda namams. Traditional Kolatam, wooden-stick dances and devotional music added to the festive atmosphere.

The Hanumantha vahanam symbolises unwavering devotion and selfless service, recalling the sacred bond between Lord Rama and Hanuman. The procession was among the highlights of the day’s religious celebrations.

Adding a cultural dimension to the festivities, 516 artistes representing 25 troupes from 14 States presented traditional dances, folk performances, and musical renditions along the procession route, showcasing India’s diverse artistic heritage.

The evening was dotted with the procession of “Pushpaka Vimanam” wherein, Lord Malayappa accompanied by his two divine consorts Sridevi and Bhudevi, appeared as Govardhanagiridhari Sri Krishna on the specially crafted Pushpaka Vimanam.

Made primarily of coconut palm leaves and adorned with traditional flowers, the structure measured 24 feet in height and 15 feet each in length and width, weighing approximately one tonne. It featured figures of Sri Anjaneya and Garuda along with representations of deities associated with the four yugas.

Eminent florists from Tamil Nadu and personnel of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam (TTD) Garden Department toiled for more than a week in crafting and designing the floral palanquin. Chennai-based donor Ramprasad Bhatt had lent his support and expertise in its preparation. The day came to a close with the procession of Gaja vahanam in the night.

World.title: Indian student groups in London protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, SIR; Govt supporters hold counter-protest
World.content:
Hundreds gathered at Mahatma Gandhi’s statue at Parliament Square in London on Saturday (October 17, 2026) for a protest organised by the Opposition Congress and UK-based Indian students’ groups against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

While the “Stop Vote Chori” protest cheered for activist Dhruv Rathee as the keynote speaker, chants of “Modi, Modi” rang out from a smaller group across the Gandhi statue, being kept apart by Metropolitan Police officers.

The face-off between the groups got heated as each tried to drown out the other’s chants.

“We don’t want any foreign interference. I am here at Parliament Square to address Indians and NRIs,” said Mr. Rathee, addressing the gathering in Hindi.

“It is important to spread the message against ‘vote chori’ in our country. These protests will stop the moment the Chief Election Commissioner is replaced by a candidate that is chosen in agreement between the government and Leader of the Opposition,” he said.

His address followed slogans of “Inquilab Zindabad”, “Vande Mataram” and the reading of the preamble of the Constitution of India.

The protest was organised by the Indian Overseas Congress Youth wing and supported by several diaspora platforms including Save Democracy, Students’ Federation of India (SFI) U.K. and South Asia Solidarity Group among others.

Meanwhile, India Diaspora (ID) U.K. had issued an “Urgent appeal to all London Bharat Premi Janta” to gather in counter-protest.

ID U.K. founder Hirdesh Gupta said: “The Indian diaspora in the U.K. stands firmly, shoulder to shoulder, with Modi Ji and his government in their vision of a strong, united and developed India.”

The big turnout followed a smaller protest and counter-protest gathering outside the High Commission of India in London on Friday (October 16, 2026).

The demonstration on Saturday (October 17, 2026) is among a series since an “Emergency Protest” on Tuesday, called to “amplify” the demands of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) — including the demand for the removal of Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of the SIR of electoral rolls in India.

The Election Commission maintains that the exercise is intended to update electoral rolls by identifying deceased, duplicate, shifted and otherwise ineligible entries.

World.title: Transfer of 30.63 lakh farm electricity connections to Rythu Discom is conspiracy to end 24x7 free power, alleges Harish Rao
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Deputy Leader of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) Legislature Party and former minister T. Harish Rao has accused the Congress Government in Telangana of conspiring to discontinue 24x7 free power supply to agricultural pump-sets by handing over all farm-related power connections to the new Discom — Rythu Power Distribution Company of Telangana Ltd (TGRPDCL), despite serious objections raised by power sector experts, farmers, social scientists, employees and political parties.

Opposes G.O.17 on transfer of 30.63 lakh farm-related power connections

Opposing the G.O. 17 issued by the State Government on Monday (October 12, 2026) to transfer all farm-related power connections (30,62,853) — agricultural pump-sets (30,60,821), lift irrigation schemes (512), Hyderabad Metro Water Supply (105), CPWS/Mission Bhagiratha (1,145) and water connections with separate DTRs (270) — Mr. Rao said on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that it was an indication of government’s dictatorial attitude against the farming community.

He demanded that the G.O. be withdrawn immediately. Instead of explaining to people as to how the Rythu Discom would benefit farmers and ensure quality power supply, the government was acting adamantly and going ahead with the new Discom.

Power sources for Discoms in Telangana

He sought to know if 2,000 staff of the Rythu Discom would handle supervision and the management of a distribution network with nearly 30.63 lakh connections, that too by allocating only 25% of thermal power procured by the Discoms to the third Discom. The Rythu Discom would have 6,15,651 agriculture transformers (DTRs) and 2.5 lakh circuit km of LT lines. The Discoms were sourcing 53.28% energy needed from the thermal power sector and the share of solar power was only 35.31%.

Solar power only during day, hydel only for 3-4 months

Mr. Rao stated that the Rythu Discom was allocated 25% thermal, 58% solar and 17% hydel from out of the energy allocation made to all Discoms. The 58% allocation (solar) made to Rythu Discom would be available only during the day hours as solar power generation was not possible during the nights. It would allow power supply to farm connections only during day time and the hydel power (2,325 MW) generated mostly for 3-4 months a year at full-scale was also entirely allocated to the Rythu Discom.

Loans to make financial stability of new Discom uncertain from day one

Huge loans and dues are also being transferred to the new Discom , making its financial stability uncertain from day one and leaving the possibility of farm connections getting assured power supply uncertain, he claimed and demanded that the government give an assurance about 24x7 quality free power supply to the farm sector.

World.title: Leopard trapped at Akathethara
World.content:
The Keralam Forest department on Saturday trapped a four-year-old female leopard that had been spotted repeatedly near homes at Maithri Nagar, Cherad, in Akathethara panchayat. The leopard was caught in a cage set up near the residential area, following complaints from residents about its presence and the loss of pet dogs. It was shifted to the wildlife health centre at Dhoni for examination and monitoring.

A forest veterinary team examined the leopard. Forest officials said it would remain under veterinary care while its health and behaviour were monitored. Residents of Maithri Nagar, in Ward 3 of Akathethara panchayat, had approached the panchayat seeking action to address the threat. Street lights were installed in the area, and the Forest department was asked to intervene.

World.title: Musk has spent $276 million on midterms to help Republicans retain control of Congress
World.content:
Elon Musk has spent roughly $366 million ​in the 2026 U.S. midterm election cycle so far, $276 million of it since July ‌to help Republicans retain control of Congress, even as Democrats’ chances ​of retaking the U.S. House and Senate have improved.

Mr. Musk’s largesse, ⁠which was reported earlier by the New York Times, makes the world’s richest person likely the single-biggest political donor in this year’s races, according to campaign finance records.

There is ‌a lot at stake for Mr. Musk with Democrats in the U.S. House of Representatives calling for investigations into his government contracts as ‌CEO of aerospace company SpaceX, as well as his work running the ‌Department ⁠of Government Efficiency under President Donald Trump.

A breakdown ⁠of his political spending, which was confirmed by a spokesman for his super PAC America PAC:

Mr. Musk has spent $366 million so far this election cycle, which began January 1, 2025. At ​least $276 million so far has ‌gone to Republican groups and his own super PAC since July. Of the $276 million in third-quarter donations:

$158 million went to the Senate Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up to help elect Republicans to the Senate ‌that is aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican from South ​Dakota.

$20 million went to the Congressional Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up for House Republicans that is aligned with House ⁠Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican.

$76 million went to Musk’s America PAC. $10 million went to the Lone Star Liberty PAC, which is supporting Republican state ‌Attorney General Ken Paxton’s run for the U.S. Senate in Texas, where recent polls have him in a dead heat against Democrat James Talarico.

$10 million went to the Republican Governors Association. $2 million went to the Republican Attorneys General Association.

America PAC is helping Republican candidates in seven battleground states and nearly three dozen House races. The new giving will be publicly disclosed ‌when many super PACs are required to disclose their third-quarter spending on Thursday (October 15, 2026).

Mr. Musk has ​also donated more money through groups that do not disclose their donors, according to the New York Times report.

Roughly $90 million spent ⁠this cycle paid for work done in the prior election or supported other ⁠issues, including an unsuccessful candidate for the Wisconsin Supreme Court and a controversial program paying $1 million to registered voters who signed a petition supporting ‌free speech and gun rights, according to an America PAC spokesman.

Mr. Musk spent roughly $290 million during the last election cycle in which Mr. Trump won ​the presidential election race against former Vice President Kamala Harris.

World.title: Fazl clarifies he criticised policies, not institutions after ministers allege he sought 'share' in KP governance
World.content:
Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday clarified that his party’s remarks regarding the country’s security situation were directed at policies, not institutions, and termed the allegations levelled against him by federal ministers as character assassination.

A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, without naming anyone, had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The remarks came after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights and raised doubts over its reasoning behind imposing governor’s rule that there was a lack of cooperation on counterterrorism.

Earlier on Saturday, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also rebuked the JUI-F chief for reportedly seeking his “share” in KP’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province. Other federal ministers have also taken exception to Fazl’s remarks.

Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Saturday, Fazl stressed that his party’s criticism was directed at policies, not institutions, and was intended to bring about corrective action rather than undermine the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism.

The senior politician called for an in-camera session of Parliament to review the country’s security situation and formulate a consensus-based policy to combat terrorism.

“Our only question is why the country has failed to eliminate terrorism. Let us sit together and find out why. Parliament is the most appropriate forum to discuss the issue and make decisions. Instead of ridiculing politicians, the government should take them on board in this fight so that we can move forward together,” he said.

“If Parliament is supreme, why are decisions taken in Rawalpindi while Parliament is simply told to follow them?” he remarked. “The issue is that this government is powerless. Decisions are taken somewhere else, and it implements them obediently,” he alleged.

The JUI-F maintained that Parliament should review the security situation and that the nation should be taken into confidence. If the public was expected to support the fight against terrorism and those engaged in it, he argued, the government should explain its decisions rather than impose “unilateral measures”.

Fazl reiterated his objection to the imposition of emergency rule in KP or any other part of the country. Recalling his family’s opposition to emergency rule in Balochistan during the 1970s, he said his father had resigned when the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto imposed it in the province.

He described the recurrence of such measures as unfortunate, pointing out that the PP had repeatedly been associated with their imposition.

Questioning the rationale behind the emergency, governor’s rule and deployment of troops in KP, Fazl asked why the province should face such treatment when Balochistan was also grappling with the same level of terrorist violence, if not more.

The JUI-F chief urged the government to develop a shared national narrative and a consensus-based counterterrorism strategy instead of questioning his party’s position.

He went on to ask why the government engaged in negotiations with the PTI, which had been in power in KP, if the party was accused of supporting terrorists. “On top of it, both (the PTI and the government) say that they had reached a consensus on all points.”

Fazl then highlighted that around 250 of his party workers had lost their lives in terrorist violence, arguing that their sacrifices should not be ridiculed or overlooked. “How can a party whose members have laid their lives be accused of supporting terrorists?” he asked.

He also questioned why he was being singled out for criticism when political leaders, including former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, had at various times disagreed with the military leadership.

Ministers assail Fazl

Earlier on Saturday, addressing the media in Jaranwala, Chaudhry said, “I am upset. We did not expect Maulana sahab […] to consider this as spoils of war and seek his share in the absence of a PTI government in the province.”

He emphasised that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was not a political move aimed at strengthening the PML-N’s presence in the province by dismissing the PTI-led government.

“This was an administrative setup,” he said, adding that it had been formed with a “one-point agenda: combating terrorism”, rather than with an intention of establishing a political setup.

“This is not spoils of war,” he reiterated, adding that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was an “immensely responsible” decision taken after every other option had been considered.

“I am unable to understand why Maulana sahab says that he was forced to accept defeat [in elections],” he said, arguing that Fazl’s party had been defeated by the PTI in KP and the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party in Balochistan.

Chaudhry said the JUI-F was worthy of respect only if it stood by Pakistan’s interests.

The state minister also rejected the impression that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule was aimed at taking control of KP’s natural resources.

He also criticised Fazl for bringing up the 1971 separation of East Pakistan — now Bangladesh — from Pakistan in his recent statements.

“You bring up 1971 after losing the 2024 elections,” Chaudhry said.

“This KP setup is not about distributing shares, forming coalitions and governments, or engaging in politics,” he stressed, clarifying that only one member of the KP Advisory Council has a political background, as she represents the families of martyrs.

Chaudhry again offered to implement the National Action Plan and combat terrorism jointly with all stakeholders. “Politics is possible only where there is peace,” he said.

At the outset of his address, Chaudhry alleged that there must be “a relationship or a mutual interest arrangement between the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the PTI”.

“Since 2015, no PTI leader, gathering or member has been targeted by terrorists,” Chaudhry said. “On the other hand, over the past 11 years, no political or religious party, security force, public office, funeral or wedding has been spared terrorist attacks.”

He said the federal government had exhausted all avenues to bring together stakeholders and urge them to condemn terrorism by naming those involved, whether the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), or groups funded by India or Afghanistan.

The state minister claimed that in 2013, when the government decided to hold talks with the TTP and representatives were proposed by both sides, the TTP had nominated PTI founder Imran Khan to its committee.

He also alleged that the PTI founder had allowed the TTP to open offices in Peshawar.

During his address, Chaudhry also criticised the PTI, showing a press release issued by the TTP that condemned the dismissal of the party’s government.

Meanwhile, speaking at a press conference in Sialkot, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif criticised the JUI-F chief for constantly “targeting” the country’s security forces.

He declared that the sacrifices made by the security forces, officers, and the public in the fight against terrorism were “matchless”.

The defence minister referred to Fazl’s accusations that the emergency and governor’s rule were imposed to capture KP’s mineral resources, saying that he had shared a full list of people who had the mining contracts in KP.

Asif maintained that the whole PTI and opposition leadership was engaged by the government before the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule.

“But it was fruitless,” he said.

“The situation will improve in KP […] parliament can roll back the decision of imposing the emergency only if the improvement of the situation in the province is guaranteed,” the defence minister said.

He said that some individuals in KP were expecting to get a share in the administrative changes in the province.

“We will ensure free and fair elections. Whenever the time comes, everybody can take part in it,” he said.

Fazl’s remarks also prompted a response from KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, who has now been tasked with running the province under governor’s rule.

Kundi, referring to the JUI-F chief, asked whether “your land in the land belonging to martyrs in DI Khan is halal”.

“What you get is halal, what the other gets is haram,” he remarked.

The governor reaffirmed that the new KP administration would continue to function properly.

Fazl, who was involved in reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government, has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. He also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the two parties.

Addressing a rally in Multan on Thursday, Fazl further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into KP after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018.

“We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger.

He alleged governor’s rule was not imposed in Balochistan because the province’s chief minister “praises you”.

The next day, during an interaction with journalists, the interior minister said, “The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship.”

This politician, Naqvi alleged, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”.

“These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged.

He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced.

The same day, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also railed against Fazl in a post on X.

She said it was not expected of a senior politician such as him to support those who facilitate terrorism — an apparent reference to the PTI, which the Centre accuses of backing terrorism.

She also criticised Fazl for his remarks about Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, seemingly referring to his comments during the Multan address about the centralisation of power.

The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan.

In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations.

World.title: Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP, PM reiterates
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday reiterated that the Centre was “compelled” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to the provincial government’s lack of cooperation in countering terrorism.

The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament this week amid protests by the opposition.

On Saturday, PM Shehbaz visited the residence of Rashid Bashir Virk in Gujranwala to offer condolences on the demise of his father, late MNA Mahmood Bashir Virk.

After recalling the late PML-N lawmaker’s services, the premier stressed that the Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP.

He said the Centre made a “last attempt”, referring to the rounds of talks held by a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition.

The hours-long second round, held on Oct 3, had ended without a breakthrough.

“They had talks with them (PTI) day and night, for 48 hours, and sat with the intention to settle matters from every aspect,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that a draft was ready under which the PTI was to call off its long march.

The prime minister highlighted that he had held multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional, as well as with his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur.

“In every meeting, I tried my best to convey to him from the depths of my heart and with seriousness that KP is an extremely beautiful province and has very brave and honourable people, […] and I am always present in every way for their development and prosperity,” PM Shehbaz said.

The premier added that he assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in fighting against terrorism together to face the security challenges in the province.

PM Shehbaz said he had assured the chief minister that he would make the decisions regarding the administration, resources and necessities in consultation with him.

“But, unfortunately, despite all these efforts, thousands of our law enforcement agencies personnel, soldiers, officers and officers of the armed forces were sacrificing their lives every day to defend the homeland.”

The prime minister stressed that the federal government “made many efforts” regarding the situation, but there were “threats and long marches every other day in response”.

“Their past history is very horrific,” he remarked, recalling the 2014 sit-ins staged by the PTI at Islamabad’s D-Chowk during the tenure of his brother, Nawaz Sharif.

“Last year as well, you saw how the entire country was jammed by staging a sit-in in Islamabad,” he added, ostensibly referring to the PTI’s November 2024 protest that had resulted in clashes.

“This time as well, they had an entire plan of bloodshed,” he alleged.

The Oct 11 imposition of emergency and governor’s rule followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups and asserted that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their October 3 talks .

World.title: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week.

“We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.

Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh has not responded to Iran’s overture.

On Friday, Iran denied having anything to do with the Houthi attacks, after Saudi Arabia accused Tehran of encouraging the group’s escalation.

In his speech, Araghchi also said “either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Tehran was willing “to cooperate with all its brothers and neighbours to achieve the first option”.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

On Wednesday, Yemen’s Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in Riyadh housing the energy giant’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions also rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations.

Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s eastern province and Riyadh.

Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. Later, a Saudi energy ministry official confirmed the attack. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said that four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

World.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody
World.content:
India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after he was detained during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.

Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital’s central Connaught Place district. He was arrested to prevent a breach of the peace, broadcasters NDTV and ​India Today reported.

He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw.

“Abhijeet Dipke released,” CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media.

Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

More than 130 million voters were deleted ​during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Student activist Neha ​Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she ​tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released earlier on Saturday as well.

“Please, spare the people of India. ‌Impeach ⁠Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured,” Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on Oct 14 after entering Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

Rights groups and critics, however, say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents — allegations the government rejects.

A weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the movement earlier this year forced then-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over ​exam paper leaks.

World.title: Islamabad ATC summons Islamabad police chief in security breach case against Imaan and Hadi
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday summoned the Islamabad police chief and issued show-cause notices to two police officials over the continued failure to produce the case record in the security breach case against lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case pertains to the alleged disruption of a security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. Imaan and her husband were accused of removing barriers from the route. The couple was indicted in the case on Oct 7.

During Saturday’s hearing, ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain directed the two police officials to whom notices were issued to explain their failure to ensure the production of the record. He warned that they could face imprisonment if it was not presented before the court.

During the proceedings, the court expressed displeasure over the continued absence of the investigating officer and raised questions about the whereabouts of the case record.

A court official informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Gilgit-Baltistan and had not returned.

The judge immediately summoned the superintendent (investigation) to explain the situation.

Advocate Riasat Ali Azad, representing the accused, told the court that the bail application had been filed on October 29 last year and notices had already been issued, but the proceedings could not move forward because the investigating officer failed to appear with the record.

He argued that in similar cases, another police official usually appeared with the case record when the investigating officer was unavailable. Questioning how long the court was expected to wait, Azad urged the judge to make a decision in accordance with the law.

Advocate Asif Irfan, vice chairman of the Islamabad Bar Council, observed that the court was not powerless, but had so far been unable to ensure the production of the record.

Advocate Aleem Abbasi, meanwhile, urged the judge to exercise his authority and decide the matter on merit. He added that the legal fraternity stood with the judiciary in defending its independence, but questioned how lawyers could secure justice for their own children if the judicial system failed to deliver it.

Advocate Zafar Khokhar also questioned under which law an investigating officer could take the case record away and leave court proceedings stalled.

Judge Zulqarnain, however, expressed displeasure over the tone adopted by some lawyers, deeming such conduct inappropriate and remarking that he was not influenced by vlogs or commentary and always conducted proceedings impartially.

After a short break in the proceedings, SP Khurram Ashraf and Deputy Superintendent (DSP) Naeem Yousuf appeared before the court.

The SP informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Khaplu and would appear after he returned. The judge questioned the arrangement and asked when the officer would return, observing that everyone was waiting while the court had a case to decide.

When pressed for a definite timeline, DSP Yousuf said the investigating officer could take another 10 to 15 days to return.

The judge criticised the police for causing prolonged hardship to PTI workers through delays in their cases.

Expressing frustration over the situation and the alleged harassment of workers, the judge ordered the discharge of several individuals arrested in connection with the PTI’s long march.

The court subsequently issued show-cause notices to the SP and DSP, warning that failure to produce the case record could lead to proceedings for their imprisonment.

Islamabad Inspector General of Police Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry was also summoned for the next hearing on November 3.

The case

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

They were indicted in the case on Oct 7 and the ATC on Oct 10 disposed of the couple’s petition seeking to drop the terrorism charges.

On Oct 15, the court directed lawyers and witnesses in the case to appear at Adiala jail for the next hearing after police cited difficulties in transporting the couple to court.

At yesterday’s hearing, Imaan and Hadi had objected to the manner in which they were presented during the hearing of the case, with the couple and their lawyers eventually walking out of the proceedings at Adiala jail.

World.title: Shaheen Afridi wants unity to be Pakistan's identity under his leadership
World.content:
Shaheen Shah Afridi has been one of the casualties of Pakistan cricket’s brutal game of captaincy musical chairs. But at a stage in his career when he has much to prove, the left-arm pace spearhead has the One-day International (ODI) captaincy firmly in his grasp, with the 2027 World Cup looming on the horizon.

Unlike in 2024, when he was removed as Pakistan’s T20 captain after just one series in charge, the country’s cricket board appears to have committed to giving Shaheen a longer run as leader. Appointed to the ODI role 12 months ago, he is expected to lead Pakistan through to next year’s World Cup in South Africa.

When Pakistan take on Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ODI tri-series on Sunday, Shaheen will have Babar Azam among his charges. Babar replaced him as T20 captain in 2024 before eventually making way for Salman Ali Agha.

Shaheen, meanwhile, took over the ODI captaincy from former skipper Mohammad Rizwan, who is currently under investigation by the country’s cybercrime agency.

Not long ago, Babar, Shaheen and Rizwan formed the core of Pakistan’s leadership group, with Babar shouldering much of the responsibility. He appeared to enjoy the backing of the other two, but the dynamics eventually changed amid a succession of captaincy reshuffles.

Despite that turbulent history, Shaheen wants his side to be seen as a united team, with a common objective: winning the 2027 World Cup.

“We are united as a team and our collective focus is towards winning the World Cup and how we can do it,” he told reporters at a pre-series press conference at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Saturday.

“The messaging from you [the media] should be good as well, to tell the people that this team is united, there is love in this team and this team tries to play good cricket.

“It is just a game. If you portray it to the people, kids in a way that is too serious, they will be worried about why we are not winning.”

Shaheen was particularly emphatic in his support for Babar, describing the former captain as the “backbone” of the side.

“There is no pressure on Babar, he is our main player,” said the 26-year-old. “He is the backbone of this team.

“He has performed well over the past few home series.”

Under Shaheen, Pakistan’s ODI side has spent the past year rebuilding, winning all their home series in the process. Those assignments were played on slower surfaces, with spin-friendly pitches used most recently during the series against Australia in May and June.

The conditions for the tri-series, however, are expected to offer a different challenge, with pitches being prepared to better resemble those in South Africa. The surfaces appeared greener during Pakistan’s recent T20I series against Sri Lanka, and Shaheen confirmed that there had been a deliberate effort to encourage lateral movement and bounce.

“Over the course of the last four one-day series, we have tried to build this team, since our focus is on [next year’s] World Cup and how we can prepare for it,” he said. “Henceforth we have also tried to prepare the wickets accordingly.”

Pakistan will also play a five-match ODI series in England before beginning their World Cup campaign against Afghanistan on Oct 8.

“We want our fast bowlers to get help [off the surface] so when we play in South Africa and in England, both our bowling and our batting has the potential to get the other team out and chase the runs [respectively],” Shaheen said.

The conditions will also influence Pakistan’s team combination, with Shaheen indicating that the side could field three or four fast bowlers. That would make opener-turned-all-rounder Saim Ayub’s contribution with the ball particularly important, despite his recent struggles in T20 and Test cricket.

“Saim Ayub may have struggled in T20 cricket, he struggled in the Test match as well,” Shaheen said. “But as far as one-day cricket is concerned, we really need him.

“Because if we go with three or four pacers, then the team needs his bowling. If we keep giving him opportunities, he will thrive for Pakistan.”

Brook, Mendis look ahead to Tri-Series

England and Sri Lanka captains, Harry Brook and Kusal Mendis are also looking forward to the challenge of the tri-series.

“I think it’s a great opportunity to play a tri series in Pakistan against two very strong sides. I think it will definitely hold us in good stead knowing that there is a final at the end of the series as well,” said Brook in the captains’ press conference.

“Pakistan is a great place to play cricket as well and we know how passionate the crowd can be.”

He added that the tri-series will allow the side to assess where they stand in ODIs, after a successful few months during which the team has bonded and gotten a real sense of what they want to achieve on the field.

“We wanna be a side where we can win in any conditions against any opposition,

“Pakistan are gonna present us with challenges we probably haven’t quite faced yet as an ODI side, and we’re really looking forward to the opportunity of playing Pakistan and Sri Lanka in subcontinental conditions,” he said.

Kusal Mendis also said the series will be important for all teams, adding that the Sri Lankan side had trained for a few days following the conclusion of the T20I series. The series had ended in a 2-1 win for Pakistan, but Sri Lanka had clinched the third fixture by a convincing eight wickets, allowing them to enter the ODI series on a high.

“[In the] last game, the bowling part was done really well, and myself and Kamindu batted really well,” he said, adding that finishing on a “positive” note allowed the side to enter this tri-series with confidence and the knowledge that they “know how to play.”

“We have very good, talented senior players, a couple of all-rounders, and we played really well in the England series also,” he said, referring to the side’s white-ball tour of England where the ODI series had ended in a 2-1 win for the hosts.

“I hope we can do well in this tournament.”

“I have no doubt in my spin attack,” he said while speaking of the conditions, adding that even in Sri Lanka the side is used to playing on wickets with a “little bit” of spin.

“When we go to other countries, we have to use the conditions and adapt to the conditions quickly.”

He added that extensive planning was done regarding the players and their responsibility, and that each player knows where their role and responsibility lies as per the plan.

Following their opening match against Sri Lanka, Pakistan will face England on Oct 20 and 25 before taking on Sri Lanka again on Oct 27. The tri-series final is scheduled for Oct 31.

World.title: Islamabad ATC rejects police request for physical remand of ex-GB CM Khalid Khurshid
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday rejected the police’s request for 30-day physical remand of PTI leader and former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Khalid Khurshid and sent him to jail on judicial remand in connection with a case registered over the November 26 protest.

Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain heard the case against Khurshid. During the hearing, Islamabad police produced the PTI leader before the court and sought his physical remand for 30 days.

However, the court turned down the request and directed that he be sent to judicial custody.

A case was registered against Khurshid, the president of the PTI’s GB chapter, at Aabpara Police Station in connection with the party’s November 26 protest in 2024.

The protest saw more than 10,000 PTI protesters surge into Islamabad, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown to skirmish with 20,000 security forces enlisted to turn them back.

A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone had ended in the PTI leadership’s hasty retreat, with the party announcing that it was calling off its planned protest sit-in “for the time being”. Subsequently, cases were registered against several PTI leaders under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act.

Khurshid was arrested along with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and several others at the speaker’s house in Peshawar, according to the PTI, shortly after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

Sources said Khurshid had been staying at the KP chief minister’s residence since 2023 to avoid arrest by GB police.

PTI workers discharged

In a separate development, the court also discharged PTI workers arrested in connection with two cases linked to the party’s recent long march after rejecting a request by the investigating officer for an adjournment to conduct their identification parade.

During proceedings concerning the PTI workers arrested in two cases registered at Shalimar and Secretariat police stations, the investigating officer requested an adjournment to conduct an identification parade.

However, the defence counsel opposed the request, arguing that the workers had already spent more than 40 days in custody and that the police had repeatedly sought adjournments without producing them before the court.

The lawyers maintained that the accused were innocent and had been deliberately implicated in the cases, alleging that the police arbitrarily arrested individuals and falsely portrayed them as PTI workers.

The defence counsel reiterated their earlier plea for the discharge of the accused and urged the court to implement its order passed at the previous hearing.

Accepting the defence’s arguments, the court ordered the discharge of all the PTI workers from the cases.

The workers had been placed in judicial custody for the purpose of an identification parade in connection with the cases registered at Shalimar and Secretariat police stations.

World.title: Egypt's President Sisi pledges to leave office when term ends in 2030
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as “completely settled”.

Sisi, 71, a former army general who became president in 2014, made the remarks at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy in the New Administrative Capital, one of his flagship megaprojects.

Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution “would not be touched”.

“The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive. This is completely settled and there will be no discussion about it,” he said.

The Egyptian constitution, approved in 2014 following the 2013 military ouster of late president Mohamed Morsi, originally limited presidents to two four-year terms.

Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term.

Under those amendments, Sisi was re-elected in 2023 for a six-year term that is due to expire in 2030.

Critics and opposition figures have speculated about the possibility of further constitutional changes that could allow him to remain in office beyond 2030.

Before running for president, Sisi denied having political ambitions, but he resigned from his position as defence minister in 2014 and entered the race he went on to win.

On Saturday, he said the run-up to 2030 would be used to groom a new generation of leaders, with the Military Academy training hundreds of prospective officials, ministers and presidential candidates in statecraft and leadership.

During his 12 years in power, Sisi has overseen an ambitious state-led development programme centred on megaprojects which critics say have relied heavily on borrowing and contributed to Egypt’s mounting debt burden and economic pressures.

Sisi’s presidency has also faced sustained criticism from international human rights organisations over restrictions on political opposition, civil society and freedom of expression, allegations the government rejects, saying its policies are necessary to preserve stability and security.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings. EV solar charging and distributed storage policies should be developed. Renewable energy skill development and employment programs should also be launched.

In the long term, within 3–10 years, Bangladesh should aim to reach more than 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030. Offshore and onshore wind should be developed. Floating solar, river-based solar, and agrivoltaics should be implemented. A National Energy Storage Strategy should be prepared. Smart grid and power sector digitalisation should be accelerated. Local assembly and manufacturing of solar panels, inverters, mounting structures, battery packs, BMS, and EV charging equipment should be encouraged. Regional power trade should be expanded. The Renewable Purchase Obligation should be introduced. Fossil fuel subsidies should be gradually redirected to a renewable energy transition fund.

Image Visual: Anwar Sohel

The benefits can be large. Energy import costs will fall. Pressure on foreign currency reserves will decline. Industrial production costs will reduce. Export competitiveness will improve. The subsidy burden will decrease. New investment will grow. Renewable energy can create 20–25 jobs per MW through rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, solar pumps, EV charging, battery storage, smart grids, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance.

The government may worry about revenue loss from tax and duty exemptions. But this should be seen as an investment. In the short term, there may be a limited impact on revenue. In the long term, Bangladesh can save far more by reducing fuel imports, lowering subsidies, saving foreign currency, strengthening industries, and attracting new investment.

Bangladesh’s energy crisis is a major challenge but also a historic opportunity. The crisis is not only a supply problem. It is a policy framework problem. Renewable energy, especially solar power, storage, and EV integration, can be among the most practical solutions for the country.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh should adopt renewable energy. The real question is how quickly, how systematically, and how boldly the country can complete this transition.



Mohammad Ataur Rahman Sarker is a renewable energy entrepreneur and the secretary of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association.

Md. Tanvir Siraj is a renewable energy researcher.

World.title: The forgotten art of Bengali advertising
World.content:
I have never seen someone at a rustic village market, anklets jingling, shouting slogans for "Khol Company’s Ringworm Ointment."
